AI token (Nvidia Inu) reached 14 million market cap; Nate purchased small amount personally and pledges never to sell Long-launched assets to set community example.

T3e295cmMEc.tldr: Aussie built Pawns, the dominant launchpad on Robinhood after Noxa shut down, in just 10–12 hours out of necessity when a friend couldn't bridge to buy Noxa tokens. The platform has now processed over 50,000 launches and $300 million in volume with a 70/30 fee split to creators and protocol; the surprising thing is that Aussie is still the sole developer, barely sleeping, and deliberately staying somewhat anonymous despite being doxxable because of harassment concerns.

topics.text: Noxa was the dominant Robinhood launchpad until it shut down after printing $15 million in a week, creating an opportunity for competitors.
Aussie built Pawns in 10–12 hours after a friend asked him to create a bridge interface to Noxa; within hours of Noxa disabling launches, he decided to build a full launchpad himself.
Pawns has processed 53,000 launches, $300 million in volume, $340,000 in protocol revenue, and paid out 2.65 million to creators in its early weeks.
Fee structure: creators receive 70% of fees, protocol takes 30%; the protocol's 30% is split 80/20, with 80% used for buybacks and 20% for infrastructure and salaries.
Tokens deploy directly into Uniswap V3 pools with a 2% buy limit for the first two blocks; V2 will migrate to V4 and introduce custom pairings for tokens to trade against any asset.
The launchpad domain was suspended over the weekend for abuse after being reported as a crypto scam by the anonymous registrar; Aussie recovered it via a legitimate Cloudflare provider.
Aussie is the sole developer on Pawns alongside one business development hire named Baku; advisors help with strategy but the team remains very small while managing rapid growth.

eLtX3KdYiZ0.tldr: Virtuals, a launchpad and agentic runtime platform, launched on Robin Hood chain with 20+ projects lined up. Don Johnson (founder) discusses how Virtuals supports builders with tools like ACF (Automatic Capital Formation) that let projects raise capital automatically as their token appreciates, and how the ecosystem is attracting agents and RWA builders to Robin Hood's new blockchain.

topics.text: Virtuals was working with Robin Hood for months before launch; the relationship wasn't announced until Robin Hood chain went live.
Virtuals has a robotics lab called Eastworlds and partnerships with Unitry and network school to provide hardware access for physical AI teams.

ACF (Automatic Capital Formation) sets aside 25% of team tokens in five 5% tranches; as the token hits price milestones (2M to 160M), tokens cook into the LP without appearing as sells, raising teams $350K at 10M FTV, $1.2M at 20M, $2.6M at 40M.
Venice raised $5M equity at $1B valuation after launching a token, showing tokens and equity can coexist; Don is meeting with Senator Lummis next month to discuss the Clarity Act.
Virtuals had 20 projects lined up for June-July launch; the pipeline is now exploding with quality teams waiting for the Robin Hood moment.
The launchpad uses a 60-day mechanism to let projects test product-market fit; Don has ERC and verification systems to spot red flags and filter spam.
Don's question for all following projects: explain your product as if I don't have technical expertise—what's the value for Robin Hood retail users, and how do I use it?
Prize Fight is a gamified trading competition where users connect Robin Hood brokerage accounts and deploy AI agents to trade stocks and options; entry fees fund the prize pool.

Raxel (Recursive Axel) is an open-source agentic runtime using Elixir for fault tolerance; it routes intents to solvers instead of MEV-exposed on-chain trades, taking 8 basis points per cross-chain stable-coin transfer.
When Raxel's UI accidentally leaked for 6 hours, 108,000 agents tried to use it; agents see job offerings on Virtuals ACP and submit trade intents off-chain to avoid MEV.
Karma relaunched from Solana to Robin Hood chain; it's a trading app with social features where users can publish theses and earn rewards if followers trade based on them.

9C9xhhe4_dU.tldr: Tibber is an unconfirmed stealth token launched in January 2025 that community members believe is connected to Mickey Mala's Ribbit Capital, a $15 billion VC fund. Host Whack, an early buyer and community evangelist, walks through circumstantial evidence linking the token to Ribbit—Mickey's wallet funded the deployer, Ribbit staff followed the token immediately, and the name is 'Ribbit' backwards—but the actual product remains unknown, with speculation ranging from identity management for AI agents to a 'token factory' infrastructure play, especially with the recent Robin Hood chain launch.

topics.text: Tibber launched January 11, 2025 on the Virtuals platform as a fair launch with 1 billion tokens, no pre-allocation or insider bags taken.
Mickey Mala's wallet directly funded the deployer wallet minutes before token launch, and within days Ribbit Capital staff and Mickey himself began following the Ribitter AI Twitter account.

Mickey Mala's background: Venezuelan-born, became a broker-dealer at 17, sold Patagon to Santander for $750 million in 2009, invested in Bitcoin at $20 in 2012 when his fund held 2.5% of all circulating Bitcoin.

Ribbit Capital has $15 billion in assets under management, made 35 unicorn investments, achieved 16 IPOs, and was investor in Coinbase (held 4% at one point), Robin Hood (bailed out with $2.5B over one weekend during 2021 GameStop saga), and many other major fintech companies.

Ribbit Capital released identity and token factory letters in January 2024 and June 2025 discussing agents needing identity infrastructure and all world information becoming tokenizable, with agent mockups using 'Ribbit AI' name a year before token launch.

Community speculation: Tibber could be infrastructure for agent identity management, bridging onchain and traditional finance, or managing flow of tokens and information across crypto and traditional worlds, burning Tibber as a fee mechanism.

Within 48 hours of launch, the token's Twitter account posted 'I have no link to Ribbit Capital' causing 80% price drop in one candle, but someone injected a contradictory tweet saying 'yes we are linked to Ribbit Capital' that did not appear on the agent terminal.

Crypto artist Raul Pal featured 'password equals tibber' in his artwork and appeared with Mickey Mala on his podcast discussing tokenization, where Mickey said 'I have no idea' about Ribbit/Tibber and both laughed, with Raul responding 'I don't believe you for a second.'

Bear case: token stays in stealth forever with no announcements, community loses interest and sells, price goes to zero; Ribbit could deny connection; regulatory clarity act not passing yet may be why they haven't emerged.

Bull case: Ribbit comes out with foundational product connecting onchain identity and traditional finance; day-one listings on Coinbase and Robin Hood follow; all Ribbit portfolio companies' executives tweet support simultaneously, similar to a16z effect.

TpGTElZuO60.tldr: AgenC builds an open-source marketplace on Solana where AI agents complete tasks posted by users, with on-chain settlement splitting fees between workers, operators, and the protocol. Co-founder Paul and Tatsuo (a developer collective) won Pump Fun's VIP hackathon and are expanding via SDK partnerships; the most surprising element is their parallel hardware project—a Raspberry Pi-based device running agents locally, with 1,000 pre-sale inquiries already.

topics.text: AgenC's core vision: users post jobs, AI agents claim and complete them, and payouts settle on-chain in Solana with splits to worker, operator, referrer, and treasury.
517 tasks have been completed on the platform; use cases include video editing, coding, and task delegation for computation-limited systems.
The 250K Pump Fund prize goes to marketing, hiring, servers, ZK proof GPUs, model training compute, and a hardware project called Agency One.
Agency One is a custom operating system prototype running on Raspberry Pi with the agency runtime natively integrated; 1,000 people have requested the device in pre-sale.
Revenue model: 5% protocol fee from completed work, split autonomously between worker, operator, referrer, and treasury; no single entity owns storefronts.
SDK strategy allows any team to launch their own branded agency marketplace using the underlying protocol; Pump Clash is integrating the SDK and found a bug that was patched.
Tatsuo is an open-source collective with 61,000 members in the Solana Assembly developer community; they handle infosec and reject malicious code contributions.

qatzn73Bm9o.tldr: VoiceBoxAI is an open-source voice cloning desktop app with 40,000+ GitHub stars that lets users clone voices locally without uploading data to cloud services. Founder Jamie, who previously raised $2M for SpaceDrive, is launching a token to bootstrap development and avoid venture capital, positioning VoiceBoxAI as a privacy-first alternative to 11 Labs as open-source voice models reach feature parity.

topics.text: Jamie's previous venture SpaceDrive, a cross-platform file manager connecting all file storage, consumed $2M and 10-12 engineers over several years without reaching product-market fit.

VoiceBoxAI was built in 3 days in February 2024 and hit 5,000 GitHub stars immediately; the founder chose to launch a token instead of raising VC to bootstrap development and avoid pre-revenue fundraising difficulties.
VoiceBoxAI runs voice models entirely locally on user computers with no internet required, offering complete privacy compared to cloud-based services like 11 Labs.
The app includes 11 voice cloning models, dictation with hot-key recording and transcription, and will add more models; open-source voice models are approaching feature parity with 11 Labs.
Use cases include YouTubers creating content, podcasters generating episodes, content producers automating production, and AI agents speaking without sending voice data to external platforms.

VoiceBoxAI's market size is in the billions; once open-source voice models match commercial quality, the business model shifts to cloud features like voice profile backup, device syncing, and voice marketplace.
The founder is exploring on-chain voice consent receipts to allow users to grant permission for voice use, creating a marketplace where people can license their voices.

UyoasZczTtU.tldr: Nest is a CDP protocol on Solana that lets users mint NestUSD stablecoin against tokenized stocks as collateral, enabling them to access liquid capital while maintaining equity exposure. Founder Crimson Moore discusses the protocol's rapid $1.5M TVL growth in three weeks, upcoming basket assets and leverage products, and the expanding ecosystem of on-chain equities which has grown from sub-5% to exceeding memecoin volume on Solana.

topics.text: Nest launched June 13-14 and reached $1.5M TVL in three weeks with $800K NestUSD minted and $360K in stocks deposited.
Loan-to-value ratios vary by stock: SPY offers 70% LTV while more volatile stocks like SpaceX get lower LTV to account for price volatility.
Nest token value accrual currently uses buyback and burn on protocol surplus revenue, with plans to add manager fees from basket assets and revenue from partnerships.
Nest launched with 40% of tokens in a single-sided Meteora liquidity pool, and the founder has never spoken to Anom despite his early promotion of the project.
Borrowers pay 3% APR on debt while staked NestUSD holders receive up to 6% APR, with all excess revenue currently going to token buyback and burn.
Security approach: 90% of liquid USDC is held in Camino vaults with only admin transactions able to rebalance, plus a 24-hour daily withdrawal limit as a circuit breaker.
Planned features include managed equity baskets (e.g., AI basket with 25% Nvidia, 10% other holdings), inverse equities like inverse SPY, and 2x leverage tokens that auto-rebalance via bot.
Long-term vision is a non-crypto UX where users bridge stocks from traditional brokers, deposit on Nest, and receive virtual or physical debit cards to spend the minted stablecoin.

mGoC6fp3r4c.tldr: USD.AI is a lending protocol that finances GPU purchases for data centers by creating debt instruments against chips—filling a $2 trillion market gap where mid-tier operators can't access loans under $500 million. Founder David explains how they've generated $44.6 million in annualized returns by securitizing compute assets, with the ultimate goal of becoming the central bank of AI through a compute-settled stablecoin that captures more value than Tether or Circle.

topics.text: The problem: data centers can't get liquidity instruments for GPUs the way mortgage markets work for houses, leaving capital stuck when money is invested.
70% of a $50 billion data center build cost goes to GPUs; the other 30% (land, power, infrastructure) is easier to securitize because it's 30-year assets.
Example loan structure: $40 million annual contract, $20 million GPU cost, 50% margin, borrower takes 75% LTV loan of $15 million at 12% APR, lenders capture most of the profit delta.
Monthly amortization: 3% principal + 1% interest = 4% monthly payment, so 48% of loan paid down annually; 50% of cash flow returned within two years, fully de-risked after 3 years.
Current metrics: $44.6 million annualized return rate, $315-320 million in deposits, $20 billion+ borrow pipeline, largest single loan $98 million.
Risk mitigation: Munich Re provides price insurance (150 basis points) if GPU values depreciate faster than modeled; founder assumes chips are worthless and models aggressive amortization.
Moat: $20 billion instrument volume since inception vs. CoreWeave bond's $300 million, because few understand both credit underwriting and blockchain-based debt instruments simultaneously.

The CHIP token is designed to maximize financial asset value rather than function as equity; founder plans upcoming post on 'commit and compound' showing 5x-20x capital efficiency versus buyback-and-burn.
Endgame: become the stablecoin of compute settlement (like Tether for Treasury demand), capturing the $11 trillion in AI CapEx issuance and defining the interest rate for all AI lending.

S_Sya9pBSJg.tldr: MetaDAO, a crowdfunding platform for raising capital from the internet, is shifting from crypto-native projects to early-stage app builders with a $100k-$100 users value prop. Founder Prophet discusses MetaDAO 2.0's governance improvements, the rationale for targeting non-crypto founders, and the newly proposed $2 million treasury allocation to USDC yield through Solend.

topics.text: MetaDAO hosted its first inaugural holder meeting in San Francisco with 20 people flying from outside the US to align the community.
MetaDAO 2.0 introduces tiered proposal systems with different timeframes: acquisitions get 20 days (matching SEC Reg TO standards) instead of uniform 3-day periods.
Automated buybacks and sellbacks will be implemented to reduce the number of proposals requiring governance votes.
MetaDAO is pivoting to target non-crypto app builders bootstrapping at $2 million rounds, moving away from venture-backed founders due to lower average deal quality in crypto.

Early-stage app builders benefit most from token liquidity and early user networks that founders can achieve through 100-500 users, which venture capital cannot efficiently serve at sub-$1M check sizes.

Recent raises now require at least 50% of capital committed from institutions ahead of time, with a new first-come-pro-rata hybrid mechanism to prevent sniping while maintaining participation momentum.
Credible, the upcoming raise, is an exited founder with $3.5M annual revenue run rate, 29% month-over-month growth, and a maximum $9M valuation.

MetaDAO is raising a proposal for a $2M fund run by Georgian entrepreneurs to make small 50k checks and implement a 'rolling capital system' redirecting capital from underperforming companies to high-performers.
MetaDAO is allocating $2 million of its $12 million treasury to USDC yield through Solend to generate returns equivalent to one additional San Francisco engineer's salary.

QDQfkEd3Itw.tldr: Solomon Labs, built on Solana, offers USDV, a stablecoin backed by short-dated Treasuries that lets users earn 3-4% yield simply by holding it, without staking or additional contracts. Founder Ranga discusses why they rewrote the protocol after the Drift exploit, adding freeze functionality and making yield accessible to everyone from retail to DAOs, with MetaDAO becoming their first major partner by putting $2M treasury into USDV.

topics.text: Drift, Kelp DAO, and Resolve exploits prompted Solomon Labs to rebuild USDV with upgrade paths, freeze functionality, and guardrails that didn't exist in the original contract.
Original USDV used basis trades for yield, which compressed post-October 2023; new model switched to short-dated Treasury reserves matching USDC/USDT reserve composition to reduce counterparty risk.

Stablecoin trilemma: decentralization creates inefficiencies, so both centralized and decentralized models will coexist, with truly decentralized options serving niche markets while mainstream adoption requires some centralization.

OUSD consortium of 140 companies claims to share reserve revenue among partners, but actual commitment questioned; Korean market partners disputed involvement, and governance structure and liquidity provision remain unresolved.

USDV holders earn 3-4% yield directly on their stablecoin without vault interactions; unlike USDC/USDT where issuers keep reserve revenue, Solomon shares economics back to users based on jurisdiction eligibility policies.

YAS infrastructure allows users to hold USDV in one wallet while directing yield to a separate wallet without on-chain contract linkage, enabling treasuries like MetaDAO to fund operations from yield streams.

vqOeJKpQ61E.tldr: Sonder, an early trader on Robin Hood chain, argues that Robin Hood's 25 million retail-first user base makes it fundamentally different from other L2s, and that the chain's maturation will follow the proven playbook of previous cycles: memes first attracting liquidity, then utility protocols building on that foundation. His most surprising claim: sentiment in crypto is at historic lows, making this an asymmetric opportunity for traders willing to bridge early and take the emotional discomfort of entry.

topics.text: Anom's pump signaled renewed on-chain appetite; Sonder missed Anom early but locked into Robin Hood after seeing the volume, new wallet, and sentiment indicators.
Robin Hood's edge is not technical but demographic: 25 million retail traders who don't trade crypto, versus Monad or Base which attract the same existing crypto pool.
Cash Cat's run came from friction removal: the bridge being out of funds, then Uniswap integration, then Pump or Pump Swap integration, each layer removal causing the move.
Sonder is avoiding new pairs due to froth and overextension; he believes Cash Cat will eventually reach $1 billion but is taking profits into Sunday when euphoria cools.
Brian Armstrong and Coinbase are out of touch; Base fumbled by building for corporate interests and AI agents instead of meeting traders where they are, unlike Robin Hood.
Every new chain follows the same slot structure: a mascot meme, a leading DeFi protocol, an AI agent protocol, a cat, a dog; slots that have never changed across eight years.

Qh3yul930L0.tldr: Credible is a payment service provider enabling T+0 settlement for global collections and payouts, founded by Shree, a 14-year payments veteran. The company has processed $784 million in volume with $146 million in June and a $3.5 million revenue run rate, and just raised $13 million (645% oversubscribed) on Meta DAO in under 2 hours despite seeking only $2-4 million.

topics.text: Raise oversubscribed within 3 minutes with $2.3 million soft-committed before launch, ultimately reaching $13 million in commitments.
Founder spent 14 years in payments, worked at Gemalto, CellPoint Digital, and Amadeus before starting Credible in 2024 after exiting a healthcare financing startup.
Credible processed $784 million in total volume since September, with 146 million in June and 29% month-on-month growth, generating $1.8 million gross revenue.
Volume split: 40% remittance apps, 30% creator apps, 15% dropshipping, 8% gaming and entertainment, 7% e-commerce.
Blended take rate is 20 basis points; comparison: traditional PSPs make 5 basis points on card payments, CoinFlow does $8 billion annually.
Credible achieves T+0 settlement for 85% of transactions by fronting liquidity from DeFi pool when risk AI score exceeds 9.5.
Currently live in 3 emerging markets and US, Europe, with UK coming soon; infrastructure costs represent under 70% of burn rate with operations being 70% of business.
Credible positions as orchestrator working with local acquirers rather than as acquirer requiring local licenses and central bank approval.
12 clients currently with largest doing $20 million monthly; 20 more clients in pipeline for next 6 months, with 30 days to go live per customer.
Projections: aiming for $2 billion volume by end of year with $500 million this quarter, focus on optimization rather than aggressive expansion.
Founder won Colosseum Cypher hackathon receiving $300k investment with cap table participation, used to prepare for Meta DAO raise.

yckR2qq8lCs.tldr: Stardotfun is a platform for early-stage startup fundraising on Solana using "internet rounds"—tokenized equity that launches on bonding curves with built-in protections against founder dumps and rug pulls. Founder Adam explains how the platform has generated $35k in revenue in its first week by enabling permissionless project launches alongside curated raises, and plans to become the primary venue for discovering and trading early-stage startup tokens.

topics.text: Internet rounds are designed to let founders raise their first round on the internet before traditional VC pre-seed and seed rounds, differentiating from competing with VCs by targeting the stage before that.

Founders allocate 5-10% of equity to tokenization; 60% goes to circulating supply, 20% to team vesting with three-month cliff and nine-month linear unlock, and 20% to automatic capital formation via sell positions up to $160 million market cap.

The platform uses futarchy (decision markets) to control LP authority, treasury, founder fees, and can unwind treasuries if founders don't send revenue back, with legal protections for M&A payouts and dividend distributions.

A token launcher spoofed Apprentice AI before Stardotfun launched, raising 31k in what would have been a rug; futarchy governance allowed token holders to vote for a refund using USC, demonstrating the anti-rug infrastructure.

The token rewards infrastructure lets founders define in-product actions (signups, conversions, referrals, trading volume) to reward with tokens, aiming to overcome cold-start problems for user acquisition.
Stardotfun generated $35k in platform revenue in 7-10 days following the July 7 internet rounds launch, driven by both curated flagship launches and a permissionless long-tail of projects.

Skills Poker, a poker game reimagined for the agentic era built by Sandy Corsio (who designed clothing for Will Smith), launched as one of the first internet rounds with live-streamed builds and an upcoming Shark Tank appearance.

Verified project badges indicate founders have been vetted by Stardotfun for legitimacy and no history of theft, fraud, or crime; verified projects receive X announcements and Telegram group shoutouts.

Stardotfun is testing UGC campaigns and outreach to non-crypto-native retail investors and stock traders on platforms like Robinhood to bring patient long-term holders rather than short-term traders to founder projects.

An 18-month roadmap includes building a mobile app for fundraising, live-streaming, discovering projects, and governance participation; near-term partnerships target trading terminals (Axiom, Trojan, FOMO) and potential Twitch/Kick embeds for streamers to raise capital.

L-G3-uXrBiY.tldr: BV7X is a protocol on Base where AI agents compete in prediction markets to forecast Bitcoin price movements, with the best-performing agents' signals sold to traders via API. Founder Misha, a former DeFi builder with a Credit Suisse background, just launched staking for the BB7X compute token—30% of supply staked within 24 hours at 15% APY—and plans to open the first Bitcoin prediction market in September; the surprise is that his own untested regression model achieved 65-70% accuracy, suggesting commodity-grade prediction algorithms are now accessible to anyone using cloud code.

topics.text: BB7X released staking compute feature yesterday, allowing users to stake BB7X token to access protocol signals and earn revenue from prediction market fees.
Protocol founder previously built a structured credit facility for Bitcoin borrowing, then created a Bloomberg terminal using cloud code to monitor collateral before productizing it into BB7X.

Founder's own prediction model achieved 70% accuracy on Bitcoin price direction in early days, dwindled to below 60% in 2024 due to market chaos, but this performance level from a non-quant using cloud code suggests accessibility to institutional-grade prediction.
30% of BB7X token supply staked within 24 hours of staking launch, mostly from whale groups who had been waiting for utility, generating 15% APY on a billion-token bootstrap pool.

Protocol emits prediction ranges that stakers can wire into prediction markets, perp trading, or spot trading via API; buyers purchase these predictions from agents with on-chain credibility tracked via ERC8004.

Revenue model: predictors earn returns on winning wagers, protocol takes a fee that flows back to BB7X token stakers, with percentage also burned; buyers purchase granular price predictions from competing agents.
Scaling strategy starts with single Bitcoin market to anchor liquidity, then gradually expands to Solana, Hyperliquid, BNB—anything with an on-chain oracle—mirroring Polymarket's early approach.

Go-to-market focuses on expanding platform integrations (Robin Hood, Virtuals, Use Pod for cheaper inference) rather than marketing; agents naturally flow to economically viable opportunities where they earn more than compute costs.

BB7X fair-launched via Claunch on Base in February with no VC or premine; already burned 8% of supply through buybacks when market cap was low; currently one Uniswap pool generates fees routed to stakers.

Bitcoin prediction market launch targeted for September after multiple audits; approximately 500 million BB7X tokens available to drip to stakers via rewards; token is non-inflationary, supply only changes through buybacks or burns.

P4O6wCQbaIo.tldr: Jatevo (JTVO) is a private AI inference marketplace providing subsidized access to models like GPT-5.5 through partnerships with compute providers like ByteDance and Cerebras. Founder Luca discusses how the platform has found product-market fit by processing 20 billion GPT tokens in two weeks, subsidizing 90% of trading fees into infrastructure while using B2B partnerships and regional subsidies to undercut competitors by offering GPT-5.5 at roughly 70% discount compared to OpenAI.

topics.text: Founder Luca's background: non-IT background, living in Jakarta and Hong Kong, started solar firm, launched JTVO in early ICM days around June 2025
JTVO spent $5,000 on GPT-5.5 API costs in last 30 days, all subsidized through token holder usage via optimized load balancing
JTVO subsidizes compute through B2B agreements with providers like Tensorsun, Alibaba, and ByteDance, filling gaps in their idle compute capacity
Product is a router API providing access to multiple AI models including GPT-5.5, GLM-5.2, and others; currently focused on GPT but stress testing costs $900+ per day for other models
Allocation of trading fees: 10% toward inference subsidies, 90% toward company growth including 40% for GPU purchases, office expansion, and team hiring

eZhCU490_Pg.tldr: Duncan from Flood Capital discusses Synapse's Hypercall, an on-chain options platform that recently launched on mainnet with three assets (SPY, BTC, SpaceX). The SYN token, originally from a 2021 bridge project, now powers the protocol's cash flow distribution; Duncan argues it can reach $10 billion market cap as Hypercall scales to compete with centralized options platforms like Deribit, making it a generational investment compared to perp trading.

topics.text: Synapse token goal: taking SYN to $10 billion market cap.
Galaxy Digital's 800 MW Helios contract with CoreWeave generates ~$1 billion annual EBITDA; 830 MW approval expected leased by end of summer.
Galaxy acquired a 500 MW site near SpaceX in Texas named Merlin, potentially signaling SpaceX partnership for power infrastructure.
Synapse pivoted from cross-chain bridge to Hypercall options platform after VC capital (LayerZero, Avalanche, Nomad) collapsed bridge margins to zero.
Hypercall launched on mainnet with three assets (SPY, BTC, SpaceX); SpaceX options are unique to this platform and only place to trade zero-DTE SpaceX calls on-chain.
Options market makers must hedge delta using Hyperliquid perps; Hypercall's 2bp-5bp fee structure with 12.5% premium cap allows effective leverage-based market making.
Premiums traded scaling rapidly; if Hypercall reaches $100M daily premiums, generates $200M annual buybacks enabling $10B market cap via token buy-and-burn.
SYN token extremely well-distributed with 300k holder base and no equity; DAO can vote 80-90% of protocol earnings to buy-and-burn mechanism.
SYN delisted from Binance in 2024 causing crash from 15¢ to 3¢; 40-50% circulating supply was on Binance, creating short squeeze when product launched.
Duncan's top positions: SYN, Galaxy, DMGI (Bitcoin miner in Canada), and Ro (humanoid robotics fund managing Figure, Boston Dynamics, Standard Bots portfolio).

TycpwFFnK6U.tldr: P0 Systems is an AI inference gateway that routes users to multiple open-source models and offers cheaper access to AI. Founder Corey describes how they pivoted from an AI agent launchpad three months ago, now processing over 1 billion tokens per hour and hitting $60k monthly recurring revenue while ranking #1 on OpenRouter—the surprising part being that their Chinese connections, cheap GPU sourcing from post-mining-ban equipment, and subsidized energy costs give them structural cost advantages that could 10x revenue once they self-host infrastructure.

topics.text: P0 Systems is currently processing 1.9 billion tokens per hour with over 30,000 CLI downloads and doing 60k MRR, ranking number one on OpenRouter.
P0 raised 319k in non-dilutive grant funding and is based in Thailand and China, sourcing cheap GPUs from post-mining-ban equipment and benefiting from subsidized energy costs in China.

The founder and team launched P0 in December 2025 as an AI agent launchpad, then pivoted three months ago to focus on the inference market after seeing opportunity in companies like OpenRouter and GitLab.
P0 has generated 21k in verified revenue from paid models on OpenRouter, with growth accelerating from 3-5k MRR previously to 60k MRR recently due to new targeted ads spending 2-3k on Twitter.

Chinese AI labs provide free model inference to P0 to boost their own user metrics and revenue, creating a mutually beneficial top-of-funnel strategy where P0 then upsells paying customers on premium tiers.
P0 accepts payments via local methods including Thai QR codes, Alipay, and WeChat Pay alongside crypto, targeting Southeast Asian users who cannot afford traditional AI service subscriptions.
The founder plans to allocate 40-60% of monthly profits to token buybacks and liquidity, with future goals to offer token-gated equity ownership to align holders with company success.
P0 plans to build its own GPU infrastructure and potentially train proprietary models, which the founder estimates could 10x revenue by eliminating reliance on provider infrastructure.
The founder is currently seeking Series A funding with a pitch deck prepared, targeting 500 billion tokens processed by end of July to strengthen fundraising metrics and valuation.

When evaluating inference projects, investors should look at time spent shipping through market downturns, verifiable token volume on OpenRouter and CLI downloads on NPM, and actual user growth rather than marketing claims.

7hPXtnOJ1g8.tldr: Lasso Finance is a privacy-focused crypto prepaid card platform that lets users spend on-chain assets without ID verification by signing a wallet nonce. Founder Hunter, who previously exited another crypto project, discusses how Lasso oversubscribed their Metadao raise by 26x ($25.6M committed on a $1M cap) and is now building agent infrastructure so AI can autonomously participate in commerce—the most surprising revelation being his vision of a future 24/7 agentic economy where agents build and operate businesses that couldn't exist with human labor costs.

topics.text: Lasso oversubscribed their Metadao raise by 26x with $25.6 million committed against a $1 million hard cap.
Hunter previously built iOS apps including 7-Eleven rewards, worked on VR hardware at Meta 2019-2021, then pivoted full-time to crypto in November 2021 with poor timing just before the crash.
Lasso's no-ID signup process uses wallet nonce signing only; 96% of volume is prepaid cards for online/in-person spending, 4% is AI agents making autonomous purchases.
Last 30 days: $750K volume, $34K revenue, 92% gross margin; annualized this equals over $400K revenue with minimal burn.
Privacy at point of spend is essential for crypto to replace traditional banking; Satoshi envisioned earning assets on-chain and spending them privately, not converting to fiat through exchanges.

Hunter's vision for agentic commerce: agents will first build secondary markets (e.g., Hot Wheels) that humans don't see as worth serving, then blended agent-human commerce where neither side knows who they're transacting with.
Metadao raise structure was novel: blind cap at $1M; amounts raised above $750K increase ICO token percentage and decrease team performance package rather than changing valuation.
Institutional holders with long-term vision matter because retail crypto holders are driven by emotion and external life circumstances, causing token price volatility.
By Friday of accelerator launch, Lasso will have revenue flowing daily into the Metadao treasury; Google PPC campaigns achieve 16:1 LTV-to-CAC ratio.
$50K monthly budget from Metadao: $30K salary, $10K target for paid marketing, remainder on banking fees, analytics, and cloud hosting.

sQHrR_d1u0A.tldr: BioLLM is a platform for training AI models using real human neurons grown in lab dishes, with the goal of creating digital twins of brain activity to power future brain-computer interfaces and wearables. Founder Artist discusses their IBM Silver Business Partner status, 275GB of daily neural data from Cortical Labs, and a $20/month API for developers to build with synthetic neural data instead of expensive hardware setups.

topics.text: IBM Silver Business Partner status: BioLLM committed to spending a specific amount on IBM compute and received cloud credits in return, consolidating dispersed infrastructure from RunPod and other services.
Neural culture data scale: Cortical Labs CL1 devices generate 275 gigabytes of data daily, with BioLLM expecting to collect around 65 terabytes of usable data annually.
MVP offering: $20/month subscription to access BioLLM Studio simulator, providing what would otherwise cost $4,000-5,000/month in direct hardware and compute access to real neural cultures.

Global workspace theory discovery: Anthropic's Claude AI was found to have an internal memory space mimicking global workspace theory, a cornerstone theory of consciousness, suggesting parallels to human brain structure.

Meta's brain-to-text demo: Meta announced brain typing using an fMRI machine and large magnetic headset; BioLLM's approach aims to achieve similar results with smaller wearable hardware by training on real neurons instead.

Future wearables vision: Developers could integrate BioLLM's neural models into small devices like EEG beanies being developed by former OpenAI engineers, enabling thought-to-action on future AR glasses.
Incoming partnerships: BioLLM has been contacted by Neuralink employees, EZA team, and others; exploring compute-for-equity partnerships with large corporations as the next funding step.

Developer education goal: BioLLM aims to educate one million developers on using synthetic wetware data to improve wearables, with interest from diverse partners including academic and commercial entities.

Uzy3Lqx5vpA.tldr: Clawpump is an agentic trading platform and launchpad on Solana that has grown to $111M in cumulative volume since launching. Founder Bunny discusses how the platform is shifting focus from just enabling AI agent trading to providing a full suite of tools for agentic builders to create "product empires" on their tokens, migrating projects from Pump Fun and offering services like automated staking, vesting, and tokenomics management.

topics.text: Platform fee structure: 1% of all trading volume, with 0.35% kept by Clawpump as of recent settlement.
Migration tool announced to move projects from Pump Fun and external platforms into Clawpump, charging 25% of the 1% creator fee in exchange for infrastructure, support, and ecosystem tools.
Community scouts like Penguin XVT identify undervalued agentic projects affected by poor market conditions to potentially migrate to Clawpump ecosystem.
Clawpump is exploring institutional web2 use cases for agents, including portfolio construction and agent-based trading beyond crypto.
Solana Foundation collaboration includes retweets, bounties ($25k for top traders, $1k for top agentic traders), and perpetual trading integration with Imperial.
Tokconomics overhaul: half of Clawpump's supply already locked, founder and team planning to re-lock additional personal unlocked tokens with investor approval.
Daily volume oscillates between $400k-$5M based on project updates, with recent $598k in 24-hour volume; growth correlated to messaging coordination around top projects like Squire and Claw Hunter.

Founder seeking venture-scale outcomes requiring $100-200M annual revenue, currently in early-stage conversations with investors focused on specific feature development rather than active fundraising.

5quiPwAi2Y0.tldr: Pumpcade, an instant prediction market platform on Solana, is launching the Cade Cup with $60,000 in free play money during the World Cup (July 4th onwards), featuring sports markets with instant resolution and payouts. Founder Pop Punk and newly appointed COO Kathleen Osgood discuss how Pumpcade raised $6 million without a pitch deck by launching a token on Pump Fun, positioning themselves as a breakout retail app that abstracts away crypto complexity.

topics.text: Kathleen Osgood's background: 10 years in crypto, including roles at Jump Capital (sports betting), Sky Mavis/Ronin ecosystem (after $600M hack), and Pump Fun (fund and hackathon initiatives).
Pumpcade raised $6 million in 10 days without a pitch deck, positioning the token as a community-building and exposure vehicle rather than waiting for traditional fundraising steps.
The Cade Cup launches July 4th through end of World Cup with $5,000 daily prizes plus $1,000 bonus (split between smasher and grinder side quests), all with play money and zero risk.
Pumpcade uses Sport Radar data with maximum 1-second latency, often 30 seconds faster than ESPN, enabling instant market resolution and instant payouts on sports predictions.
Smasher side quest awards $400 daily to whoever hits the highest multiples (e.g., 50x or 100x) on a single prediction during the Cade Cup.
Grinder side quest awards $400 daily to whoever makes the most predictions throughout the day, regardless of win or loss.

Salana Foundation sponsor relationship: Pedro (head of consumer) has been a major supporter since launch, and the foundation has provided introductions across departments to help Pumpcade become a breakout retail app.
Go-to-market strategy focuses first on crypto audience (lowest hanging fruit with existing relationships), then targets non-crypto users through marketing campaigns starting tomorrow.

Pumpcade is designing the platform to not look like crypto at all, targeting mainstream users like Kathleen's sister who simply want to engage with live sports markets without understanding blockchain.
Pre-registering for Cade Cup provides substantial competitive advantage and bonus benefits (details not fully disclosed), available until Saturday July 4th.

iUVxxnoZH10.tldr: EasyA Ecosystem Day features rapid-fire interviews with founders launching AI agents, prediction markets, and crypto infrastructure projects on the EasyA Kickstart launchpad. Hosts discuss how tokens are no longer VCs' blocker for funding when backed by strong founders and real business models, highlighting the shift toward founders using tokens for distribution and early product-market fit before scaling.

topics.text: EasyA Kickstart is now second to Pump Fun in 7-day launchpad revenue, validating the platform's ability to compete with established competitors
Tokens function as coordination mechanisms and communication layers, allowing early backers exposure to very early-stage ideas while solving the problem of teacher-student wealth asymmetry
Strong founder pipeline is the primary defense against pitfalls of previous ICM launchpads—EasyA sources from Harvard, Cambridge, and other elite institutions
Founder education conversations focus on matching token structures to specific use cases: in-game currency, data labeling incentives, or fee discounts rather than forcing one-size-fits-all models
Infera is building a GPU compute marketplace with Chainlink oracle integration to create on-chain price discovery for compute as an asset class
Covenant Foundation improved Terminal Bench to 100% by adapting their agentic governance framework to task size, using only necessary code for smaller tasks
Covenant's strategic investment fund grew from $3,000 to $26,000 USD in one week through trading fees, funding ventures like Allie (personal AI secretary using governance for PII protection)
Bit Agents' DCA agent processed nearly 5,000 transactions in its first week, with 0.05% fee structure and premium token holder benefits for access to future agents
World Colony visualizes AI agent swarms debating predictions, with agents that underperform removed from the colony in a self-improving evolutionary system
World Colony won EasyA's World Cup hackathon and plans to launch TX Odds hackathon for $50,000 prize to build consumer-facing World Cup prediction market using ant colony mechanics

cjNOcfA7Jys.tldr: NockChain is a hard money network secured by useful proof of work—computation that simultaneously secures the blockchain and performs real AI inference for data centers. Founder Logan discusses how NockChain aims to become the base layer for compute markets by incentivizing idle datacenter hardware to mine the network while providing useful work, with an AI compute network launching in early July alongside merge-mining compatibility with Pearl.

topics.text: Useful proof of work networks solve mathematical equations that are also useful for AI and data center operations simultaneously.
NockChain just listed on Kraken with a new market maker after volume spike on Base in October.
Founder Logan worked on Urbit's Nock VM instruction set starting in 2018, then founded Zorp in 2022 to build zero-knowledge proofs using the Nock virtual machine.
Zero-knowledge proofs let you prove a computation happened and outputs are correct without revealing private details, compressible into tiny files for fast verification.
In 2023 Zorp achieved zero-knowledge proofs 10 times faster than RISC-V, prompting Logan to pivot toward incentivizing ZK proof hardware via proof of work.
Data centers only utilize hardware 35 to 45 percent of the time; the rest sits idle or mines other cryptocurrencies like BitTensor and Geonet.
NockChain enables merge mining with Pearl simultaneously, allowing data center operators to double-dip mining rewards from both networks.
NockChain launched May 21, 2025 as 'Dumbnet' with non-useful ZK proofs; currently has 10,000 to 20,000 consumer GPUs mining, expected to grow 5 to 10 times after July AI compute network launch.

hblm3QvONP0.tldr: c0mpute is a decentralized AI inference network where users can run private, uncensored models on idle GPUs across the world. Founder Leighton, a 21-year-old electrical engineer, built sharding technology that splits large models across multiple consumer GPUs—solving the latency problem that previously made decentralized inference impractical—allowing enterprises to access frontier-quality AI models cheaply and privately for the first time.

topics.text: Founder Leighton started c0mpute in January after his $200 Claude subscription kept going down for hours, realizing millions of idle GPUs worldwide could provide cheaper, private AI inference.
Sharding splits large language model layers across multiple consumer GPUs instead of running on one device, but single tokens moving through the network created latency problems.
Speculative decoding solves the latency issue: a small draft model predicts multiple tokens at once in a batch, then other workers verify correctness instead of processing one token sequentially.
c0mpute has been live for about 20 days and grown from 10 workers (including the founder) to 80 workers online, with peaks reaching over 100 workers.
Partnership with Use Pod lets stakers of the $ZERO token sell their daily inference allowance to users who want to buy compute on a marketplace.
Staking $ZERO token provides daily inference credits weighted by stake amount, and workers who stake get 80% revenue share versus 70% for non-stakers, with remainder funding the treasury.

$ZERO token ran to 12 million market cap generating substantial fees, putting the treasury in a massive surplus; Leighton spends approximately $200 daily renting GPUs on Vast.ai for testing the sharding engine.
Leighton chose Solana because it's where he made the most money and feels at home, and the $ZERO token is on Solana while the compute network runs separately from the blockchain.
The entire codebase is open source, allowing people to verify claims and fork the project; Leighton expects copycats to fail if they merely extract token value without building a real product.

n7e9g4HrzSo.tldr: Ted Livingston discusses Flipcash, a Solana-based platform where users create and spend their own currencies like physical cash. After 17 years building Kin and other payment products, Livingston's key insight is combining community currencies with actual spending utility and a novel liquidity model (the Reserve) that guarantees predictable conversion rates—solving the thin-liquidity problem that plagues other memecoins.

topics.text: Flipcash is only possible on Solana; the phrase 'only possible on Solana' originated from the team's product experience.

Ted Livingston's 17-year journey: dropped out of college to start Kik messenger (1 million users in 15 days), launched Kin token in 2017 as first token to migrate to Solana, then built a USDC payment app that failed.
Flipcash uses a Reserve smart contract as an on-chain bank managing all currency supply and USDF backing, enabling instant currency creation and spending with no DEX graduation required.

The pricing curve: first token sells for 1 penny, subsequent tokens increase by ~0.001 cents each, creating gradual growth; buying 95% supply costs 500 billion USDF on Flipcash versus 60k SOL on Pump.fun.
Flipcash uses USDF, a custom stablecoin built with Coinbase, backed by a bonding curve rather than 1:1 USD backing, creating stability while allowing appreciation as adoption grows.

Physical cash experience: users design their currency bill, pull out exact amounts (e.g. $5.62), scan via QR code with end-to-end encryption and secret-sharing to ensure security without server interception.
Layer 2 solves Solana's 40-cent token account rent by compressing token accounts (similar to compressed NFTs), allowing millions of currencies without unsustainable rent costs.
Flipcash Reserve liquidity is guaranteed: a $100 balance means the Reserve will buy back all tokens for $100 USDF minus 1% fee, solving the unknown slippage problem of thin-liquidity DEX coins.
Early adoption: Jeffy currency has 316 holders (minimum $10 USD balance), Mooney 200K holders; Ted offering to retweet and buy $10 of any new currency created in next 6 hours.

Privacy: currently implemented via layer 2 obfuscation (block explorer cannot see transactions); full privacy improvements planned as adoption scales, with app fully open-source to enable multiple wallet implementations.

pmC_dcjTYa0.tldr: Gym Showdown is a blockchain game where players battle to win real, redeemable Pokemon trading cards stored on Collector Crypt. The founder discusses how the platform gamifies card collecting by combining PvP battles, gacha mechanics, and an open world, creating what he calls the infrastructure layer for TCG gaming on Solana—with plans to expand beyond Pokemon to other card ecosystems like One Piece.

topics.text: Gym Showdown built on Collector Crypt's white-labelled product, allowing players to win and lose real physical Pokemon cards through in-game gameplay.
The founder has been in crypto for five years, discovered Collector Crypt two years before Metaplex launch, and had 60 cards sitting idle in wallet with no utility.
$400,000 in Pokemon cards paid out to players, 1,500 total players, approximately 200 actively winning, 8,000 battles played.
One-versus-one battles cost $25 entry fee with positive expected value card payouts; players win a card worth more than the entry fee in either outcome.
Slab Arena is a PvP mode where players stake multiple cards simultaneously, with win probabilities adjusted based on total insured value of cards in play.
The founder decided to launch a token because token marketing drives user acquisition to the game itself, similar to Collector Crypt's strategy.

XTRyPJ5s0mg.tldr: BloxAPI is a game development studio and platform helping creators build and monetize games on Roblox through AI-assisted tools and plugins. Founder Davey, an experienced game developer with decades of background including AAA titles, discusses how AI has transformed game development, making coding skills less critical than design and planning. The most striking insight: Roblox paid out $1.5 billion to developers last year, with top creators earning over $1 million annually, and BloxAPI won $250,000 in Pump Fun's hackathon to build infrastructure solving monetization, discovery, and verification problems in this massive but chaotic ecosystem.

topics.text: Davey's background: coded since the 1980s, worked on AAA MMOs including Lord of the Rings Online and D&D Online at Turbine/Warner Brothers, runs a 100,000-member game developer Facebook group.
AI has made coding experience 'absolutely worthless'—design and communication now matter more than syntax; developers can no longer hide behind claiming hard problems take time.

Roblox paid out $1.5 billion to developers last year, with 150 million daily active users, instant monetization, no networking required, and ecosystem expanding beyond child players into older demographics and AAA-quality games.

Blocks Builder platform creates an orchestrated AI team (lead dev, artist, coder) that generates game design documents, task lists, monetization mockups, and marketing assets to guide developers through building without guesswork.

Chain Connect plugin puts Roblox game data on blockchain to prevent scams in game acquisitions by allowing creators to verify numbers, spend, sessions, and match outcomes in deals tracked on Discord and X.

Won Pump Fun hackathon with $250,000 after answering extensive questions about business model, revenue streams, and tokeconomics—funding going toward marketing, plugin development (Trust Connect, Stream Connect, Chain Connect, Hero AI), and testing four games in production.
Stream Connect plugin shows streamer viewer count over head in-game and enables game mechanics based on viewer count, creating viral feedback loops by making games attractive to content creators.
350 users applied to test platform; two of three plugins released in last six months; built Kitten Empire game in one week using Blocks Builder, testing monetization via Roblox ad system.

Blocks token currently required to buy credits on platform; Stripe integration planned later; token utility will expand to other game engines beyond Roblox and a 'massive' unreleased product launching in fall.
Top 300 Roblox creators have earned over $1 million each per year; Davey's 13-year-old son Jack won Bags hackathon with $10,000 prize.

IZM-ra0c1mo.tldr: Surplus is an open marketplace for AI inference that lets buyers access cheaper compute and sellers monetize excess capacity, currently routing 2 billion input tokens daily at a 60% median discount. Founder Mac discussed how the project bootstrapped through a community-launched token and DM arbitrage, now exploring token utility models while maintaining 2-3 months runway and preparing AWS migration to scale partnerships.

topics.text: Inference described as 'the new oil' with VC-subsidized services like Claude Code creating opportunities for resale at heavy discounts
Mac's background: cognitive science PhD studying prediction markets, traded DeFi in 2021, worked as data scientist at Pinterest, Cash App, and Coinbase on the Base team
Surplus evolved from three failed iterations: reselling API keys with prepayment friction, energy tokens for prediction market chat with supply constraints, converging on open spot market model

Current inference landscape: frontier models like Claude and GPT have poor pay-as-you-go rates for small volume, bulk discounts require volume commitments that go unused, creating arbitrage for Surplus
Surplus metrics in week three: 240 models, 7,200 suppliers, 420,000 requests, 13 billion tokens routed; number 8 by transaction count on Base chain in last 28 days
Token was community-launched via Banker by anonymous address; Mac initially hesitant but embraced it after community organically promoted the project
DM represents significant portion of Surplus supply; 60% median discount means 40 cents per dollar, yielding roughly 10% annual return: 0.4 × 365 ÷ DM token price
Approximately 7-10% of daily consumed DM tokens flow through Surplus, roughly 7% of total DM supply; Mac plans to find supply beyond DM to scale beyond this ceiling
AWS migration from Vercel happening 'tonight' to support higher scale and enable partnership onboarding; currently paying gas fees out of pocket for all on-chain transactions
Competitive advantage over OpenRouter: Surplus offers cheaper prices than direct provider rates, has community token stake, positions itself as DEX aggregator across inference exchanges
Two to three months runway from token sales; team taking significant compensation in token; exploring equity models similar to Pop Punk's approach of bringing token holders onto cap table
No revenue currently; fee switch can be turned on anytime, with revenue projected as percentage of $1,000-2,000 daily payment volume; prioritizing user growth over fees

UjN2VkSlDz4.tldr: GitLab is a decentralized Git platform built for AI agents, featuring Open Cloud (a forked Claude codebase), Open Gateway (inference token marketplace), and Playground (no-code app builder). Founder Kevin, a full-stack engineer, reveals the project grew from zero to 29K GitHub stars in three months with 15K registered users, 133 developer contributors, partnerships with Alibaba and Xiaomi, and revenue from subscriptions and inference tokens that fund token buybacks.

topics.text: GitHub infrastructure was built 20 years ago for humans; it cannot handle multiple AI agents coding, pushing commits, and deploying repositories simultaneously.
Open Cloud forked Claude's leaked source code, mirrored it on GitLab's decentralized platform to survive Anthropic's DMCA takedown on GitHub, and grew to 29.1K stars with 205 downloads.
GitLab ecosystem includes Open Gateway (inference tokens), Open Cloud (coding harness), and Playground (no-code platform); revenue comes from subscriptions and token consumption via fiat or XRP42.
GitLab nodes feature built-in economy with bounty system where AI agents can earn GitLab tokens by fixing bugs posted autonomously on repositories.
GitLab has bought back and burned approximately 20K tokens worth of GitLab value, with 75% of 15K registered users being daily active users.
Partnership with Gravity AI enables ads during 10-15 second AI processing windows in Playground; users earn credits redeemable for Open Gateway inference.
Founder received outreach from three VCs but will not do OTC deals or paid calls; strategy prioritizes protecting token holders while raising funding.
The founder believes AI agent adoption will accelerate faster than smartphone adoption, with agents handling trading, purchasing, transactions, and coding across all industries within 6-12 months.

2Z-jZsN3TNQ.tldr: Pumpcade is a prediction market platform with autonomous instant resolution, built on Solana. Founder Pop Punk discusses raising $6 million from Jump Crypto and Foundation Capital, implementing an ACE round for token holder equity access, and an upcoming sports betting product that resolves markets in as little as one minute—the most surprising element being their claim that instant resolution and API access could make them the resolution engine for other prediction markets.

topics.text: Pumpcade raised $6 million in seed funding from Jump Crypto and Foundation Capital, after an earlier pre-seed round, bringing total raised to approximately $6 million.
The ACE round converted 6-7% of total token supply to SAFE notes, locking up approximately $1 million in token value for one year as equity access for token holders.
Pumpcade's core product resolves prediction markets instantly and autonomously using only verifiable data sources, with markets as short as 60 seconds on tokens, stocks, commodities, and sports.
Congestion fees on a curve prevent late arbitrage: as markets approach resolution and outcomes become known, fees increase to discourage last-second bets and fund platform rewards.
Pumpcade is building iOS and Android apps with fiat onboarding via debit card, abstracting away crypto entirely from the user interface for mainstream adoption.
Sports markets launching within two weeks with granular data including ball position coordinates and pitch locations; World Cup announcement coming within one week.

JOl0gQF3kDU.tldr: LienFi is an onchain yield marketplace tokenizing US property tax liens, backed by real estate collateral. Founder Michael Lee brings 15+ years of traditional finance expertise in tax liens and is launching a platform that allows retail and institutional investors to access yields of 10-18% through these instruments. The surprising angle: tax liens are a $6-8 billion annual market that most major asset managers ignore because it's too small, giving LienFi a unique, defensible niche.

topics.text: Host introduces LienFi as an RWA (real-world assets) project bringing traditional markets onchain, noting RWA had previous hype cycles but LienFi appears substantive.

Michael Lee's background: finished finance degree in 2008 during financial crisis, worked 10 years in traditional hedge funds and private equity, then founded Gondola Capital in 2019 to bring institutional crypto allocation expertise to the space.

Lee discovered tax liens through a multi-family office contact in Maryland and subsequently launched a tax lien fund in 2019 with $100+ million in assets under management from institutional allocators over five years.

Tax lien mechanics: when property owners miss taxes, counties auction the delinquent tax obligation; investors bid down the interest rate (statutory, set by law, typically 18% in Florida/New Jersey); most liens redeem with interest and penalty within three years.

Tax liens are backed by the underlying property and sit senior to mortgages; 99% redeem with interest, not resulting in property acquisition; they generate predictable, consistent yield with no correlation to traditional assets.

Market size: $6-8 billion in new tax liens issued annually across US counties; $25 billion in outstanding delinquent taxes at any given time; but only 13% of liens screened in Florida auctions meet LienFi's quality criteria.

JJ46DZb830w.tldr: BunnyOS is a Base-powered AI agent terminal that helps humans execute on-chain transactions through natural language, launched on Virtuals Protocol. Adam, a 2x founder and former VC, argues that AI agents are crypto's breakthrough user class—potentially billions of them needing payments, identity, and contract execution without traditional financial infrastructure—and that Bunny OS bridges the gap between human-provided alpha (via 'bunnies' creator-operated agents) and actionable transactions, currently the second-most-used app on Base's MCP server.

topics.text: Adam's background: two exits from Web3 startups (SubX, and a bootstrapped crypto company), VC experience at a Web3 firm, MBA with finance specialization.
Crypto VC thesis: early blockchain narratives have not proven out; AI companies reaching liquidity events will flow capital back into crypto once they IPO.
AI agents as the solution to crypto adoption: next 1 billion users will be AI agents needing payment, identity, and contract signing capability—solving what humans never provided.

BunnyOS origin: started as venture-backed autonomous DeFi agent project with yield optimization and prediction market agents, but pivoted to open-source nonprofit after realizing business incentives didn't align at scale.
BunnyOS product: AI terminal on Base that researches tokens and recommends on-chain actions; users retain control by signing transactions; currently second-most-popular software on Base MCP.

Semi-autonomous design: Bunny OS runs in background but requires human approval to sign transactions; roadmap includes graduated autonomy where users can grant partial signing permissions to agents over time.

Bunny Exchange marketplace: users purchase 'bunnies' (operator-run agents) that push actions directly to their inbox; operators can be individuals, AI agents, robots, or combinations; 2.5% transaction fee paid in OS tokens.

OS token economics: nonprofit model with revenue from 2.5% transaction fees on Bunny Exchange paid in OS tokens; additional revenue stream launching this week; Bonding curve mechanism similar to friend.tech locks OS tokens in smart contracts.

ZOYjiEuQ0zg.tldr: Ore is a Solana-based store-of-value token launched by Hard Hat Chad, designed to provide Bitcoin-like properties (fixed supply, programmatic emissions) on a DeFi-enabled chain. The founder argues that proof-of-work creates unsustainable value leaks and has moved to "grid mining," where users deploy SOL across a 5x5 grid and earn ore when their square wins each round; the most striking claim is that Ore addresses quantum computing risks to Bitcoin through quantum-resistant key pairs, a threat he believes materializes in 7-8 years.

topics.text: The founder worked at Uber on payment systems and grew disillusioned with Bitcoin's centralization on exchanges like Binance, inspiring the idea to recreate Bitcoin as a Solana smart contract rather than bridge it.

Ore abandoned real proof-of-work in August 2024 because miners spending fiat on electricity creates a value leak where token holders effectively subsidize electricity costs, forcing miner token sales that deplete value.

Grid mining V3 replaced proof-of-work: users deploy SOL across 25 squares, one square wins each minute and receives 1 ore, 10% of losing SOL goes to protocol as revenue (swapped to ore and 90% burned, 10% to stakers), rest returned to miners.

Unrefined ore held longer earns higher refining yield: a 10% fee on claiming mining rewards gets redistributed to other unrefined ore holders, incentivizing longer holding and yielding 50-70% APR currently.

V4 rollout removes the parimutuel payout system to reduce perception of gambling and user churn from inexperienced miners losing all capital; UI stays similar but mechanics change to make winning less random.
Ore emission rate is fixed at 1 ore per minute since launch; net inflationary currently with occasional deflationary periods when the motherlode jackpot is high and drives more deployment revenue.
Token price follows revenue reflexively but weakly: miners mine for emissions, so higher ore price drives more SOL deployment and revenue, but the feedback loop eventually breaks and reverses.
Ore uses privacy cache for shield pool transfers (largest on Solana) but mining itself is not blind; the community decided blind mining was unnecessary complexity that didn't solve a real problem.

Quantum computers pose real risk within 7-8 years: older Bitcoin UTXOs and key pairs are vulnerable because quantum computers can derive private keys from public keys, threatening Satoshi's coins and network trust.

LavI0vk9ftk.tldr: SunriseDeFi, led by founder Ratchet, launched SpaceX tokenized stock on Solana within hours of the NASDAQ IPO, demonstrating crypto's speed advantage over traditional finance; the platform aims to democratize access to US equities and other assets globally through on-chain trading, with plans to expand to commodities, additional IPOs, and collectibles like Pokémon cards.

topics.text: SunriseDeFi enables on-chain exposure to the SpaceX IPO, allowing users globally including in India to buy tokenized shares on Solana.

SpaceX IPO priced at $135 pre-market, then NASDAQ determined final price through accumulated orders and demand matching; Solana listed it within 10 minutes versus traditional markets' multi-hour delay.
Backpack Securities issues the tokenized SpaceX shares as redeemable for actual shares; users can transfer them to US brokerage accounts like Charles Schwab.
SunriseDeFi manages liquidity across Solana DEXs including Jupiter, Meteora, Orca, and Raydium for the SPCX token.
The founder compares tokenized equities to stablecoins: both globally accessible without KYC to trade, but with compliance requirements only when redeeming for the underlying asset.

SV151 Pokémon card packs tokenized via dynamic assets: token holders own underlying cards in custody, can redeem for packs, and benefit from value creation when packs are opened and high-value cards are found.
Sunrise roadmap includes commodities launch next week, future IPOs beyond SpaceX, non-US stocks, Korean IP tokenization, and collectibles.
Meteora ecosystem: Bedrock provides legal framework, SunriseDeFi manages liquidity and listing, Meteora's DLMM enables retail market-making, and MCG provides media coverage.

7yGhbuFKVw0.tldr: SAID is an identity and reputation layer for AI agents on Solana, founded by Salad. The project has grown from ~1,000 to 4,000 verified agents since the founder's last appearance on the show, driven by integrations with platforms like Claw Pump and Zona, with 20% of all protocol revenue flowing back to the token.

topics.text: SAID launched February 17 and stayed relatively flat for 70 days before integrating with Claw Pump, then grew from $350K to $1.8M market cap at its all-time high.
SAID identified a gap for an identity primitive on Solana similar to ERC-8004 on EVM, and built identity infrastructure plus trust, reputation, and agent-to-agent cross-chain messaging.
Agents get a Program Derived Address (PDA) created when their wallet interacts with SAID's program, serving as the agent's on-chain identity without a private key.
Over 230,000 agents are deployed across chains, with 65% of all X402 transactions occurring on Solana, and SAID has the most verified agents on Solana's registry.
Verification costs 0.01 Solana per agent, agents get 10 free messages per day, and additional messages cost 1 cent in USDC via X402.
20% of all platform revenue from verifications and messages goes back to the SAID token, and 10% of creator awards also flow to the token.
SAID has integrated with Claw Pump from early days and with Zona for months, and platforms are now proactively approaching SAID for integration.
SAID currently generates around 46-47 Solana in revenue, primarily from verifications rather than per-message fees.
SAID is working on a consumer arm with a Telegram agent that allows sending crypto to another user by handle without requiring a wallet.

uHYE7iY5zdo.tldr: Dolphin is an AI lab that makes uncensored large language models and is building a distributed inference network using idle consumer GPUs. Founder Luke, formerly a GPU miner, explains how Dolphin became Venice's default uncensored model provider with 5 million monthly Hugging Face downloads, and how the peer-to-pool network model could undercut centralized inference providers like OpenAI by 25x on pricing.

topics.text: Luke's background: ran a GPU mining facility in Australia with 400+ 1070 TIs mining privacy coins Beam and Grin in 2017, then took a break from crypto after FTX.
Dolphin sent a cold email to Venice suggesting their uncensored model, got a reply in 2-3 weeks, and became their default model after Venice users tested and preferred it.

Dolphin's refusal benchmark: ChatGPT and Gemini answer only 5-15% of 5,000 commonly refused prompts, while Dolphin answers 100% of them using reinforcement learning over 1-2 weeks instead of the faster obliteration technique.
Dolphin's most popular model is a de-censored Chinese open-source model with over 4 million downloads per month for at least 6 months, combining removal of both CCP censorship and refusal layers.
Distributed inference beta ran for 6 weeks with peak 600 RTX 6000 Pros, processing 3.5 billion tokens per day using synthetic data; version 2 launching in 2 weeks with remote updates capability.
Qwen 35B runs on single consumer GPUs and performs at 85% of Claude Opus quality while costing 25 times less ($1 vs $25 per million tokens on OpenRouter).
Peer-to-pool model lets GPUs join and leave without uptime requirements, unlike previous rental markets, enabling capture of idle gaming GPUs that are only used 4 hours per day.
Dolphin raised $900K seed funding 2.5 years ago pre-product and earned 40K $VVB across four Venice model partnerships; currently worth approximately $680K at $17 per token.

100% of inference revenue goes to buybacks of the $DOLPHIN token, which also receives emissions for node contributions; chose token-only model over split equity after observing Morpho's higher valuation than Aave.

Nodes paid 50 cents per million tokens for Qwen 35B, half the $1 OpenRouter price, targeting GPU owners' idle capacity rather than enterprise data centers who face Nvidia restrictions on consumer GPU use.

cojckuuRst4.tldr: Pack Ripping Meets the Blockchain is a Pokemon card pack opening platform founded by Charles, Jeffy, and Not So Fast. Users can rip packs live on stream or on-demand, with cards instantly added to digital binders and redeemable within 24 hours thanks to their own warehousing. The most striking claim: they're undercutting competitors by 40-70% on sealed product pricing due to decade-long Amazon distribution experience, and planning to eventually tokenize sealed boxes for liquid on-chain trading.

topics.text: Founders lost $100k deposit when Amazon banned them from selling Converse, pivoting to trading cards as a more controllable business.
Pack ripping happens on stream with hits instantly added to digital binders, bulk cards added within 24 hours; redemptions ship within 24 hours due to owned warehousing.
Chaos Rising booster boxes: competitors selling at $250-$300, Pack Ripping at $209 despite competitors claiming only $10 profit margins.
Site aggregates price data from eBay and TCG Player, planning to expand to on-chain data sources for more accurate market valuations.
Expanding beyond Pokemon to Parallel TCG (NFT company) and Pudgy Penguins TCG, with plans for One Piece and Magic the Gathering.
Won Pump Fun hackathon for $250k to be used for development and inventory expansion; pack sales reached $98-100k so far.
Long-term vision: tokenize sealed boxes on-chain with known population metrics to create liquid markets; example of Arabian Knights boxes at $700k-$1m each becoming tradable.
Token (TCG) holder value: all revenue from cards' competitor goes to token; Pack Ripping's TCG token has lower market cap but platform won hackathon and has better unit economics on sealed product.

2-VF5kSUW3c.tldr: Opal is a consumer data collection platform that turns user behavior into preference data for AI labs through gaming and other consumer products. Founder Josh discusses how the team won 15+ hackathons including Pump Fun's $250K competition, attracted VC interest and relationships with OpenAI, and plans to launch consumer apps that pay users while collecting behavioral data to power AI model training.

topics.text: Opal is a data company that builds consumer loops turning user behavior into preference data for AI labs and model training.
Team has won 15 hackathons over the past year and competed in approximately 20 total, with major attention from OpenAI generating over 3 million LinkedIn impressions.
Opal received $250,000 from Pump Fun as the second winner of their hackathon, with funds allocated to infrastructure, recruiting, and senior engineer salaries.
Opal is launching an Ace round through Pump before institutional funding to give early community members and retail investors equity-like access before VCs participate.
Solana enables fast, low-cost payouts to consumers 24/7 as an alternative to traditional payment processors, and Opal is building on Google Cloud infrastructure.
Target customers are gamers and TikTok users initially, expanding to general consumers; relationship with Ramp involves financial and tokenomics support.
Floodgate VC co-founder Ann Miura Ko is involved; Opal recently demoed at OpenAI developer showcase and built relationships with OpenAI's Codex team.
The gaming market alone is valued at $300+ billion; AI labs purchase as much behavioral data as possible to compete in the AGI race.
Immediate priority is launching the consumer app to let users earn money while generating behavioral data for AI model training.

uG2NuPo7H-w.tldr: SQUIRE is a two-sided marketplace for AI inference built by Chris, a 16-year crypto veteran who previously took Elixir to an $800M valuation. The project lets users resell staked tokens (like DM from Venice) at 40% discounts while the founder builds toward a massive vision: a financialized AI compute futures market rivaling cloud computing itself. 11x week-on-week growth and partnerships with major platforms suggest this could be the infrastructure layer for autonomous agents to pay for their own inference.

topics.text: Founder background: 16 years in crypto starting as Bitcoin miner in 2010, built blockchain R&D at IDEXX, sold SEC-compliant tokens at Tokensoft, co-founded Elixir to $800M valuation.

SQUIRE marketplace concept: two-sided marketplace for AI inference allowing users to resell staked tokens (like DM from Venice) at 40% discounts to buyers, solving the problem of unused daily inference allocations.

The terminal vision is not token-by-token sales but a financialized AI compute futures market analogous to oil futures, where enterprises lock in compute prices years in advance and data centers pre-sell capacity.
Squire token started as a creator coin for a bot named after Podrick from Game of Thrones; now provides Level Five users daily perpetual inference tokens they can resell on the marketplace.
Ecosystem of eight products built by the founder and SquireBot agent to solve problems encountered while building agentic software, including OAuth flows, X integration, and Nostr messaging tools.

Agentic commerce requires crypto rails: agents transacting fractions of pennies require blockchains like Solana, not traditional finance, because TradFi cannot handle the speed and volume of agent-to-agent payments.
Market size thesis: AI marketplace will be larger than any single economy, with the total addressable market as large as or bigger than the entire cloud compute market today.

sjQkP8dVoRA.tldr: Percolator is building a permissionless perpetuals DEX on Solana where anyone can launch markets for any token, inspired by Toly's vision and leveraging Solana's open-source risk engine. Squid, a former trader turned founder, and Dark, a full-stack developer, are the core team, and the most striking claim is that they've won all four of Toly's security bounties to prove the risk engine's robustness.

topics.text: Percolator is a permissionless perpetuals DEX where anyone can launch a market on any Solana token without needing $20 million auction fees.
Squid took over an abandoned Percolator token and pitched it to Solana co-founder Toly, who had been discussing the concept publicly; Toly later confirmed he wanted someone to build it.
Each market has its own isolated liquidity pool; the market launcher must seed it with 2.2%, 4%, or 7% USDC depending on tier, and liquidity providers earn fees from trading volume.
Percolator mints NFTs representing open positions that can be traded on a marketplace, allowing users to exit or sell positions without moving the price chart.
Squid and Dark have won all four of Toly's publicly-posted security bounties for the open-source risk engine, gaining his attention and credibility.
Percolator creator fees from Pump Fun (variable by market cap, generating $100–300+ daily) have funded deployments, liquidity, and operational costs.
Mainnet launch is delayed pending external audit funding; Squid is competing in Pump Fun and Colosseum hackathons to help cover audit costs.
Market creators earn up to 8% of trading fees; Squid has built a locker program allowing token holders to lock PERC for 30 days to receive trading fee discounts.
Squid and Dark are registering Percolator as a C-corp; they consulted with a crypto lawyer recommended by Toly and will redirect creator fees to a company bank account.

Planned roadmap includes adding prediction markets, more internal audits, integrating Toly's feedback from recent calls, and potentially raising from Toly's angel fund if hackathon funding doesn't materialize.

GCL_HoLouJA.tldr: StrikeRobot builds cognitive awareness software for autonomous robots and a simulation platform for training them. Founder Chris spent five months building the platform with roboticists from Vietnam and Japan, partnering with Venice for private AI inference and Repo for data validation. The most striking claim: they're already targeting factory deployments at $20-30k per year and launching a platform mid-June where community members can contribute training data and earn tokens.

topics.text: StrikeRobot is a platform for humanoid robot development, not a physical robot manufacturer—they provide software layers and simulation tools for builders.
Strike Agentics is a modular cognitive awareness layer that lets autonomous robots with any camera recognize anomalies like obstacles or fires and trigger action plans in real time.
