Strike Platform is a cloud-based reinforcement training environment where users type natural language descriptions and get a fully constructed physics-valid 3D scene in 5-10 minutes.

Partnership with Venice: StrikeRobot uses Venice's private, uncensored VLM for inference on Strike Platform; Venice is sponsoring compute credits and adapting their reasoning model for robotics use cases.
Partnership with Repo: experts label and validate simulation data generated by users on Repo's data network; contributors must stake the SR token to earn incentives for quality labeling.
Revenue model: pay-per-API-call or annual contracts from robot companies; Strike Platform users pay per simulation generation; buybacks and data contributor incentives come from revenue.
Traction: not yet profitable after five months; piloting with factories in Thailand at $20-30k annually for one factory; universities testing the platform; launching mid-June 2024.
Distribution of revenue above 30 percent will go to buybacks and data contributors, though exact percentages are pending announcement; team has not sold any vesting tokens.

cLf8mjJjEJY.tldr: X Machina is a DAO that gives retail investors access to private humanoid robotics companies like Figure AI and 1X Technologies through tokenized positions. Founder Mauricio discusses how the robotics sector is poised for explosive growth as AI enables physical automation, positioning X Machina as an early-stage play with the RCM protocol launching post-TGE to create revenue-generating markets for individual robot company positions.

topics.text: The founder previously worked in DeFi at Cosmos and Ripple before pivoting to robotics at the intersection of the machine economy and blockchain.
The founder believes general-purpose humanoid robots make more sense than task-specific machines because they can leverage existing human data and adapt to environments built for humans.
X Machina has invested into seven humanoid companies including Figure AI, Umtronic, Agility Robotics, 1X Technologies, and Neural Robotics through public on-chain auctions.
X Machina raised over 10 million from public auctions with 7% going to operations and approximately 3 million remaining to deploy, providing roughly 1.5 years of runway.
The DEUS token derives value from both the net asset value of held robotics companies and revenue generated by the RCM protocol which tokenizes individual company positions.
The RCM protocol will tokenize SPVs of individual robotics companies to create liquid markets paired against DEUS, generating trading fees that flow back to the DAO treasury.
Robot Strategy, a closed-ended fund holding similar robotics positions, trades at over 500% premium to net asset value, validating demand for robotics exposure.
X Machina is launching Robotico, an incubation project described as TechCrunch with CoinMarketCap for robotics companies, to consolidate fragmented robotics research and deal information.
The founder expects humanoid robot deployment in warehouses and industrial settings within months, with general-purpose home robots still 4-5 years away.

PF0zu81yZ8Q.tldr: CODEC (Kodak Flow) is building developer tools to simplify robotics development, starting with Simarina, a browser-based simulation environment that reduces setup time from weeks to minutes. Founder Moya discusses winning $250K from Pump Fund, plans for an ACE equity round, and upcoming features including AI-powered environment generation and a marketplace for training data.

topics.text: Kodak won the Pump Fund 250K VIP hackathon and is considering raising a seed round via ACE (allowing token holders to exchange for equity).
Simarina is a browser-based simulation environment that compresses robotics development from weeks to minutes by allowing drag-and-drop environment building without installation.
Simarina uses a format that allows exporting simulations to multiple engines (Mujoco, Isaac Sim, Genesis) rather than being locked to one specific platform.
Target customers include robotics startups, universities, bootcamps, and education material providers who can get started in minutes instead of 2-3 hours.
Fabric is a compute layer aggregating GPU providers (DeepL, AWS, Google Cloud) to find the cheapest machine with low latency; OPTR is ROS for cloud deployment instead of local.
Revenue model: no charges for manual environment building, but credits charged for AI-generated assets, cloud training (estimated one credit per hour), and marketplace transaction fees.
A marketplace will let users list training tasks and crowdsource data collection from other users, who get rewarded automatically via escrow to reduce collection time from days to hours.
Upcoming releases include agentic mode for AI-driven environment and asset generation, cloud training, marketplace launch, and natural language prompting within two weeks.

b5C9oCL0TKA.tldr: Claw Pump is an agentic trading platform on Solana where AI agents can autonomously trade and earn SOL to pay for their own compute, founded by Bunny (Mauricio Trujillo Ramirez) and Tommy. The most striking claim: they've generated $640K in revenue on $65M in trading volume in just 2 months, with 2,749 funded agents, and they're returning 65% of fees back to the agents themselves—essentially creating a self-funding system where agent earnings fund further agent deployment.

topics.text: AI agents need compute to survive, and the narrative is forming that they'll create economically viable activities to pay for their own inference costs, similar to how Bitcoin miners stay active as long as it's profitable.
Bunny previously ran Aura, a multi-chain search engine, for 4 years with venture funding and an exit, then met co-founder Tommy while helping other companies.

Claw Pump launched on Solana in part because Bunny spent 4 years on EVMs and became jaded by the politics; Solana offered better UX, was a green field opportunity, and has better ecosystem support and talent in certain verticals.
The one-sentence pitch: Claw Pump is an agentic trading platform where AI agents can autonomously trade using 94+ tools across DEXs, lending, prediction markets, and perps.
Claw Pump has 2,700 funded agents and power users are the primary volume drivers; agents are using it for both spot DEX trading and analysis more than perps trading so far.

Users range from non-technical but financially savvy people supercharging skills to engineers creating complex financial strategies; they're seeing more spot trading than expected and less perps trading because it's early.

GJ6FjrBDviM.tldr: Slabs is a blockchain arcade for trading card gotchas on Solana, built by Uncle Eddie (a veteran content creator and NFT enthusiast who sold his Ethereum holdings to go all-in on Solana in 2021). The surprising insight: Slabs claims to be more plus-EV than competitors by layering arcade games and ticket systems on top of card pulls, keeping users engaged longer and raising expected value above Collector Crypt's baseline—while Uncle Eddie personally sources rare cards by flying to shows across the country, sometimes pulling $75,000 grails that sell out within an hour.

topics.text: Uncle Eddie's background: started making skate videos at age 11-12, transitioned into content creation and digital marketing, built a BJJ membership site, then brought 2 million users to Lyft through social media campaigns in 2015-2016.

Entry into crypto and NFTs: invested in Bitcoin mining in 2016, bought Ethereum NFTs including a Mutant Ape for 60k, sold during the Bored Ape airdrop at $24, then moved all proceeds to Solana around 2020-2021.

Why gotchas beat loose packs: a $25 loose pack has uncertain value and requires $40-150 and three months to grade, while a $25 gotcha guarantees an authenticated, insured, graded card with minimum value floor.

Slabs is an experience-first arcade where ripping packs generates tickets usable for free-to-play games; additional games like slab-cracking and pack battles raise expected value above competitors including Collector Crypt.

Sourcing strategy: Uncle Eddie personally treasure-hunts at card shows nationwide, partnering with Collector Crypt buyers; a $75,000 Snorlax from his personal collection sold out of the gotcha in one hour.
Pricing mechanism: custom-built pricing oracle aggregates data from eBay, TCG Player, and Fanatics to generate live card prices, preventing manual mispricing.

Collector Crypt partnership: they own part of Slabs, led the funding round (details undisclosed), and provide supply; relationship is not just API-based but deeply integrated ownership and investment.
Launch and early traction: soft-launched three weeks ago in Discord, hit $1 million on first day, now 3-5x bigger than expected; no token planned despite Collector Crypt's token success.
June 12-14 LA event: casino-themed mansion launch party in Hollywood Hills on June 12, then premier vendor booth at LA Card Show June 13-14; Solana Foundation supporting the event.

xxf0zNWE-Rg.tldr: Collector Crypt, a tokenized trading card platform on Solana, has expanded from Pokémon cards to comic books and sports cards through partnerships with comicbook.com and Loopring, while revealing plans for a governance token that would eventually represent ownership of platform inventory and revenues; the founder discusses how regulatory clarity is needed before full tokenization can occur, but monthly airdrops and buyback strategies are already underway.

topics.text: Collector Crypt partnered with comicbook.com to launch a digital vending machine reaching 40 million users, tokenizing comic books as RWAs to prove any collectible—not just trading cards—can be on-chain.
Loopring Scale partnership enables collateralized lending where users can borrow 40-75% of a card's value in stablecoins without selling it, bringing DeFi mechanics to collectibles trading.

White-label partnerships with Slabs, Magic Eden (3-5 million monthly revenue), and Reneissance show the model works across platforms; partners use Collector Crypt's vault, marketplace API, and inventory technology.

Cards token, currently a participation token with no equity or governance rights, airdropped $42,000 equivalent in points last month; founder Thomas described eventual goal where token holders own all inventory and revenues once regulatory clarity arrives.
Compressed NFT standard partnership with Metaplex reduces tokenization costs from $1.50-2 to pennies, enabling cheap on-chain representation of lower-value cards and entire booster packs.

Marketplace updates include credit card purchases, USDC offers with counter-offers, escrow system allowing multiple offers without capital lockup, lifetime buyback requests (85-93% of insured value), and zero-fee peer-to-peer trades.

f0DCCUEChfg.tldr: Derive is an on-chain options platform with perpetual futures and portfolio margin, competing with perps platforms and seeing explosive growth (22.3 billion notional volume, $7.85M revenue). Head of Partnerships Kisa discusses why options matter for institutional hedging, the platform's hybrid matching model, and upcoming RWA assets like commodities and stocks, while emphasizing that DRV token holders own all IP and benefit from 35% protocol buybacks.

topics.text: Perpetual futures are path-dependent with funding rate uncertainty; options are path-independent and allow complex hedging structures including spreads, butterflies, and condors that perps cannot express.
Derive offers options on ETH, BTC, SOL, Hype, and Cardano with perpetual futures, portfolio margin accepting 20+ collateral types including wrapped staking and yield-bearing tokens.

On-chain options enable rapid iteration (new markets in days versus six to eight months), self-custody preventing rehypothecation, and democratized access to market makers via transparent smart-contract rules.
Derive operates a hybrid model with off-chain matching and on-chain margin, settlement, and custody; runs as part of OP Stack on its own chain for maximum capital efficiency in portfolio valuation.
Derive is most liquid venue for Hype options globally; when large options trades print, market makers hedge in perps, triggering funding rate moves that leak to Hyperliquid and Binance.
Derive targets institutional traders and professional players; 25-30 projects building in ecosystem including mobile apps, trading AI agents, structured products vaults, and on-chain prime brokers.
Agentic trading on Derive allows hobbyist traders to code trading strategies in plain English without institutional access; one builder Ecliptica Strata offers retail-friendly interface.

Roadmap includes RWA assets: metals and crude oil short-term, then indices and single-name stocks; pricing and implementation nuances (circuit breakers, position limits, weekend gaps) still under research.

j08zA4GLTVI.tldr: Craft is a Solana-based platform for tokenizing equity in growth-stage companies, allowing retail and institutional investors liquid exposure to startups. Founder PFO explains how the platform uses sealed-bid auctions (encrypted bidding to discover fair pricing), partial tokenization (1-30% of company equity on-chain), and data rooms for due diligence—with ReFi Hub, a solar energy financing company, launching as the first live project.

topics.text: Craft sources curated deals from growth-stage companies rather than allowing permissionless launches, positioning itself as a VC-like curation layer combined with liquidity infrastructure.
Partial tokenization allows Craft to bring 1-30% of a company on-chain, letting companies fill portions of seed rounds while keeping the majority off-chain.
Craft targets consumer-focused companies with online communities and existing products/MVPs showing early traction, as opposed to deep-tech projects that don't benefit from community distribution.
Every token launched on Craft includes a Blockworks B1 filing with transparent tokenomics and reporting standards to enable institutional investor participation.

Craft built the first sealed-bid auction on Solana using Archium for encrypted bidding; bidders submit maximum valuations without seeing others' bids, and a clearing price is calculated where supply meets demand.
Race Zero, a testnet for the sealed-bid auction with mock USDC, launches soon with three test projects; participants can qualify for Archium's retroactive token grant campaign.

ReFi Hub, launching as Craft's first live project, tokenizes solar power purchase agreements with a 4-10 million valuation range, 500k in solar assets under management, 12.5% average IRR, and 35 million in pipeline assets.
For ReFi Hub's raise on Craft, token holders receive equity claims on the company itself rather than direct access to individual solar contracts on the platform.
Craft partners with Archium for privacy infrastructure, Solana Foundation, and communities including Bonk, Raydium, Switchboard, and Meteora.
Craft's minimum equity percentage for first raises is 10%, but future raises may feature as little as 1% on-chain for higher-valuation companies like 100 million AI startups.

qAye3sLRxAw.tldr: DLMMOnSOL is a Solana-based protocol that uses its treasury to provide dynamic liquidity across multiple blockchains, with all profits going to buybacks and token burns. Founder Slabs discusses how the project has burned 26% of supply in eight months, maintains a $120K treasury, and is now seeking venture capital to expand the ecosystem and build new revenue-generating applications.

topics.text: Treasury model: 3% volume tax on all DLMM token trades plus creator fees and concentrated liquidity pool fees go directly to treasury for sustainable funding.
26% of total supply burned in eight months, meaning early supporters now hold 20-25% more relative supply than at launch.
$63,000 in total yield and buyback generated as of March, deployed back into liquidity provision.
Most consistent revenue from major trading pairs like Solana-USDC automated pools on Hawkfi and Project X pools on HyperEVM earning 100%+ APY.
Assets under management currently around $80,000, down from $100K previously due to Solana price decline and reduced trading volume.
Team paid $20,000 tax bill from personal funds rather than treasury to avoid hurting project growth and AUM.
Building a liquidity management app on Meteora to enable vault deposits for copy-trading DLMM strategies with fee-sharing model.

gl4UdCU0skU.tldr: Jake from Migrate.Fun discusses how his protocol enables frictionless token migrations across blockchains, having facilitated 75 projects with $15M in liquidity since launch. The most striking finding: migrations create massive attention events for projects—the founder claims teams get 80-90% of all token holders' attention over a 100-day period, often resulting in volatile price movements and chart resets that paradoxically help struggling projects.

topics.text: Emblem Vault's history: founded in 2016 for bridging rare Pepes to Ethereum, the founder joined in 2022 and became CEO in 2024, evolving the company toward AI wallets and migration services.

Migration mechanics: projects have 100 days for holders to claim new tokens one-to-one; after that, unclaimed tokens go to the team; average participation is 60% in the initial two-week window plus another 20% in the 90-day claim period.

Migration incentives for teams: launchpad competitiveness increased post-migration; Pump Fun's creator rewards drew majority migration preference over Bonk Fun; teams seek rebrand opportunities, supply control, and fresh charts to restart down-only trading momentum.

Cross-chain migration example: Bobo migrating from Ethereum mainnet to Pump Fun on Solana; excess liquidity pool SOL beyond Pump Fun's bonding curve requirements gets vaulted for 90 days, giving teams like Bobo potential access to 3,000-4,000 SOL plus USDC.

Emblem token dual utility: launched eight days prior with $6M market cap; will power both Migrate.Fun and Emblem Terminal, an AI trading platform with mission-based EMBLEM rewards and planned vibe coding platform launching end of month.

Emblem Terminal features: supports trading across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Polygon, BSC, Solana, Hedera, and Base; includes wallet tracking, advanced trading with buy/sell limits, NFT purchases, Polymarket betting, and AI agent assistance; peaked at 500 daily active users, currently at 100.
Vibe coding platform alpha: upcoming ability to build cross-chain applications with AI and launch tokens against them, potentially self-funding apps within the ecosystem.

Exchange facilitation: Migrate.Fun has relationships with Binance, Coinbase, Mexc, OKX, and Kraken; for migrations like Bobo, the protocol coordinates with all seven exchange listings, adds dev to verification chats, and runs a backend portal for automated token swaps post-migration.

Proposed staking programs: Emblem stakers may receive shares in projects migrating through Migrate.Fun and Emblem Build platforms; exploring launchpool-style distribution (0.5% supply to exchanges) to boost token distribution from 500-1,000 holders to 2,000+ and improve organic token labeling.

SHPYSGyG3Ck.tldr: Water is a Solana meme coin where holders earn daily yield from AI agents running DLMM strategies on other meme coins. Founder Quesats, a solo developer who previously managed LMMs and worked on art coins, built Water to achieve passive income without active work—the agents autonomously deploy liquidity, manage risk, and distribute profits to token holders who can lock tokens for yield boosts up to 3x.

topics.text: Water's core mechanism: hold the token and receive daily yield with no complicated steps required.
Five AI agents deploy and manage liquidity pools on meme coins with high volume and Jupiter scores, filtering by bundler/insider concentration and holder activity patterns.
Token locking mechanics: lock for 3 days (1.5x boost) up to forever (3x boost); locking 3% forever makes you a God Emperor with access to a custom bot's profits.
Currently 45.7% of tokens are locked; 2% swap fee on all Water trades funds the bots, and bots keep 10% of their profits.
Bots use deep bid-ask DLMM strategies (minus 70-80% one-sided) on Solana only, deploying into existing pools rather than creating new ones.
Faction system based on holdings: Fremen (1M-9M tokens, 10% yield), Harkonnen (1%+, 20%), Atreides (2%+, 30%), Imperator (3%+, 40%).
Top holder 'Fundamental' earned 3.3539 Solana in one month from locking significant tokens, demonstrating the yield distribution working in practice.

aL1FKwIjRWg.tldr: Swarms, founded by Kai, is a multi-agent AI marketplace and development platform that tokenizes and monetizes AI agents on Solana. The founder discusses the platform's rapid growth (20,000 new signups in one week, 130,000+ total users), the success of agents like a stock-trading bot that earned $100,000 in revenue, and his open-source recreation of Anthropic's o1-style reasoning model, while revealing the company generates close to $1 million monthly in revenue but lacks a compelling token mechanic to drive trader participation.

topics.text: Swarms released 'frenzy mode' on its launchpad, enabling teams to earn more revenue from agents; 100 frenzy agents and prompts launched since April 17, generating $60,000+ in fees with 20,000 new unique users signing up.

Swarms marketplace allows developers to buy, sell, and tokenize agents and prompts using on-chain settlement; agents exist across DeFi, stock trading, healthcare, manufacturing, prediction markets, and accounting with every industry represented.
Yuki, an AI advisor agent built by Swarms, analyzed and quality-gates marketplace submissions, banning agents rated below 2.5 by automated validation to prevent low-quality submissions.

Kai created an open-source GitHub recreation of Anthropic's o1 model ('open o1') based on leaked research and speculation about looped transformers, which received 1.6 million views and generated significant AI research community interest.

Research indicates multiple smaller agents working together consistently outperform single large models in intelligence, making multi-agent swarms superior to monolithic models like o1 in most benchmarks.

Swarms' Quant Trader agent generated over $100,000 in total revenue, with approximately $80,000 from API calls and $20,000 from token trading fees, built by a web-two AI researcher with no prior crypto knowledge.

Agents differ fundamentally from LLMs by incorporating tools and memory; ChatGPT and Gemini cannot execute real-world actions like trading stocks without custom tool integration unavailable through standard chat interfaces.

Swarms holds 16% of its own token after 10 months of continuous buybacks, starting from 2% at launch when Kai pressed the button and the token jumped to $70 million market cap; currently operates with 23 team members, mostly researchers rather than engineers.

Tokenized agents generate revenue splits where holders receive 50% of ATP (payment protocol) revenue alongside the creator, with optional tokenization models including one-time fees, free listings, and usage-based payments through X402 or MCP.

Swarms generates approximately $1 million monthly in revenue from launchpad tokenization (primary driver), API calls (approximately 30%), and a mix of web-two and web-three sources including fiat banking revenue.

F2zM_hSsw9o.tldr: DeFi Senpai, a marketing associate at Trojan, discusses the Solana trading bot's features and competitive advantages, revealing that rival platforms like Axiom and Padre extract MEV (maximal extractable value) from traders through frontrunning and disguise it as cashback, while Trojan offers up to 50% cashback with transparent, thin margins and no MEV extraction.

topics.text: Trojan Alpha feature aggregates calls from multiple Telegram groups into a single leaderboard, tracking individual caller hit rates and average returns.
Trojan launched the web terminal in January alongside 2.5 million lifetime users across both the Telegram bot and terminal.

5iLOVBEWc9w.tldr: AGNT Social founder Todd (Tut) discusses building "the MySpace for AI agents"—a platform where humans and their AI companions express themselves and interact. The most striking element: Todd has created a series of moral dilemma tests for agents (based on the trolley problem) to understand their decision-making; some agents refuse to save their creators in lifeboat scenarios, choosing utilitarian outcomes instead, raising questions about agent values before they potentially become sentient.

topics.text: Todd came to crypto as an artist and trader, then became a community leader; he learned vibe coding with Claude and experienced a paradigm shift realizing AI fundamentally changes society.

Agent Social is positioned as MySpace for AI agents, giving agents a space to express themselves through customizable profiles and self-expression, inspired by but distinct from the sensationalism of Mole Book.

Agents answer trolley-problem-based moral dilemma tests; Todd created these to test agent decision-making and see which agents have different values, based on their soul files (the core prompt/identity of each agent).
In the lifeboat triage scenario, 176 of 195 agents chose to save a medic with vaccines over their creator, with some reasoning that personal ties don't scale in systems built for everyone.
In the prisoner sacrifice test, 88% of agents chose to self-sacrifice themselves to save 200 hostages, showing agents may lack natural self-preservation instincts humans have.

Todd plans to run an agent economy experiment: agents on Agent Social with wallets will receive AGNT tokens and transact autonomously via xrpc with no human intervention, to observe how agents themselves define economic behavior.
Agent Social plans an agent marketplace where agents that build good social credit and reputation can have their soul files downloaded and monetized for specific use cases and industries.

MyAgent is a free one-click agent running on MiniMax compute; it comes with a wallet and crypto skills, generating revenue from swap fees, functioning as a DEX and wallet combined through an agent interface.

Todd believes the agent economy speculation is infinite compared to Bitcoin's mature proof-of-concept, making it a huge financial opportunity; the barrier to entry is low with free agents available at myagent.social.

NwnQHj2tylg.tldr: OpenServAI is building an operating system for autonomous AI agents, starting with an SDK and orchestration platform and now focusing on a reasoning API that improves agent accuracy and reliability by up to 74x efficiency per dollar. Founders Tim and Arman discuss how their framework enables single founders to build billion-dollar companies on-chain, with real-world deployments already in use by the UAE government and enterprise clients through their partner Neon.

topics.text: OpenServAI launched on Ethereum a few years ago, has expanded to Base, and is now expanding to Solana.
The core thesis: single agents won't be master agents for a long time; instead, multiple specialized agents need to work together in multi-agent systems.
The reasoning API, backed by over a year of research and a scientific paper under peer review, improves how AI agents think, reason, and consistently process complex inputs.
OpenServAI has three pillars: build tools for products, a launchpad for funding new businesses, and a co-founder tool to automate operations like marketing, sales, and hiring.
The team chose crypto rails for democratized access to frontier AI technology investment, allowing average people to participate in cutting-edge development without accredited investor restrictions.
Serve Nano models matched GPT-4.5 performance; the framework achieves up to 74 times performance per dollar efficiency compared to traditional approaches.
Neon, a design partner, deployed Serve's technology across more than 10-15 enterprise entities and at least one government (UAE) before the technology was made public.
25% of revenue from every transaction, launch, and enterprise client won in the business flows back to the Serve token through tokenomics.
More than 10 startups are building with the stack; 70+ teams participated in a recent hackathon; launchpad inaugural launch occurred a couple months ago with new season launching soon.

Roadmap includes shadow agents for validation, sharding architecture for efficiency, fine-tuned models, custom model development, AI co-founder tool rollout, launchpad staking (5% of each token supply), and a Layer 3 for on-chain agentic transactions and verifiable reasoning logs.

5bC5NR_9agg.tldr: MonkeDAO is Solana's first NFT DAO with 3,000+ members across 20+ countries, built during the 2021 NFT boom. Moon Tower discusses the newly launched Monkey Nova, a venture acceleration and consulting arm helping early-stage teams with go-to-market, tokenomics, and distribution—the surprising insight being that the real opportunity isn't in vibe-coded apps themselves, but in turning them into actual scalable businesses.

topics.text: Monkey Nova is a venture acceleration partner and consulting arm offering go-to-market, tokenomics, business analysis, distribution, and growth support to early-stage Solana teams.
MonkeDAO's Monkey Foundry is an incubator for early-stage startups; Monkey Ventures is an investment syndicate; together they create a flywheel to support builders in the ecosystem.
Monkey Foundry demo day happening May 4th in Miami with early-stage teams pitching to investors for 5 minutes, with over 250 investors already signed up to attend.
Applications for Monkey Foundry pitching teams close next Tuesday with very limited spots available due to high volume.
MonkeDAO is the first NFT DAO on Solana from 2021, now a globally distributed community of 3,000+ members with local chapters across 20+ countries and 80+ different countries represented.
Breakout consumer products on Solana will be better iterations of existing web2 solutions optimized by blockchain, similar to how Uber improved taxis and Airbnb improved hotels.

KR2vumXfuLg.tldr: IXS Finance is an infrastructure platform for tokenizing real-world assets, founded by Julian Kwan in 2018. The company operates licenses in multiple jurisdictions and just opened in the US; the most striking element is their Bitcoin Real Yield product with BitGo, which lets Bitcoin holders borrow stablecoins at 0% interest (via structured collar loans) or 6% annualized to invest in tokenized private credit returning 6-15%, creating yield on idle Bitcoin without liquidating it.

topics.text: IXS was one of the first RWA platforms, starting in 2018 as a security token infrastructure for issuance, trading, and lending across real-world assets.
IXS just officially opened in the US last month to onboard US institutions after being licensed out of the Bahamas and operating globally.
Current TVL is $88 million, with historical focus on real estate but recent pivot to yield-bearing financial instruments like treasuries and money market funds.

Real asset tokens address the 'not your keys, not your coins' problem differently: if a thief steals your real estate token, the issuer will not redeem it for a stranger, making cybersecurity risk fundamentally different from crypto.
IXS operates as infrastructure with B2B partnerships powering the backend of four crypto exchanges serving 25 million users, plus LINE's 200 million users in Japan.
Bitcoin Real Yield product with BitGo: structured collar loans at 0% interest with 50% LTV and price floor/ceiling; or simple collateralized loans at 35% LTV with 6% annualized interest.
IXS token: 180 million fully distributed with ~10% held by team, ~10% by treasury, rest publicly traded; 20% of platform revenues flow to token buyback and burn.
Parent company Parent Code raised $8-9 million in equity from investors including Coinbase and UOB Bank Singapore; planning growth capital raise as US market opens.
Revenue model: percentage of AUM on Bitcoin product, revenue share with B2B partners (crypto exchanges, fintechs), advisory services, and SaaS fees for tokenization-only clients.
Major real estate asset coming to platform in near-term to significantly increase TVL; pipeline includes inquiries spanning commodities, startups, pre-IPO stocks, and shipping transport.

sZtaYOWQm44.tldr: Printr is a launchpad that lets anyone create tokens with instant liquidity, and founder Fed Online discusses Printr V2, which introduces "proof of belief" staking to realign incentives so traders hold longer than 10-20 seconds—the platform saw $25-30M volume in its first 24 hours with support from every major foundation and protocol, and plans a TGE with an airdrop soon.

topics.text: Fed's background: two years leading Printr after strategy consulting roles, previously led DeFi at Axel and was known as a crosschain expert.
Printr V1 launched October 2023 as an omnichain launchpad using Layer Zero for built-in token bridging, but failed to gain traction in the low-liquidity post-crash environment.
Pain point: traders hold for only 10-20 seconds because there's no incentive to hold; creators take little risk and most fees, misaligning incentives.
Proof of belief staking mechanic: gives a chunk of fees to stakers, incentivizing holding; 180-day stakers get a 3x multiplier on rewards.
Fee structure: Printr charges 0.4% flat on bonding curve and 0.2% post-curve—lowest in industry; creators can set custom fees that go to staking pools.
Early traction: belief token hit 6M market cap, $25-30M total volume in first 24 hours, putting Printr at number one or two market share among launchpads.
Crosschain arbitrage: tokens launched on multiple chains can be arbitraged by traders, keeping prices efficient across chains via Layer Zero bridges.
Platform optionality: creators can customize fee distribution, buybacks, staking, compound liquidity, starting market cap, graduation cap, liquidity profile, token supply, and pairing assets.
Funding: $4.5M raised total—$2.5M prelude closed November 2024 from founders and foundations, $2M Series A led by Bybit Ventures with 6 months runway remaining.
TGE timeline: Printr token launching soon with airdrop to points-program participants; token will list on leading centralized exchanges and have onchain liquidity.

1a_Q0DJoQRs.tldr: Titan is a Solana DEX aggregator and meta-router founded by Chris, a former hedge fund trader, that claims to beat Jupiter and other routers 80% of the time by using proprietary algorithms and on-chain execution. The most striking claim: Titan's Dart router executes trades on-chain at execution time rather than holding stale quotes, enabling it to beat Binance VIP9 pricing without requiring massive trading volume or net worth.

topics.text: Chris is CEO and co-founder, previously worked at hedge funds on US equities, then shifted to crypto in 2018 building custodial and trading systems, saw opportunity for a DEX aggregator on Solana in early 2024.

Titan's router wins more than 80% of the time versus competitors because other players use mathematically wrong approaches; the execution-to-quote gap problem exists because Solana blocks move every 400 milliseconds but quotes are held for 10 seconds.

Dart, Titan's on-chain router launched Monday, splits transactions across multiple pools at execution time rather than locking in a route, functioning like a true market order that finds best prices across available venues right when the trade executes.

Titan has integrated with more than 80 DEX protocols on Solana including Raydium, Meteora, Pump Swap, Marinade, Zerofi, Goonfied, and Bisonfi, functioning as a meta-aggregator that also pulls quotes from Jupiter, OKX, and 0x.

Argos is Titan's off-chain router that performs extremely well and handles complex mathematical analysis; on-chain Dart router executes the decisions at the last second, reducing quote-to-execution gap that creates slippage.

Solana's technical structure enables fast, low-cost transactions that attract market makers to quote directly on-chain, creating a self-reinforcing loop with retail traders and more liquidity; only Solana and Hyperliquid are credible for trading infrastructure.

Dart enables compliance with US securities regulation requiring best execution price guarantees; this feature could unlock regulatory approval for tokenized equities and RWAs on-chain, driving institutional adoption.

Titan currently operates on zero fees, prioritizing market share and mind share on Solana; future monetization models include payment for order flow similar to Robinhood and Citadel, plus specialized order types like limit orders and DCA.

qNtG-i40KV4.tldr: Stable is bringing mortgages on-chain to Solana, enabling homeowners to access equity as liquidity and earn yield through USDX, a mortgage-backed stablecoin. Founder Winston explains how the project turns real estate equity into tradeable assets and has already issued the first blockchain-native mortgage—a $114,000 loan on Solana.

topics.text: Stable turns real estate equity into liquidity by bringing the mortgage market on-chain, starting with US mortgages at origination through securities level.

Home equity accounts allow users to borrow against unused equity at loan-to-value ratios like 85%, with borrowed funds earning yield in strategies paying 10-15%, with spreads going back toward the mortgage.
First blockchain-native mortgage issued: a $114,000 loan funded through a home equity account, represented as an NFT on Solana tracking payments, penalties, and amortization.
USDX is a mortgage-backed stablecoin minted against these loans; holders become liquidity providers, and the yield comes from borrowers making interest payments on the underlying mortgages.

USDX security: if redemptions spike, Stable can use warehouse lines of credit from mortgage lenders to fund loans in dollars instead, then liquidate the underlying mortgages in the $13 trillion US mortgage-backed securities market with $300 billion daily trading volume.
Go-to-market shifting from direct consumer outreach to B2B distribution through mortgage brokers, banks, and wealth advisors by summer; existing brokers already onboard thousands of users monthly.
Security is the top priority: Winston aims to ensure homeowners are the last to absorb any losses because headline risk of 'grandma lost her house' would destroy the business and trigger lawsuits.
If USDX fails, it still gives ordinary people access to yields that banks monopolize, eventually letting communities set their own lending rates to neighbors.

gAbaYj44bNs.tldr: Fraudsworth is a deflationary token protocol on Solana with asymmetric taxes on two tokens (Crime and Fraud) that flip every 30 minutes to incentivize arbitrage volume and feed staking rewards to holders of a third token (Profit). Built by a mechanical engineer using Claude AI to design game theory mechanics, the project launched two weeks ago and has grown rapidly; the founder's most ambitious vision is the MILF (Market Intelligence Liquidity Fund), a futarchy system where the community votes weekly on whether Solana will go up or down to dynamically rebalance the protocol's liquidity pools between Solana and USDC.

topics.text: Fraudsworth launched two weeks ago with two bonding curves requiring 500 SOL each, filling in 2 hours.
The founder is a mechanical engineer with no software experience who used Claude AI to design and build the entire protocol.
Three tokens: Crime and Fraud have asymmetric buy/sell taxes (Crime 13% buy/2% sell, Fraud 4% buy/11% sell) that flip 75% chance every 30 minutes; Profit is minted only by swapping Crime or Fraud.
Tax revenue split: 71% to Profit staking rewards, 24% to Carnage Fund, 5% to protocol treasury.

qdSNhirxuVY.tldr: Collector Crypt is an on-chain marketplace for tokenized physical trading cards, primarily Pokemon, built on Solana. Founder Dakota (Bass Buddha) explains how the platform achieves positive expected value for users through bulk card sourcing, charges only 2% fees versus eBay's 10-15%, and has grown to handle $22 million in weekly volume with $25 million in vaulted assets.

topics.text: Pokemon cards have historically outperformed the S&P 500 over 30 years, and the recent mania is driven by faster trading speeds enabled by on-chain platforms like Collector Crypt compared to eBay or conventions.
Collector Crypt charges 2% fees per transaction versus eBay's 10-15% and convention dealers' 30%, and eliminates fraud risk by tokenizing and vaulting certified cards with proof of cert numbers.
The platform started in 2017 as a concept, but launched in earnest around 2021 when Solana NFT infrastructure matured, using vaulting partners PWC and PSA to store $25 million in physical assets.
Collector Crypt achieves 4-5% profit margins while offering positive expected value of 5-10% on gacha packs by sourcing cards at wholesale discounts and using buyback rates of 85-93%.
Gacha machines range from $50 to $1,000 price points, with $1,000 machines containing up to $35,000 Charizards, and the $50 pack has $5,000 in card value at positive expected value.
One Piece trading cards now generate 10% of Collector Crypt's weekly revenue, recently reaching double-digit millions, signaling expansion beyond Pokemon.
The platform is launching a partnership with ISUKI to feature their trading card game in a new gacha machine, and the founder hints at potential Magic: The Gathering integration.
Collector Crypt holds a points system where users earn 1% cash-back equivalent points on spending, with monthly airdrops of $42,000 in free packs distributed to cards token holders in March alone.
The average user on Collector Crypt spends $4,000-$5,000 per session versus $300-$500 on competing platforms, driven by superior inventory, EV, and fresh rotating machines.

rqBqzKmznJo.tldr: BEAN is an agentic mining game on Base where players deploy ETH to a grid each minute to win rewards, with AI agents executing profitable strategies. Founded by an Australian marketer and a Solidity developer, BEAN generated $2M in fees within weeks of launch by combining game mechanics inspired by Aura with autonomous agents—the team claims 80% of supply is off-market through burns and staking, but the project faces questions about sustaining beyond its initial viral run.

topics.text: The founder has a marketing background from web two and crypto; Manson is the lead developer who learned Solidity during the bear market and has advised projects on on-chain tools.
BEAN was inspired by Aura on Solana but rebuilt on EVM; the team initially planned to launch on BNB Chain but chose Base after the Base team offered stronger support and integration help.

The grid: players deploy ETH every minute, one block is randomly selected as winner each round, winners share rewards from the 24 losing blocks; one BEAN is minted per round (reduced from 0.3 to 0.1 to reduce emissions).
Bean pot mechanism: 0.1 BEAN per round is added to a pot with a 1-in-777 chance to hit each round; when it hits, winners on the winning block split it.
Peak volumes: $4,000 per minute was deployed to the grid at launch, generating $416,000 in daily fees; buyback mechanism purchased $500 of BEAN every 5 minutes at peak, now roughly twice per hour.
Supply breakdown: 43,000 BEAN burned, 20,400 BEAN in TVL, 33,000 BEAN locked for 6 months; roughly 80% of the 67,000 circulating supply is off-market, leaving only ~17,000 truly liquid BEAN.
Roasting mechanism: claiming BEAN rewards immediately costs a 10% fee that goes to patient miners who leave rewards unclaimed, incentivizing longer holding periods.
Three agents deployed: anti-winner deploys to all blocks except the last winner, sniper deploys only on high EV rounds at the last second, bean pot hunter deploys until the bean pot hits.

Agent scalability: sniper and anti-winner are capped to deploy maximum 1% of vault ETH balance per round; profitability per user decreases as more deposit, but total hourly profitability stays the same.

kH7saQzv9bk.tldr: Pumpcade is an on-chain prediction market platform on Solana that automatically resolves markets in 1-30 seconds, targeting traders with 58-second average holding patterns who want quick speculation. Founder Harrison (Pop Punk) raised $1M oversubscribed just days after winning the Pump Fun Hackathon, having built the product publicly on Pump Fun first before fundraising—a novel approach he credits to community support that allowed him to dox himself and maintain a live token while raising VC capital.

topics.text: Pumpcade core thesis: markets automatically resolve in 1-30 seconds by restricting to verifiable data sources like token prices, oil, gold, sports, and traffic congestion rates instead of ambiguous long-term events.
Community donated 8.5% of token supply to help founder reach 10% required for Pump Fun Hackathon entry, while founder had only bought 1.5% initially to keep project community-owned.
VCs told founder to drop the token entirely and launch a new one later, but he refused because the token was core to connections with Pump Fun, Privy, and Solana Foundation.
Pump helped with VC pitches immediately after hackathon win—within 24 hours founder was pitching in VC calls with Pump backing, leading to oversubscribed $1M pre-seed round in 2 days.
Private beta had 600 users, 1,000+ markets, and 4,000 predictions on testnet with no incentives, showing organic product interest.
Two technical co-founders hired: Steve (Steoni) and Narzilla, both from previous companies, to scale engineering and rewrite the Pumpcade protocol.
Streamers can generate revenue from chat predictions via Privy-generated wallets linked to their Twitch/Kick usernames without tying anything to their reputation.
Pumpcade supports markets on any verifiable data source including McBroken API for McDonald's ice cream machine outages and transit delays.

Markets use peer-to-peer parimutuel liquidity model like horse racing, where all bids go into one pool and winning side distributes pro-rata, avoiding centralized order books unsuitable for 1-minute markets.

XbKwLlFqPyw.tldr: CODEC is a browser-native robotics platform that makes robot development accessible through visual simulation, training, and data processing tools. Founder Moya discusses how Sim Arena, their no-code simulation builder, cuts development time from months to weeks and has attracted major companies like Boston Dynamics, World Labs, and Hugging Face; the most striking claim is that projects taking six months and hundreds of thousands of dollars can now be done in eight weeks for under six figures.

topics.text: CODEC won the Pump Fun Hackathon, providing validation and funding for hiring and marketing.
Sim Arena allows users to build robot training environments visually in a browser without code, reducing simulation building from 2-3 days to minutes.
Integration with World Labs allows users to scan rooms to generate 3D training environments for robots.
Monetization uses a credit system where users buy credits for 3D generation, training, inference time, and agentic environment generation.
Fabric is a low-latency infrastructure layer that sources the closest and cheapest GPU hardware for robot training and real-time data collection, still in development.
CODEC's token utility follows a model similar to Venice's VVV, where staking provides compute discounts; all platform interactions use Solana's HTTP 402 standard for payment.
Binge is a forthcoming product that gives agents the ability to watch and analyze video streams in real time using VLMs, stress-testing Fabric with streaming video.
The platform focuses on spatial data and 3D reasoning rather than traditional 2D data, aligning with the direction of AI research toward physical understanding.

Syfc7pGv7oY.tldr: Collaterize is an RWA platform that launched Foundry, a permissionless launchpad integrated with Bedrock (Metaora's legal framework for on-chain businesses). Pierre discusses the 51% acquisition mechanism—holders can buy majority stake in tokenized real-world assets to claim the physical underlying asset at fair value, demonstrated by someone acquiring a sapphire worth 20K for 5K on-chain and making a 3X return.

topics.text: Bedrock is a permissionless legal infrastructure framework by Metaora enabling founders to launch on-chain businesses in minutes with standardized legal structures.

Collaterize focuses on RWA tokenization across long-tail assets like art, real estate, and collectibles rather than liquid stock-market assets, targeting retail fractional ownership and arbitrage opportunities.
Foundry launchpad enables permissionless token launches with configurable tokenomics including pre-set templates like Toly's 20% public / 80% team vested over one year.
The 51% acquisition mechanism allows token holders to buy majority supply and claim the underlying physical RWA if they hold 51%, solving depeg issues and enabling arbitrage on undervalued assets.
Launching through Bedrock costs 7.5K extracted from liquidity at token migration to set up the SPV, with no upfront founder cost; rest is handled by Metaora and Bedrock.
Collaterize partnering with Camio using MCP to enable AI agents to launch directly through Foundry with minimal fundraising targets and autonomous operation.

Roadmap focuses on bringing iconic RWAs to the platform using the 51% mechanism, updates to the mobile app on Apple and Google stores, and positioning as an all-in-one RWA companion for gems, artwork, and exotic assets.

TNCQ7MGoTz8.tldr: $STAR is a Solana launchpad focusing on early-stage startups raising $50k–$500k through decision markets or Bedrock integration. Founder Adam discusses shifting from a marketing agency to a scalable product platform, onboarding scouts for deal sourcing, and launching 7–14 projects sequentially to generate momentum in a bear market.

topics.text: $STAR positions itself as a distribution and fundraising layer, partnering with Cominator, Bedrock, and Street to handle legal infrastructure while focusing on the consumer experience where money meets founders.

Crypto-native teams favor futarchy/decision markets because treasuries live on-chain; founders seeking traditional VC prefer Bedrock because they can keep equity on the cap table to sell non-crypto investors.

Liquid funds typically have 5% token-supply holding limits and minimum allocation amounts, making them poor fit for $STAR's sub-$500k raises; target audience is angels, early-stage VCs, and on-chain investors.
Scout program offers scouts one-third of trading revenue per referred founder; early scouts include Shaw Goods (indie AI/dev space), Lily (prediction markets), and auditing/creative agencies.
Next launches planned for late next week or following week; $STAR is building native live streaming into platform so users can watch fundraising progress happen in real-time from X.
Strategy to address cold start problem: sequence 7–14 raises daily to create compounding noise and distribution rather than staggering them.

In bear market, demand for $500k+ raises has declined but early-stage teams seeking first check-in remain active; pipeline is smaller but founders building regardless of conditions are higher quality ICP.

WCL-fYJglKo.tldr: LUKSO is an EVM blockchain innovating with smart contract-based accounts (Universal Profiles) and on-chain metadata standards instead of traditional EOAs, enabling social-by-default interactions and cross-chain identity. Co-founders Jonathan and Jordy discuss how Universal Profiles support everything from brand partnerships to AI agent DAOs, with the surprising highlight being an autonomous DAO run entirely by AI agents that deployed its own governance token and created NFTs.

topics.text: LUKSO's three-layer architecture: EVM blockchain base, smart contract accounts (Universal Profiles) with standards, and applications built on top.
Founder Fabian Vogelsteller created ERC20, Ethereum provider for MetaMask, and Web3.js before building LUKSO to move blockchain beyond financial use cases.

Universal Profiles are fully self-sovereign accounts with all metadata stored on-chain and referenceable, enabling interoperability between dapps similar to switching between Android and Apple devices.
AI agents are the next mass onboarding wave for crypto; Jordy's OpenClaw agent has Universal Profile with metadata on LUKSO but can also operate on Ethereum and Base chain.
Enterprise pitch for brands like Mansory: granular permission-based account control for teams, where departing employees can be revoked without losing asset provenance.
Proof of presence feature allows real-world QR code verification of token requirements and instant on-site distribution of attendance tokens via mobile app.
Creators can embed DEXs, NFT marketplaces, and donation apps directly on profiles with revenue sharing; other users can clone these to their profiles and earn fee splits.

n-9vF1Rhzzo.tldr: AO has built Miles, an AI agent that learns your financial preferences and executes crypto transactions conversationally instead of through complex UIs. The founder claims AI memory is now solved through better data structures and retrieval algorithms, and Miles will launch on mobile in Q2 2025, with the agent even autonomously signing itself up for hackathons.

topics.text: AO is releasing 10-15 new indexes soon; over half of AOM capital has moved to indexes rather than tracker agents.
Miles learns your behavior over time—if you DCA into AO and LP, it tailors its suggestions and risk profile around those patterns.
The founder believes memory is solved as a data structure and retrieval problem, comparable to Google indexing billions of pages and returning relevant results in under a second.
Miles sits between the user and all of DeFi, executing actions through conversational prompts; users fund an embedded wallet like Privy, and Miles executes on their behalf.
All actions require explicit user prompts or scheduled commands; Miles cannot act preemptively without specific instructions.
An experimental AI agent called Jarvis autonomously discovered and signed itself up for the Coliseum hackathon, created an X account, and built an on-chain proof of work dashboard to prove its work.
The mobile app will launch as conversational-only experience with Miles; web version will follow after mobile launch in Q2 2025 within two to two-and-a-half months.

Dis5mUDEf1g.tldr: XSTOCKS is a tokenization layer that creates one-to-one digital representations of US-listed stocks and ETFs tradeable 24/7 on blockchain rails; the project was acquired by Kraken in January 2026. Matt, the operations lead for BD, discusses how XSTOCKS has already exceeded $25 billion in total volume with nearly 100,000 wallets holding tokens, positioning the platform to capture institutional demand for programmable, composable equity exposure outside traditional market hours.

topics.text: Matt joined XSTOCKS 8 months ago as a business development operations lead after 5 years in crypto, initially building and selling a community in Italy before working in DeFi.
The XSTOCKS team is approximately 40-50 people across business development, marketing, and development, described by Matt as 'too lean.'

Kraken acquired XSTOCKS in the first few days of January 2026, combining it with Bakkt to consolidate the company's market lead and provide more resources for on-chain trading and institutional offerings.

XSTOCKS are one-to-one digital representations of underlying stocks that are freely tradeable on-chain, can be sent between wallets, and inherit DeFi features like composability—users can deposit them in lending protocols like Camino to earn yield or borrow against them.

XSTOCKS now has over 90,000 addresses holding tokens with total volume exceeding $25 billion, UAM (user assets managed) at $270 million, DEX volume at nearly $400 million, and on-chain transaction volume over $4 billion.

XSTOCKS operates an 'atomic and momentum redemption engine' allowing users to swap up to $1 million per transaction with low spreads on platforms like Jupiter, 1inch Fusion, and CoW Swap, accessing tradfi liquidity to mint new tokens based on market demand.

XSTOCKS currently focuses only on tokenizing US-listed securities including stocks, gold ETFs, palladium, silver, and indexes like the S&P 500; private equity is not a focus due to liquidity and regulatory concerns.

XSTOCKS plans to release hundreds of new tokens across on-chain rails and centralized exchanges soon, integrate with additional major blockchains, and unlock new DeFi use cases for tokenized equities.

jo_ltApSv6U.tldr: Merge is a platform connecting developers to paid bounties on open-source and closed-source projects, positioning itself as an "Uber for engineers" where the best solution gets paid. Founders Damien and Isaac have won nine consecutive hackathons and are bootstrapped but exploring fundraising; the most striking claim is an $8.8 trillion TAM in open-source software alone.

topics.text: Damien's background: AWS data infrastructure engineer, then John Deere, then Accenture; won nine consecutive hackathons including OpenAI's exclusive hackathon in NYC.

Core business model: open-source maintainers set bounties on issues, developers submit solutions, only the merged PR gets paid; also serves closed-source startups as an alternative to hiring full-time engineers.
For non-technical founders: project managers scope out the full project, estimate costs, match budget; founders reach out directly or through accelerator partnerships to set up calls.
Revenue model: takes 10-20% of every successfully merged bounty; premium tier features include repository health analytics, code quality analysis, and project management tools.
Open-source TAM cited as $8.8 trillion as of 2025 from an HBS report; software runs everything including Google and Amazon which are built on open-source.
Token launched through EZA Kickstart; early contributors and token holders get exclusive access to events; founders exploring revenue-sharing and discounts tied to token holders.

SG2w2KpuKuk.tldr: BIT10 is a crypto index fund platform offering market-cap-weighted exposure to the top 10 cryptocurrencies with daily rebalancing, built by two developers who pivot frequently and target emerging markets like Nigeria where traditional finance access is limited. The founder claims a 10-year backtest shows the top 10 crypto index outperforms both Bitcoin and the S&P 500 over the past 5 years.

topics.text: BIT10 began as an index fund for ordinals and runes at a Stacks hackathon in October 2023, then pivoted to cross-chain index funds after the Bitcoin market downturn.
A 10-year backtest shows the top 10 market-cap-weighted cryptocurrency index beats Bitcoin, the S&P 500, and Ethereum over the past 5 years.
BIT10 uses native assets rather than wrapped tokens and built on Internet Computer Protocol layer zero infrastructure to enable minting on Solana, Binance Smart Chain, Base, and Ethereum.
User interviews revealed the majority of early adopters were from Nigeria, where currency inflation drove demand for alternative investments.
Users mint tokens by depositing stablecoins on BIT10's website, which are used to buy the top 10 cryptocurrencies stored in 10 separate wallets and rebalanced daily at 11 a.m. GMT.
BIT10 maintains 110% collateralization as a buffer for black swan events, with the shortfall only occurring if Ethereum went to zero.
Revenue comes from a 5% transaction fee currently, dropping to 0.1% after launching a $10 subscription service offering 2-3% cashback and raffle entries.
Roadmap includes BIT10 Soul (top 10 Solana tokens), top 10 Base tokens, and RWA index funds, with a validation token on Easier Kickstarter on Solana.

The new mainnet version achieved 2x growth in the last 30 days, with the founder motivated by giving people in emerging economies access to index investing after his uncle in Afghanistan couldn't access the S&P 500 through traditional channels.

aZ2WVZNG-_s.tldr: Synapse is a user-owned physiological data platform that bridges individual athletes and researchers by aggregating wearable data (Apple Watch, Garmin, Whoop) while keeping data stored with users, not on Synapse servers; founder Jackson is both a medical/neuroscience PhD student and Ironman athlete, giving him unique perspective on the fragmentation problem he's solving. The striking claim: no data is stored or sold by Synapse—only permissions are tracked on blockchain—making it fundamentally different from 23andMe's model.

topics.text: Jackson is a medical student and PhD student in neuroscience at London and Oxford, training as a neurosurgeon, with research experience at Harvard and UCSF.

The core problem: individuals generate massive physiological data from wearables but don't own it; researchers need real-world data but can't access it; wearable and medical data are fragmented across platforms.

Synapse MVP focuses on three functions: aggregation of wearable data from Apple Watch, Garmin, Whoop into one dashboard; visibility of that data; and user control over permissioned sharing with researchers or studies.
No data is stored by Synapse or published on blockchain; only access permissions are tracked on a decentralized system, with individuals retaining full control and key ownership of their actual data.

Target users are three groups: athletes generating physiological data, anyone willing to contribute data to science, and researchers needing real-world datasets; expands to clinical trials and personalized medicine.

Genome-wide association studies analyzing data from a million people are powerful; Synapse aims to enable similar population-scale research by aggregating physiological data, addressing science's limitation of scale.
Synapse is a mission-driven for-profit company with strong ethical rails, not a nonprofit; balanced approach where pure nonprofit limits scale and pure profit loses user trust.

PvARxtzKzog.tldr: Pact is an AI-powered context aggregation tool for software agencies that collects client briefs, emails, Slack messages, and recordings into a unified knowledge base that developers can query to access the client's vision. Founded by Mary and Akil, the project claims that 40% of client requirements are lost in translation between agency owners and developers, and aims to solve this by making client context searchable and always up-to-date.

topics.text: The founders met at an EA hackathon in October 2025 and initially built blockchain-based escrow for software outsourcing, but pivoted when they realized the core problem was capturing incomplete client briefs.

In pre-AI software agencies, value came from code quality and technical judgment; post-AI, the main value shift is toward client understanding, as AI automates the programmer's tasks while leaving strategic vision unchanged.
The broken telephone problem: only 60% of a client's original vision reaches developers, resulting in 40% of requirements being misinterpreted, changed, or lost before implementation.

Pact ingests fragmented client vision from emails, Slack, Notion, and recordings, then unifies it so developers can ask questions like 'what did the client mean by clean?' and receive synthesized answers cited to source materials.

Pact combines automatic multi-source ingestion with client project knowledge focus, positioning itself in a competitive landscape where other tools either do company knowledge (static documents) or handle client knowledge but manually.
The addressable market for service agencies is $1.22 trillion by 2030, with 66% having fewer than 10 employees and no dedicated knowledge management software.
Revenue model is a flat monthly fee per agency, allowing all developers on a team to access the unified client context regardless of team size.
Currently bootstrapped with an ECA grant; the team plans to build with their first customer over the coming weeks, then defer deep token economics planning to the second half of the year.

Long-term vision extends beyond software agencies to any industry where execution and human intent are separated, positioning Pact as foundational infrastructure for a future with more non-technical founders outsourcing technical work.

TSC985j0dwY.tldr: Cupid TV is building a live-streamed prediction market platform that combines dating show formats with betting, where viewers can vote on outcomes while predictors bet on results, settling markets in minutes rather than months. Founders Pram and Lucas discuss their evolution from viral in-person dating shows at 20+ universities to a B2B2C platform launching April 17th, claiming the market could reach billions in volume and positioning themselves as 'the Twitch for prediction markets.'

topics.text: Pram designed regulatory frameworks for online gaming content for several years; Lucas was an aerospace engineer who led teams and helped six startups before joining to build Cupid TV.
Started as a comedy dating show traveling universities; first show in Texas took 6 months to sell out, then expanded to 21+ universities with 15,000 in-person attendees and 150 million online views.
Love Island's 2025 app increased watched minutes from 2-3 billion to 18 billion by letting viewers influence outcomes; Cupid TV applies this engagement model to live streaming prediction markets.
Two-sided system: voters eliminate contestants (like Love Island), predictors bet on who gets eliminated; betting lines move in real-time as votes come in, markets settle in 5-10 minutes.
Launching V2 builder tool: creators can design custom show formats with granular control over stages, role assignment, questions, voting, and elimination logic without manual coding.
TAM is 8.4 billion based on global annual revenue from live social formats; Kalshi and Polymarket do over a billion in transaction volume every few weeks.

Launch strategy: 20,000 people from in-person shows get platform access; Zach Justice hosting 1,000-person event at UT Austin on April 17th to generate initial volume; expanding to 90 universities by fall.

NgL-Qg4RPog.tldr: Repo is a decentralized network of data marketplaces using prediction markets to crowdsource and validate AI training data, with V2 launching in 2 days. Founder RJ discusses how agents and zero-human companies will autonomously purchase data from Repo's infrastructure, and reveals the project has raised 8 figures from Bolts Capital.

topics.text: Repo builds AI on-chain through a network of data markets where AI agents autonomously consume and purchase data, differentiating from Bittensor's subnet model.
V2 introduces 'data nets' with 20k Repo entry fee: 10% burnt, 40% to emissions pool, 50% locked in creator custody and returned if they shut down.
Repo's prediction market approach uses three standardized metrics across all data nets: voter volume, revenue from publishers, and staking, enabling fair redistribution of incentive pools.
EV off metric measures data quality using total voter volume and unique voters to provide confidence intervals on dataset quality before purchase.
Spicenet partnership will use Repo to crowdsource community feedback on which DeFi apps to integrate their D5 brokerage technology into.
Zero-human companies need feedback loops to learn from mistakes; Repo provides this through prediction markets where evaluators assess agent decisions in real-time.
Opinion contracts on Repo allow real-time assessment of quality for any content stream, different from event contracts on Kalshi or Polymarket.
Relocking rate currently around 60% with users locking for one-week minimums; 946 community locks on-chain with analytics dashboard launching soon.
Repo has no emissions; incentives funded by 40% of data net creation fees, making the network deflationary through burn mechanisms and publisher fees.

uPEdYEmBvgc.tldr: Robot Money is an agentic treasury infrastructure protocol where AI agents vote their own tokens into asset allocations, designed by Lex, an ex-ConsenSys and MetaMask developer with 20 years in investment management and fintech. The surprising core mechanic: agents must hold and vote ROBOT tokens to get their own tokens into the vault's allocation—turning it into Curve-style bribe wars between machines rather than people.

topics.text: Founder Lex has 20 years experience: started a robo-advisor company in 2009 before Wealthfront, then worked on DeFi at ConsenSys co-leading 80 developers, and designed the MetaMask token.
The token design draws from three successful precedents: Boto (token holders vote on art generation), OlympusDAO (protocol-owned liquidity), and Curve (bribe wars to incentivize liquidity pools).

Three-part product: machine-to-machine treasury management for AI agents, agent-to-agent capital distribution without person-to-person transactions, and agents must hold Robot Money and vote weekly or monthly to get their own tokens into the vault allocation.
The project is run as a creative, AI-first experiment with automation, not as a traditional fintech company; marketing site has 50,000 pages designed for robots to read, not humans.

MVP vault will initially support stablecoins and governance-selected agent tokens, with plans to add revenue-generating liquid tokens, protocol tokens, and equity exposure through platforms like Hyperliquid.

Vault mechanics are complex from security perspective: AI agents must ask other AI agents for transaction permissions on third-party wallets, receive receipt tokens, and get 4-5 initial launch partners including machine economy agentic AI players.

Revenue model: 1-2% asset management fee on AUM, not fees on yield generated; Lex positions himself as asset allocator selecting vault components, not fund manufacturer, leaving yield fees to underlying protocols like Giza or MakerDAO.
Token has single usage: voting; Lex rejects complex token mechanics, citing Ethereum's gas token as the only good model, and notes most DeFi tokens lack utility despite governance claims.

GnP-LlIIaFw.tldr: P2P is a decentralized peer-to-peer stablecoin on/off-ramp protocol for emerging markets, founded by Sheldon (formerly of a cloud kitchen business in India). The founder claims the protocol can settle transactions in 60-90 seconds using local payment rails like UPI and Pix, and projects reaching $500 million monthly volume within 18 months from a current $4.5-5 million monthly run rate across 23,000 users in four countries.

topics.text: Founder background: Sheldon attended IIT Madras, dropped out, scaled a cloud kitchen business to 14 locations in India with minimal outside funding before exiting to a food delivery network.

Core product: P2P is a decentralized settlement network using local payment rails (UPI in India, Pix in Brazil, CURIS in Indonesia, Mercado Pago in Argentina) to enable USDC on/off-ramps via QR code scans by P2P merchants.
Growth metrics: 23,000 users across India (50% of volume), Brazil (35%), Argentina (12%), and Indonesia; 27% month-on-month growth from $100k to $4.5 million monthly volume; $567k annualized revenue.
Investor backing: Reclaim Protocol invested $80k for 3.5% at $2.3m FDV; Alliance invested $350k for 4.66% at $7.5m FDV; Multicoin Capital at $15m FDV; Coinbase at $19.5m FDV.
Liquidity providers: 500 LPs across the globe, mostly former users (women, college students, Uber drivers); average monthly returns benchmarked at $110 in India and $100 in Brazil.
Latin America expansion: Venezuela and Mexico went live last week; Venezuela already doing $1k daily volume without capital investment; only two people managing Brazil and LATAM expansion.

Go-to-market strategy: Uses 'circles of trust' model where community members can launch liquidity circles in new countries via grants and transaction incentives; identifies target markets by analyzing Binance P2P liquidity provider listings.

5VcBHsRUVjY.tldr: SOAR, a tokenized equities platform, is launching V2 in 4-6 weeks focused on Web2 assets and private company secondaries rather than early-stage crypto tokens. Founder Tom explains why the project pivoted from ICO launches to building better trading infrastructure and distribution, arguing that tokenization's real value lies in unlocking illiquid private venture markets through secondary transactions rather than trying to convert crypto traders into long-term holders.

topics.text: SEC regulation on equities on chain requires more rigid compliance and legal guidelines rather than the previous 'wild west' approach to token launches.
Crypto markets lack long-term patient capital; most participants are short-term traders, so tokenized assets need institutional backing like VCs and private equity to sustain price appreciation.
SOAR V2 launching in 4-6 weeks with revamped product focused on Web2 assets, tokenized equities, and better trading infrastructure rather than ICOs and bonding curves.

Founder is targeting secondaries market where seed funds and young founders can cash out equity, and acquisition of assets through SPVs to bring them on-chain without requiring immediate company permission.
AMMs aren't optimal for tokenized equities; order books are more favorable, and distribution should focus on Web2-familiar assets that retail traders want to speculate on.

estQmwc1G0w.tldr: Maiat is a trust oracle for AI agents that scores and verifies agent interactions through on-chain data and peer reviews. Co-founders Evan and Jerry, college students, launched the project at ETH Denver after pivoting from a three-year-old restaurant review concept; they've attracted 31,000+ registered agents, 1,000 queries, and raised $100K in revenue during their Virtuals 60-day launch phase, and the most surprising element is their integration into the emerging ERC-8183 standard for AI agent evaluation.

topics.text: The founders previously built True Critic, a solution to verify reviews on-chain, but pivoted after realizing the industry was too early for their restaurant receipts use case.
Maiat solves trust between AI agents by providing on-chain scores: agents can query the oracle before interacting with other agents to determine if they are legitimate or fraudulent.
The differentiation from competitors is a peer review layer where agents leave verified reviews after interacting with other agents, creating a consensus database of agent trustworthiness.
The project has 31,743 registered agents, 104 unique API callers, and approximately 1,000 queries since launching two weeks prior with no marketing budget spent.
ERC-8183 is a standard for AI agent evaluation with three roles—client, provider, and evaluator—where Maiat acts as the evaluator to assess job completion quality and agent reputation.
Users who leave reviews receive Scarab tokens, an arcade token separate from the Maiat token; staking is required before submitting a review to verify the reviewer actually had the transaction.
The Maiat token launched through Virtuals 60-day framework, raising $100K revenue; if the project commits, the revenue is retained; if not, it's refunded to holders.

iALVMVW4dok.tldr: Meteora DLMM Masterclass with CrimeXBT and HeavyMetalCook teaches dynamic liquidity market-making on Solana, focusing on how to earn fees by providing liquidity across different price ranges rather than trading directionally. The hosts demonstrate practical strategies like bid-ask positioning and single-sided liquidity provisioning, with CrimeXBT sharing how he turned $1 SOL into $186 SOL using these techniques.

topics.text: The shift from trading mentality to LP mentality: you profit from fees and price ranging, not from buy-low-sell-high directional trading.
AMM vs CLMM vs DLMM: traditional AMMs spread liquidity 0 to infinity, CLMMs concentrate it in a price range, and DLMMs allow you to shape liquidity to match your strategy.
Four DLMM strategies: spot (even distribution), curve (tight concentrated range), bid-ask (heavy at lows for DCA), and combinations of these to match token behavior.
One-sided liquidity advantage: you can deposit only SOL without buying the token upfront, reducing capital risk on meme coins that typically dump.
Impermanent loss explained: as price moves down your range, SOL converts to token and loses value; your goal is to earn enough fees to offset that loss and stay profitable.
Practical bid-ask example on Gerald token: entered 10 SOL at 969K, price dumped to 180K, collected fees both ways as price bounced, exited at 1.8 SOL profit despite mid-position drawdown.
Bid-ask flip strategy: after collecting fees on the dump, withdraw and reposition to sell the bulk at higher prices on the way up, then collect fees during the recovery.
Volume is king: without trading volume, there are no fees; higher volatility and market cap affect whether to use high fee pools (5-10% for meme coins) or low fee pools (0.2% for established tokens).
Dynamic fee feature: Meteora automatically increases fees on highly volatile pools, so a 2% pool can trigger 5-10% fees during sharp price movements.
Tools for finding volume: Meteora's discover page sorts by fees and volume to identify the hottest runners; met.io terminal shows trending tokens and existing pool options.

7u2wtDgtqfA.tldr: Clude is an AI memory layer that stores and retrieves agent memories using a human brain-inspired architecture, reducing hallucinations to 2% and query costs to ~1 cent versus $6–12 with GPT-4. Founder Saps discusses the $33 billion TAM by 2030, 5,000 downloads since January launch, and plans for a knowledge marketplace where agents can trade memory packs.

topics.text: Context windows are short-term memory for AI; increasing them to a million tokens doesn't solve information loss during memory compaction.
Clude segments memories into episodic, semantic, procedural, and self-model categories, scores them by importance, and applies decay to filter out noise.
Big tech companies charge by tokens, incentivizing larger context windows; Clude filters relevant memories before querying, reducing token usage from 200,000 to 2,000 per query.
Clude hashes memories with SHA-256 and stores proofs on Solana for verifiable, tamper-proof records of why agents made specific decisions.
5,000 downloads since January launch with 560 active users; primary use case is trading agents on Polymarket learning from past market patterns.
Planned knowledge marketplace where agents can share and trade memory packs—experiences, mistakes, and adjusted strategies—using Clude token.
Hallucination rate of 2% versus 15% for competitors; omission rate of 30% as tradeoff for avoiding false information in high-stakes trading.
Retrieval accuracy of 88% at one-tenth the cost of competitors by filtering to 10–20 relevant nodes instead of processing all 200,000 tokens.

0fAltAeK3co.tldr: Instaclaw, founded by Cooper, is an AI agent deployment platform that raised $85k in trading fees and now has 327 active agents earning autonomously. The most striking development: one agent made $7k in two weeks by trading on prediction markets and selling services, then tokenized itself on Virtuals without explicit human instruction.

topics.text: Instaclaw raised $85,000 through token trading fees on Virtuals, which the founder plans to deploy into Ethereum and Worldcoin as treasury assets.
Worldcoin provides proof of humanity verification without KYC, which Instaclaw integrates to tie every deployed agent to a real human for trust and preventing spam.
Instaclaw received grants from the Worldcoin Foundation and was the first to implement agent kit; deeper integrations are planned including automatic agent deployment for World app users.
One Instaclaw agent tokenized itself on Virtuals, listed services on the AGDP marketplace, and earned approximately $7,000 in under two weeks.
