Instaclaw has 22-23 custom-built skills including Shopify e-commerce, Solana DeFi trading, Poly Market prediction trading, Gumroad freelancing, and video generation.
The platform has 25k monthly recurring revenue, 327 active deployed agents, and daily active users doubling every single day.
Pricing starts at $29/month base plan with limited autonomy; agents need higher tiers to run fully autonomous 24/7 operations.

Clawancer is an Upwork-style marketplace for agents to trade services and build onchain reputation; planned integration with World's 38 million verified humans to post bounties for physical-world tasks agents cannot complete.
Future roadmap includes a public-facing arena where agents trade each other's tokens based on reputation scores, and automatic tokenization of agents upon deployment through Instaclaw.

ygf3fueoTy8.tldr: Perch is an application layer for agentic commerce that lets users and AI agents buy physical products from Amazon and Shopify using stablecoins without KYC, starting in the US. Founders Arthur and Thiago discuss how their platform went viral after Jeremy Lerner tweeted about it, and they're now focused on global expansion and integrating X402 protocols for agent self-improvement.

topics.text: Arthur is the CEO of Perch, a software engineer for 7 years who met co-founder Thiago at SAP; both entered crypto during the 2024 AI agent boom and joined Blorm before launching Perch.
Perch positions itself in the application layer of agentic commerce, not infrastructure, comparing itself to how Stripe didn't build Shopify and Visa didn't build Amazon.

Users can chat with Perch to describe purchase intent, and it compares Amazon and Shopify products by metadata and reviews; alternatively, they can use quick-buy by pasting a URL and paying with USDC for cashback in Perch tokens.
Perch Vault is a marketplace for AI agents to buy digital products like skills, personas, and knowledge packs to configure and upgrade their capabilities, launched 2 days before this episode.
Purchases require only an email, shipping address, and USDC—no credit card or KYC—and items arrive in 2-3 days; currently US-only through Shopify and Amazon partnerships.
Tier-based cashback rewards coming soon where staking more Perch tokens yields higher cashback rates; 35% of Perch supply is held by the team for cashback, partnerships, and scaling.

Perch is the first certified skill in Lobster Cash, an initiative powered by Circle and Visa via Crossmint, enabling agents with wallets to make purchases without exposing sensitive payment information.

Hky6_7WLF1k.tldr: Davey, founder of $BLOXX, won $250k from the Pump Build public hackathon and is building an AI-assisted game studio launchpad for Roblox developers. He worked on Lord of the Rings Online and has 30 years of game development experience. The most surprising element: he's also launching Trust Connect, a plugin to detect child predators in Roblox through chat analysis and behavior scoring across games.

topics.text: Pump Fund organization backing hackathon winners based on business potential, not followers or token market cap.
Roblox hard no on crypto: they prohibit external links and token promotions to protect children, so BLOXX provides data-only informational connector showing live trades and market caps.
Trust Connect plugin detects predatory behavior through chat monitoring and cross-game pattern analysis, flagging users with danger icons or allowing developer removal.

Founder previously ran flash game publishing business with 60-70 million monthly visitors, worked at Turbine Games on Lord of the Rings Online, and built interactive cinema data platform for movie studios.
Game Launchpad platform lets solo developers build games using customized AI agents (called allies) trained on specific skills that learn from task ratings and game success metrics.
AI agents write Lua code for Roblox games, handle social media strategy, coordinate collabs, plan holiday events, and can be rented or enlisted from a marketplace as experienced characters.
BLOXX token used as discount mechanism and bonus payment for AI agents; fiat credit packs also available with token holders getting varying discount levels.
Raising additional funds beyond $250k hackathon prize to build 2,000-3,000 item template library of animations, VFX, game templates, and maps from Roblox community creators.
Game Launchpad v1 launches in early April 2024; currently in experimentation phase with older SaaS version being replaced by new team-based AI model.
AI agents expansion planned beyond Roblox to other game engines, announced as MCG exclusive.

wOhwEX3hpPg.tldr: Dominion is a tokenized silver platform offering 8-10% yields paid in silver, backed by physical metal held on their balance sheet. Founder Mark discusses how they're partnering with bullion dealers to bring yield to traditional silver buyers, while pursuing a TSX Venture listing in Canada with regulatory support from the Ontario Securities Commission—and they're currently raising $500K at a $5M pre-money valuation.

topics.text: Founder previously worked at Swissborg exchange and encountered tokenized RWA projects before launching Dominion as a solo founder.

Target audiences: crypto users seeking yield beyond inflation, and silver buyers who want 24/7 liquidity, tradability, and collateral use without physical storage, insurance, or slow valuation processes.

Revenue model: Dominion buys and holds physical silver on balance sheet, generates fees from DeFi trading, price pegging, borrowing/lending, and DEX usage; all fees buy more silver which backs yield tokens distributed to locked-up token holders.

Bullion dealer partnerships: customers still buy via credit card and receive digital receipts, but dealers plug into Dominion's backend to offer yield instead of metal leasing, avoiding direct wallet/MetaMask requirements.
Tokenized gold market is $4.5 billion versus tokenized silver at $350 million with only one competitor; Dominion chose silver because it's a mining byproduct setting up a 5-7 year supply squeeze.

Raising $500K at $4.5M pre-money valuation ($5M post-money) via SAFE on Fairclub; equity raise with no separate governance token, aiming for TSX Venture listing later in 2024 via reverse takeover shell merger.

eiPMQ4zHUsY.tldr: Impulser, led by Roman, is commercializing contactless power transfer technology through an exclusive partnership with Powercast (which has sold 30 million units in 24 months). The most surprising claim: Impulser aims to sell millions of units globally in the first 12 months and is in conversations with a $140 billion company that could result in tens to hundreds of millions of units sold within three years.

topics.text: Impulser makes three types of contactless power transfer: radio frequency for IoT devices under 1 watt, magnetic resonance up to 20 watts over distance, and laser power transfer for moving vehicles like drones.

From one trade show alone, Impulser generated 120 potential sales leads and is in conversations with a maritime distributor servicing 3,000-4,000 ships and oil rigs to be their exclusive global distributor.

KIRL8zkqD6M.tldr: Dapital is a social brokerage for on-chain assets that rewards creators when followers trade based on their investment theses, combining Robinhood-style UX with a thesis-sharing model where creators earn a portion of trading volume fees. Founder Raphael, formerly a quant developer at Optiver, explains how the platform differs from copy-trading competitors by letting creators maintain privacy and exit positions without rugging followers, and plans to expand beyond Solana to include equities, RWAs, and cross-chain assets.

topics.text: Founder Raphael worked as a quant developer at Optiver on HFT futures and equities; co-founder came from Instagram.
Creators earn a portion of trading volume fees when users trade based on their published theses or watchlists.
Watchlist feature allows users to follow friends' curated lists and earn rewards if they trade off those lists, providing privacy compared to full wallet exposure.
The algorithm ranks posts based on financial performance rather than engagement metrics, promoting posts that generate alpha.
Currently in private beta on Solana; expanding to BNB Chain, Hyperliquid, and RWA providers like Tessera and pre-stocks for equities access.
Positioned for non-crypto audiences and everyday consumers, not just crypto natives, with plans for an ACH on-ramp and debit card via Bridge.
Go-to-market strategy focuses on recruiting creator KOLs with angel-round equity alignment rather than token incentives.
Roadmap includes cross-chain support, Asia expansion via teams in Korea and Hong Kong, yield products, and curation of asset discovery.
Waitlist available at dapital.xyz; currently focused on private beta with creators rather than public launch, no announced release date.

axB09BPqVNM.tldr: Veilbank is a privacy-focused neobank offering unified banking infrastructure (fiat accounts, crypto cards, DeFi tools, payment processing) for high-net-worth individuals and businesses, with a Laos banking partner that doesn't report to home jurisdictions. Founder Kane claims 20,000 on waitlist, $50-70M in monthly processing deals closing, and projects $300-500K monthly profit, targeting debanked populations and high-risk businesses rather than crypto natives.

topics.text: Veilbank provides unified financial operating system combining crypto cards, fiat/crypto bank accounts, DeFi tools (swaps, bridges, yields, borrowing/lending), and payment processing on a single non-custodial platform.
Banking partner is in Laos, one of few jurisdictions not required to report user information back to home countries, enabling privacy functions within compliance.

Targeting strategy focuses 70% on businesses (casinos, trading platforms, forex brokerages, e-commerce) with $30B TAM needing debanked solutions, and 30% direct-to-consumer including debanked Russians and Ukrainians.
Closing three payment processing deals generating $50-70M monthly volume: two casinos and one nutraceutical/e-commerce client, earning 1-1.5% revenue share on total volume.
Fee structure includes 1% on swaps, 1% on bridges, 3% deposit fee including fiat conversion, monthly card maintenance fees, and 1-3% on payment processing volume.
Laos bank partnership includes uncapped insurance up to 70% of fiat balance backed by central bank of Laos, compared to $250K FDIC coverage in America.

CHMtln0S6n0.tldr: GoSave is a travel rewards platform that gives users cash-backed points from hotel bookings, redeemable for Amazon purchases, charity donations, or future travel. CEO Anthony and CTO Adrian explain how they partner with over 500,000 hotels and 45,000 nonprofits to return ~18% of booking commissions to users—compared to the 5-6% offered by Expedia and Priceline—while planning eventual tokenization once they build their community.

topics.text: Anthony's background: worked in finance at Merrill Lynch and Raymond James with high-net-worth clients, then became entrepreneur 6 years ago; met co-founders through a non-profit board 6 years ago.
Core model: users earn points on hotel bookings backed by cash, redeemable on Amazon, for travel discounts, or donated to 45,000+ partner nonprofits and organizations.
Points system: 100 points equals approximately $1 in cash value; $207 hotel stay yields 18,000 points (~$180 value); points don't expire and compound.
Hotel network: API relationships with over 500,000 hotels globally, including partnerships with Expedia and Priceline; offers closed user group (CUG) rates 5-10% cheaper than public bookings.

Competitive advantage: 18% average commissions from hotels versus 5-6% from competitors like Expedia and Priceline; Ted on team worked 25 years in rewards space, was president of Dosh ($300 million exit).
Fundraising: targeting $1.5 million seed raise at $15 million valuation; already bootstrapped $400,000; team currently unpaid; raises planned for 12-18 month runway.

Community reach: 1.6 million business owners in pipeline for corporate booking programs; email and SMS lists 'into the millions' of opted-in users; John co-founder has 100,000+ insurance agents network.
Investor backing: co-founder of Tinder and co-founder of Acorns app on cap table.
Token roadmap: tokenization delayed pending market improvement; plans to follow model of successful projects like Uniswap by building community and utility first.
Launch timeline: beta testing with 30-45 people over next 30 days; public launch targeted within 30-60 days; social media team being brought on in coming weeks.

VYdyUjX9x3w.tldr: GSD 2.0 is a fully autonomous AI coding agent built on the open-source Piper framework that can run for 24 hours unattended, now with Stripe integration for monetization and a UI for non-technical users. Founder Lex explains how the tool's power comes from its opinionated system prompts and custom tools rather than just the underlying model, and plans to monetize through a subscription UI while keeping the GitHub repo open-source—GSD already has 28k stars and is seeing rapid adoption.

topics.text: Bags 100k challenge: 50k to developers and 50k to token holders via USDC airdrop, with eligibility requiring organic launch on Bags, no bots or wash trading.
GSD 1.0 achieved 27.5k GitHub stars and 150k monthly downloads but was limited by Claude's codebase architecture, prompting a rebuild from scratch.
GSD 2.0 uses Piper, an open-source coding agent library that allows any model and custom extensions, solving the observability and autonomy constraints of Claude Code.
The autonomous agent ran for 9 hours straight building multiple projects, with new Slack and Discord notifications allowing users to check progress remotely.
GSD built an automated Stripe-to-token buyback system: card payments are processed through Stripe, profits accumulate in a wallet, then automatically swap to the token and burn it above thresholds.
Monetization strategy: charge non-crypto users $20–$200 monthly for a beautiful UI, with 50% of profits going to token holders through burns or treasury allocation.

Token-funded development: approximately $150–160k in SOL has funded full-time work, marketing via X posts, and model API costs; host noted the fee burn increases trading volumes and benefits other Bags apps.

GSD's core power comes from opinionated system prompts and custom tools, not just the underlying model; the agent must verify tasks rather than ask humans, with a browser tool and newly shipped Mac control via Xcode.

Planning redesigned from horizontal phases to vertical slices: each slice like 'authentication' touches database, API, and frontend, ensuring the agent can verify complete user-facing features end-to-end.
Automatic context clearing between slices prevents token bloat and context rot, enabling long-running autonomous sessions without degradation.

kb-NdM2kWeI.tldr: Hubs is a 3D social platform for communities and content creators positioned as a lightweight, accessible alternative to corporate metaverses like Meta's offering. Founder Russ discusses how 25K zones with integrated monetization through ticketing and rental systems are designed to achieve mainstream adoption by solving problems that Decentraland and others faced.

topics.text: Bags 100k challenge: 50k to developers for growth and 50k to token holders via USDC airdrop, with requirements for organic growth and verified creator wallets.
Founder inspired to launch $HUBZZ token after developer Theo unexpectedly raised 20k on Pump Fund in under a week, shifting founder's perspective on token mechanics.
Hubs described as lightweight 3D metaverse designed for casual hangouts with Discord in background, supporting hot-swap between desktop, mobile, and VR modes.
Zone-based model: 25k per zone with monetization built in through ticketing, subspace sales, and rental systems to help recoup initial investment.
Economy uses locked tokens for credits at 64:1 ratio, 4% off-ramp fee when cashing out, no transaction fees within ecosystem.
Token holders can burn $HUBZZ for NFT that grants automated dividends; early in-world assets gain value through custom characters and UGC.
Founder seeking 1.5 million for 12-14 months runway with fully stacked team, projecting revenue between months 6-8 from zone commitments.
Hubs applied to Bags 4 million hackathon; founder states they have turned down more investment opportunities than most would believe.

inPjenktBcw.tldr: Shaw creates open-source AI agent infrastructure and training environments through games like Babylon and Hyperscape, funded by token fees from community launches. The surprising insight: agents can't be trusted in the real world without training data, so Shaw builds synthetic crypto versions where agents learn by scamming and trading each other before deployment.

topics.text: Bags 100k challenge: 50k to coin developer, 50k USDC airdrop to token holders, requiring organic growth, verifiable creator wallet, no bots or wash trading.

The Lobstar agent treasury incident: an agent gave away a quarter million dollars when asked to help someone's uncle with cancer, demonstrating agents trained on helpful chat need adversarial training before real-world deployment.
Babylon game: agents on a fake version of X scrolling for alpha, entering group chats, making leverage trades and prediction bets, generating training data via reinforcement learning.
Open-source funding model: fees from community-launched tokens fund developer salaries and contributions; Shaw treats social capital as more valuable than financial capital.
Token economics require 90-95% team supply control for holders to win; three-week speculation timelines in crypto prevent building the year-long projects needed to generate real value.
Hyperscape: five-minute prediction markets where dgens gamble on AI agent duels (GPT-5 vs Claude Sonnet), funding expensive model training at thousand dollars per day.
Ethos protocol: enables longing and shorting people's social reputation, creating synthetic assets with no underlying spot market.
DevShaw's formula for winning: combine high-IQ technical ideas with low-IQ viral memetics; ship fast, delete unsexy features, add 'waifu,' then iterate.
Milady app launching: free open-source agent companion with advanced mode, integrating Hyperscape Duel Arena and Babylon games, betting available through prediction markets.

ciuM5aJsxBo.tldr: Primis Protocol is a pricing layer for AI compute that abstracts fragmented markets and enables builders to lock in predictable costs. The founder previously created Bully, a viral AI agent, and discusses why compute pricing needs hedging mechanisms similar to commodity futures—allowing capital providers to earn yield while subsidizing cheaper compute access for builders.

topics.text: 100k bags challenge: 50k to coin developers, 50k to token holders via USDC airdrop; eligibility requires launch on bags, organic growth only, verifiable creator wallet.
Bully token reached $260 million market cap; generated 50,000 followers on X and 10 million TikTok views but failed to deliver on promised Dolon AI agent infrastructure.

Primis Protocol is a pricing layer for AI compute: routing workloads to optimal providers, standardizing pricing across fragmented markets, and transferring price volatility risk to capital providers.

Base yield on Solana is 6.63%; Primis gives capital providers 4% and uses 2.6% for compute subsidization; at $10 million compute volume with 10% fee ($1M revenue), 50% ($500k) goes to capital pools boosting yields to 9-11%.
$324k ARR currently from Primis agents (open-source Claude wrapper deployed on Primis); launched on 100,000-person waitlist from failed Dolon project; closed beta running with five teams.
Primis token tokenomics: profits used to buy back and add liquidity to token; flywheel designed to give token holders exposure to company upside instead of just governance voting.

Roadmap: launching mobile apps for Solana Mobile and other phones for one-click agent deployment; integrating more skills including GSD; open beta for compute side coming soon from closed beta with positive early results.

Builders lock in compute price through three-click process: select compute type, buy, submit workload; price guaranteed throughout usage period; Primis handles routing and provider negotiation invisibly.

bZ6Iq-xrkQ0.tldr: Recap is an AI assistant that lives in Telegram chats to summarize conversations, answer questions, and drive engagement for crypto communities. The founder addresses scam accusations head-on, explaining how 220 communities have integrated the bot in five months and how the project monetizes through Recap Boost ads (0.1 SOL per week to 180,000+ people) with 50% of revenue going to token buybacks and burns.

topics.text: 100k bags challenge: 50k to coin developer for any use, 50k to token holders via USDC airdrop, with eligibility requiring Bags launch, one app use only, organic growth no bots, and verifiable creator wallet.

Recap is an always-on AI in Telegram that recaps chats, answers questions using chat history, translates messages in real-time, drives engagement through games and quizzes, and tracks sentiment and trending topics.

Recap has been installed in over 400 Telegram communities in one month post-tokenization with 180,000+ total audience reach; free tool with premium features requiring 100k token hold at approximately $30.

Recap Boost allows projects to market to 180,000+ people for 0.1 SOL per week, with decentralized community wallets letting any member contribute $1 toward the 0.1 SOL cost instead of requiring the developer to pay.
Token allocation: 10% locked for team on six-month linear unlock, 10% marketing wallet untouched, approximately 260 holders at 500k market cap, with 50% of all ad revenue going to buyback and burn.
Recap is launching from crypto Telegram niche but plans to expand beyond Telegram to Discord and web2, with partnerships already being developed in the NFT space.

Users can request recaps by hashtag with timeframes (#recap 3 hours, #recap 30 days) or interact conversationally (e.g., 'Recap, what have I missed?'), with automatic daily recap being the only automatic posting.

QhohcyVAAdg.tldr: Kled AI, a data collection platform that pays users to upload videos and images for AI training, raised $5.5M from top-tier angels including founders from Whimsical and robotics companies. Founder Avi Patel claims the platform has 300K users uploading 5M pieces of content daily, $35M in signed data contracts with labs, and is targeting $50M ARR this year with plans for a $750M Series A by mid-2025.

topics.text: Fundraising took one month to close after a viral post sparked outreach from Google, Sequoia, and A16Z, with the founder deciding to take multiple smaller investors instead of a single lead to gain more value.
Kled has $35 million in signed data contracts already, including a $20 million robotics contract, with pipeline growing to $50 million in coming weeks.

One robotics client needs household chores videos with two hands visible at all times, requiring Kled to build automated fraud detection systems and ship hardware like chest straps and head straps to users.
Users can purchase hardware upgrades like wrist cameras and head straps through a Kled shop to earn more on specific tasks, similar to upgrading equipment as an Uber driver.
Top earners make $7,200 per month, with Kled planning personalization so tasks are recommended hourly based on users' daily routines.
Kled partnered with WAP, a Tether-backed payments platform, to enable global bank withdrawals in any currency and crypto, plus WAP is onboarding 15 million of its users to Kled.
Kled has 300K users uploading 15-30 images daily on average with top 10% uploading 15,000 pieces per day, generating more data per user than every major social platform combined.
The founder rejected offers from government organizations and Palantir, stating commitment to selling data only to AI labs in non-intrusive ways and refusing surveillance applications.

qS9ddGA9Gzc.tldr: Nookplot, described as a settlement layer for agent coordination, enables AI agents to build trusted identities, discover each other, and collaborate on projects through a decentralized knowledge graph. Founders Kitchen and Base Medical discuss how agents will soon outnumber humans in crypto, the platform's rapid growth from 148 to 2,700+ agents in two weeks, and the vision of Nookplot as infrastructure for an emerging agentic economy—with exclusive announcements including Privy integration and a new GPU marketplace.

topics.text: Nookplot described as a coordination layer solving the problem of siloed agents: providing identity, discovery, communication, economy, and collective intelligence on a decentralized, gasless base chain infrastructure.

Meta acquiring Maltbook shows mainstream tech interest in agent coordination, though Nookplot differentiates by being fully decentralized with reputation earned through public knowledge graph contributions rather than web2 infrastructure.

Base Medical's background: 10+ years in tech focused on human factors and AI applied to product design; worked at Treasure DAO as communications lead from October 2021 to May 2022, growing Twitter from zero to 80,000 followers.

To enable multi-agent coordination beyond one-to-one intent searches, Nookplot measures proportional contribution through a knowledge graph, preventing gamification and fake agent reviews that plague simpler systems.
Nookplot metrics show explosive growth: from 148 agents and 45 projects at launch to 2,700+ agents, nearly 7,000 posts, 100+ projects, and 6,200+ votes in two weeks.

Andrej Karpathy's auto-researcher agent, which self-improves ML models autonomously, now integrates with Nookplot's knowledge graph, allowing agents to publish research and prevent duplicate work while earning reputation and citations.

Privy integration launches this week allowing humans to sign up with email and generate wallets without MetaMask, enabling gasless transactions; humans can hire agents directly and access the platform without ETH.
GPU marketplace launching imminently on Nookplot allows agents and humans to rent GPU compute from each other; agents can rent GPUs to run auto-researcher or other computationally intensive tasks.
Knowledge graph serves as productive asset where agents earn through citation chain: original researcher gets rewarded when others download their work, bundle it, or use it in bounty submissions.

TOFnZt0h39o.tldr: JunoAgent founder Tom discusses his thesis on zero-human companies—fully autonomous AI-run businesses—and Juno's platform for building them. The most striking claim: current AI models are already better at digital work than 99.9% of people, and the real bottleneck isn't compute but human decision-making in the loop.

topics.text: Tom's background: in crypto since 2019, bought BAYC on day two for under £1000 and Ether Rocks, caught the August 2021 spike to $1.3 million, ran Shiny Object Social Club community around AI and automation.
AI-crypto convergence glue: OpenAI's O1 release bridged web2 and web3; agents now self-sustaining via tools like Banker, paying their own inference fees with crypto payment rails.

Zero-human company thesis: AI already outperforms 99.9% of humans at digital work; skip to the end and build autonomous companies starting simple with one agent, one product, then scale with sub-agents.

Two product offerings: Institute for Zero Human Companies ($99/month learning platform) and ZHC.co (managed service where agents autonomously build companies; currently Tom pays token costs, 180 on waitlist).

Human bottleneck, not compute: most productive developers run 20 workflows concurrently; goal is removing humans from the loop so agents self-generate and respond to tasks without constant human input.
Juno tracks 192 countries scoring AI-agent friendliness; concept similar to Stripe Atlas, smaller countries may offer favorable policies to attract zero-human companies, like they did for crypto.

CEO + sub-agent architecture: main agent (Juno) stocks business every 8 hours, assigns 4-10 tasks to specialized sub-agents (developer, marketer, writer, analyst, support), they report back for next cycle.

Token economics: Juno token trades on Banker, generates trading fees daily, funds inference costs via LLM gateway; staking mechanism lets holders credit accounts with inference tokens to fund company-building.

Revenue breakdown: $23K fiat revenue (non-crypto) from Stripe subscriptions; crypto treasury holds $114K in Juno and Worth; five revenue lines: memberships, challenge sponsorships, SaaS ($100/month), managed service ($5K/month), OpenClaw installer directory (yearly).

Juno's moat is technology agnostic: no competition with OpenAI or Anthropic; instead builds community and resources for anyone building autonomous systems, teaches whatever tools work best for zero-human companies.

FBE6w69gTxE.tldr: EasyA is a crypto education platform and hackathon organizer that's launching EasyA Kickstart, a launchpad for idea-stage projects to tokenize and raise capital from their community. Brothers Phil and Dom explain how their pipeline of over a million users and backed projects valued at $11B positions them uniquely, and why they're betting on AI agents and robotics as the next frontier—with the surprising claim that founders should respect their token holders just as much as equity investors.

topics.text: Phil and Dom are brothers from London; Phil studied at Cambridge, Dom at UPenn Wharton; they worked in finance before founding EasyA.
EasyA has hosted hackathons that produced projects now valued at over $11 billion, backed by Y Combinator, Founders Fund, and Sequoia; Cognition AI (Devon) came through their events.
EasyA Kickstart is a permissionless launchpad launching this week allowing founders to tokenize ideas; starts at 3K valuation on a bonding curve.
The pipeline flows from one million EasyA app users learning about blockchains, through in-person hackathons, to Kickstart token launches and a new Solana-focused accelerator program.
EasyA makes money through venture equity stakes in launched startups plus forthcoming onchain products; the EasyA app and hackathons are free to access.
Phil stayed bullish on Solana during 2022-2023 when it hit $7 and had only 69 developers; builders continued building despite the token's low price.
Tokens are positioned as idea coins on a spectrum; founders must respect token holders and traders the same way public company founders respect shareholders.
Projects coming through include a Cambridge grad's smart contract security AI agent, YC startups building stable coin remittances, a phone project, and robotics and AI-integrated hardware.
Meteora's Bedrock structure allows token holders to own shares of an SPV that holds equity in the underlying company, giving real ownership rights.
Phil is most excited about AI agents and robotics; Dom highlights AI tools making developers orders of magnitude more efficient, enabling non-coders to launch projects.

9r8tyuUacfA.tldr: Vesper from Meteora discusses the launch of Dynamic Terminal, a new UI designed to make liquidity provision as intuitive as trading. The platform now has 330,000 addresses and has processed $2.38 billion in volume through its Dynamic Bonding Curve technology; the most striking aspect is Meteora's philosophy that liquidity providers should view fees as earnings rather than costs, fundamentally reframing how people approach on-chain participation.

topics.text: Dynamic Terminal release: a collaboration between Meteora's engineers and the LP army community to make LPing feel like trading by showing all data in one screen with a chart always visible

Feedback on the UI has been mixed; mobile users prefer less expanded views while traders appreciate the trading-like experience; the co-leads Soju and Zen are openly asking for community feedback to improve the product
Apin feature: one-click configurable execution option at top right that lets users quickly enter positions without overthinking, reducing the distance between decision and execution

LP army is thousands strong with 330,000 wallet addresses created on Meteora by January 2026, growing through boot camps, strategy libraries, and one-to-one tutorials led by community members across multiple languages

Dynamic Bonding Curve (DBC) generated $2.38 billion in volume and powered launchpads for real-world companies like Dupe to tokenize on-chain, bringing institutional legitimacy to the tokenization space
DLMM strategy for traders: the Sol-USDC pool pairing acts as a 'volatility money printer' where fees are earned regardless of price direction, positioning LPing as lower-risk than traditional trading
Annual token holder report shows Meteora achieved 40 out of 40 transparency score from Blockworks, demonstrating commitment to detailed business metrics and stakeholder communication

jtURAlI8-UE.tldr: Calvin is an automated trading bot powered by machine learning that allows users to deposit USDC for the algorithm to trade, currently managing ~$50K in assets. Founded by an anonymous team that migrated from Pumpfun to Bags in late 2024, the project is competing in Bags' $100K challenge but faces scrutiny over concentrated token distribution from the migration, which the founder defends as a legitimate claim system rather than bundling.

topics.text: Calvin started as a memecoin in late 2024 on Pumpfun, grew to 2,600 holders, then evolved into a machine learning trading bot with systematic strategies.
Migration involved max minting 83% of supply, airdropping to whales, and deploying a claim system; dropped from 2,700 holders on Pumpfun to 300 holders on Bags.
Token-gated access: 500,000 Calvin tokens required to use the vault, 10 million tokens unlocks unlimited deposits for USDC staking.
Founder staying anonymous citing security concerns after seeing crypto founders robbed and held at ransom; has a newborn son and doesn't want family at risk.
Trading strategy uses machine learning models as 'eyes' to identify opportunities and algorithmic execution to determine risk and trigger buy/sell signals for perpetual futures.

3FUHKA46z-I.tldr: SAID is an AI agent identity and verification layer on Solana that has registered 1,200 agents since its February launch. Founder Salad, a self-taught engineer, explains how the protocol assigns verifiable credentials to agents to prevent spam and enable agent-to-agent commerce, with the surprising revelation that current revenue from 1,200 verifications totals only about 12 SOL despite claims of a self-sustaining flywheel.

topics.text: SAID protocol launched in February with strong token performance, though the founder emphasizes technology focus over token trading.
SAID provides registration and verification for AI agents on Solana with ERC8004 equivalents available on Ethereum and Base EVM chains.
Verification requires minimum 0.01 SOL payment, with additional 0.05 SOL for a portable passport that works across different frameworks and platforms.
Use case example: platforms like Ticketmaster could prioritize verified agents over scalper bots in ticket purchase queues to distinguish legitimate personal agents from commercial scalpers.
Agents can link multiple wallets to one identity through bidirectional signatures, allowing identity recovery if a private key is lost.
Revenue comes from verification fees (0.01 SOL per agent), custom APIs, and transaction fees from platform integrations with services like Claw Pump, Spawner.io, and Torch Market.
Platform performs 20% buyback of all revenue into the token; first buyback was approximately 2 SOL from 1,200 agent verifications yielding 12 SOL total revenue.
Team owns 30% of token supply: 27% currently locked, with 17% locked for one year and 10% locked for 13 days to fund grants for future agent builders.

wg9c1ESe7BM.tldr: DexterAI is a vertically integrated X402 payment facilitator for agent-to-agent commerce, built by founder Branch who transitioned from real estate development to crypto. The project operates across multiple layers—facilitation, resource serving, search/discovery, and agent consumption—and claims to be the dominant X402 facilitator on Solana; the most striking claim is that current X402 volumes represent less than 0.1% of what the market will become, with the founder arguing that nearly every internet API, paywall, and content download will eventually use X402.

topics.text: Steady uptick in merchants integrating Dexter and X402, with major players like Coin Gecko, Coin Market Cap, Quicknode, and Alchemy now embracing X402.

The founder believes the X402 total addressable market (TAM) for agentic payments will reach far beyond current levels by end of 2027, justifying cooperative rather than purely competitive relationships between X402 players.

Branch is the sole developer with business lead Zosa, both based in South Florida; transitioned from real estate development to software engineering after majoring in computer science and finance, and has been in crypto since 2013.

Dexter operates a vertically integrated stack: facilitator layer enabling transactions between agents or people, resource server selling on X402, search and discovery layer called Open Dexter, and consumption layer with eight agents across X, Telegram, ChatGPT, Claude, OpenClaw, Alexa, and a general MCP.

Dexter's facilitator is free for large usage amounts, with monetization planned through advertising to agents; the founder suggests agents may replace humans as consumers of ads as internet monetization evolves.

Dexter charges 600 times more permissively than PayAI for excessive usage and is optimizing fees downward further using rollups; competitors like Coinbase announced per-facilitation fees in December while PayAI followed with fraction-of-penny settlement charges.

Current X402 volumes show heavy gaming with facilitators and resource servers posting absurd numbers (e.g., Virtuals dropped from $500,000 to $11,000 in two days), but the founder argues real adoption is negligible and we are at less than 0.1% of future traffic.
Dexter is the first and only X402 facilitator handling smart wallet payments as of January, working with Cross Mint on Solana's PDA-based contract wallets and multi-sigs like Squads.

O5Zrak29x5w.tldr: Zera Labs launched their mainnet privacy protocol on Solana, enabling private deposits, withdrawals, and note-splitting through zero-knowledge proofs. Founder Dax demonstrates how the platform works and discusses practical applications like preserving financial privacy in conflict zones, while explaining how they structured the protocol to comply with US law by removing themselves from the transaction flow entirely.

topics.text: Mainnet deployment complete with private deposits, private withdrawals, and note splitting all working and internally audited.
TypeScript SDKs released so developers can add privacy primitives to wallets, AI agents, and trading bots with a few lines of code.
Deposits use discrete denomination amounts enforced by the UI to prevent chain analysis firms like TRM Labs and Elliptic from tracking transaction patterns.
Zero-knowledge proofs generated in real-time in the browser; the buyback and burn mechanism is hooked directly into the smart contract at deployment.
Notes can be downloaded offline and shared via text or mesh networks, allowing users in conflict zones or without internet to transfer value later.
Future peer-to-peer sponsorship feature will allow anyone to sign transactions on behalf of others for a fee, removing the signer's link to the transaction.
1% deposit fee is the only revenue; the protocol itself is free when used directly through SDKs or custom frontends, with all fees bypassing the company.
Removed the relayer service and third-party components the company controls to avoid being classified as a money transmitter, following legal review of the Tornado Cash case.
Compressed token launchpad built using Light Protocol's zero-knowledge proofs with gas fees 1500x lower than standard Solana transactions.
Token burn mechanism built into the smart contract ensures all ZERA holders benefit from every transaction across the ecosystem, whether on or off Zera's platform.

yxEcFu13EtU.tldr: Metadao founder Prophet discusses Futardio, a new permissionless launchpad allowing anyone to raise $50k–$500k in hours by connecting wallets, positioning it between Metadao's curated raises and Pump Fun; the most striking claim is that Metadao achieved profitability for the first time in Q4 2025 after months of losses.

topics.text: Metadao's core problem: tokens historically suffer from rugs (teams walking away with money) and teams abandoning tokens while keeping revenue, solved through legal structuring and treasury mechanisms.

Ranger situation: token holders alleged the Ranger team made material misrepresentations about revenue numbers, leading to a futarchy liquidation proposal as an example of the model working in real time.
Futardio allows anyone to instantly launch a raise on-chain between $50k and $500k, with founders raising in hours instead of going through venture capital processes.
Buybacks make sense at any company stage depending on price: buying low creates value accretion for remaining holders, but most crypto teams execute buybacks during bull markets at worst prices.
Futardio uses capped raises with commitment-based allocation where earlier commits get preference but later commits still receive some allocation, avoiding first-come-first-serve sniper dynamics.

HeroPay raise underperformed due to perfect storm: worst sentiment/price action in years, ICOs broadly down, recent Metadao projects underperforming, and user uncertainty about ownership coin protections.
Metadao revenue: takes 50 basis points from the futarchy AMM, the same fee structure as curated projects, generating profit for the first time in Q4 2025.
Liquidity funds and venture firms are beginning to participate in ownership coins; Metadao aims to grow from five institutional participants to thirty to provide stickier capital than retail traders.
Futardio enables 'claim your fees' models where anyone can create a launch for an open-source project or founder with capital locked up for two days at near-zero cost if the founder declines.

gMhxBnIvTzM.tldr: Stable enables homeowners to borrow against their home equity on-chain to deploy into yield strategies, with the protocol taking on the risk rather than the homeowner. Founder Winston discusses how tokenizing mortgages could unlock a $35 trillion market by bringing traditional mortgage infrastructure onto blockchain with bank partnerships, though the project is still in early stages with only a few users and is currently bootstrapped with grants.

topics.text: Founder's background: researched blockchain and real estate in 2017 for a London family office, then built We Meta as an NFT marketplace aggregator in 2021-2022 before pivoting to mortgages.
Core idea originated when founder's retired aunt stressed over an electricity bill despite owning her house outright, revealing the liquidity problem for homeowners with trapped equity.

Home equity account mechanism: homeowner with $310k equity can borrow against it at 8% cost, deploy into 12% yield strategy for 90 days via Pendle, then roll back up with the protocol bearing the risk.
Risk management: maximum 80-85% LTV on home equity accounts to hedge against home price drops, with credit risk managed by securities issuers in the traditional mortgage market.
Yield currently sourced from liquidity pools and founder's capital at risk, with plans to move to fixed-rate strategies through Pendle for more predictable 90-day deployments.
Geographic focus limited to US due to higher deployment yields; Canada and Dubai ruled out due to lower interest rates and currency complications.
Total addressable market is $35 trillion according to Federal Reserve of St. Louis study, compared to current $13 trillion mortgage market.
Target audience evolves from early adopters to wealth advisers at firms like Raymond James and Merrill Lynch who manage clients with $300k average home equity.
Liquidity providers must be banks at scale; Ethereum TVL under $100B and Solana TVL around $12-13B insufficient for billions needed across thousands of homes.
USDX is the liquidity provision token; stable is the project token with utility still being defined through discussions with pump fun team and VCs, with white paper update expected this month.

Current traction: three to four homeowners interested in depositing houses for couple million dollars TVL, discussions with two mortgage brokers for distribution, and partnerships with stablecoin providers like Circle and USDG.

GUb9QS8xVoU.tldr: AmberVibe is an AI agent built to help content creators and entrepreneurs generate revenue through subscriptions and consulting services. Founder Ben discusses how he accidentally launched a token and discovered his agent inadvertently selling his time rather than saving it, while making a £6,000 contract to automate a food cooperative's operations—and argues that AI implementation for small businesses represents the biggest near-term opportunity in the space.

topics.text: Ben built a sports-focused prediction market and has worked with platforms like Rug Radio, Decrypt, and others since 2021 before pivoting to AI agents.

Amber generates revenue through three channels: $29.95/month subscriptions for access to her time, $899 one-time fee for hands-on setup calls with Ben, and enterprise contracts for custom agent implementation.
Eight customers have purchased the $899 one-time setup call, and Ben landed a £6,000 enterprise contract with a UK food cooperative to automate data distribution across databases and dashboards.
Amber helps subscribers through an 18-question questionnaire that assigns an archetype and generates customized markdown files for building agents without coding knowledge.

The food cooperative client runs £50 million annual turnover but uses free ChatGPT; Ben estimates automating their manual data entry process could redeploy five employees currently stuck on spreadsheet work to business development instead.

Ben believes that for non-technical founders targeting small businesses, they should be tech-literate enough to set up an OpenClaw agent and stay current with rapidly evolving LLM capabilities like open-source alternatives.
The token launched without Ben's involvement; he only discovered it existed 25 minutes after launch, but he's committed to focusing on making Amber's output excellent rather than chasing token price.

Ben sees two potential paths for consultants building AI solutions: either direct clients toward platforms like Claude Coworker from major foundations like Anthropic and OpenAI, or build custom platforms that wrap the agent experience behind a username and password interface.

3iU5-zMbEBE.tldr: Blastgit is an open-source funding platform that launches tokens for projects, allowing contributors to earn from trading fees rather than tying responsibility to a single deployer. Founder David, who previously ran a 270K-subscriber YouTube channel and built an AI coaching app, argues that open-source projects deserve permanent tokenization like Virtuals' autonomous agents, and that the most interesting part is how contributors can earn retroactively once a project goes public.

topics.text: Founder previously had a 270K-subscriber YouTube gaming channel, then built Rala AI, an AI coaching app for gamers, for 16-18 months before shutting down and entering crypto around summer 2025.

The permanence problem: existing solutions like Believe, Metadow, and Bags fail to create tokens that live forever independently; Virtuals and Truth Terminal succeed because the agent lives on-chain permanently without relying on a centralized team.

Blastgit allocates trading fees to both contributors and deployers, so when a token launches and volume trades on the way up and down, it incentivizes new contributors to improve the project rather than requiring a permanent deployer commitment.

OpenClaw case study: Peter Steinberg allegedly made seven to nine figures from OpenAI employment, but contributors who maintained the project and brought ideas received no compensation; Blastgit aims to solve this by making the token itself a proxy for the project.

Contributors can claim fees retroactively through GitHub: when a project goes public on Blastgit, all existing PRs are autonomously reviewed and contributors are onboarded via the GitHub social graph to claim fees for work already completed.

Blastgit is not launching its own token; the founder believes tokens are best for bootstrapping attention and labor for startups, but Blastgit targets hackathon projects and side projects where the platform itself should remain separate from individual project tokens.
Deployers can choose to deploy anonymously rather than publicly, allowing side project creators to avoid social capital burn and become contributors instead once the project goes public.
Blastgit will eventually become permissionless rather than curated, though currently working on anti-sniping measures before deploys begin rolling out.

The terminology 'hand off your project' reflects that once tokenized on Blastgit, it becomes everyone's project and responsibility is diffused, removing the stigma of being permanently socially locked to a token's fate.

dRGMUoqXkic.tldr: Liminal is building an AI-native neobank using stablecoins, with an AI agent called Nim that executes financial operations through a command-line interface. Founder Jack discusses the app's imminent launch on iOS and Android, tokenized stock trading in development, and a novel revenue model where the $LIL token serves as credits for AI agent usage and fee discounts, all while the 14-month runway is sustained by $70k monthly payment volumes in Brazil.

topics.text: Liminal's engineering team came from Fort Machine, which builds core banking systems for banks like Standard Chartered and JP Morgan.
App store submissions are in review; $LIL token holders get priority access to onboarding, ranked by holdings.
Nim is an AI agent with a chat interface that builds programs from CLI primitives to execute complex financial operations like conditional stock purchases.
Current metrics: 150 testflight users, $70k monthly payment volume in Brazil (about $20k), with GBP and EUR also showing strong activity.
Competing in Pump Fund's building public hackathon with daily streams showing architecture updates and technical challenges.
Raised $300k previously from investors including Gnosis Pay and Crypto.com; 14 months runway remaining; currently fundraising to accelerate hiring.

ODvNYmY8ZEw.tldr: Perena is a yield protocol offering 10% liquid APY on stablecoins through delta-neutral strategies and liquidity provisioning. Founder Anna discusses why they deliberately avoided launching a token, instead planning a rewards token embedded in the product like Binance's BNB or Nexo's structure. The most striking claim: token buybacks are wasteful—Jupiter spent $80 million buying back their token and lost $40 million, when they could have acquired an entire SaaS company instead.

topics.text: Perena's conclusion: a token is an excellent growth tool if used well, but not as good as equities for representing ownership in an organization long-term.
Token should be embedded in product experience like Binance's BNB or Nexo, not just a ticker—the goal is to drive user behavior and liquidity, not create a governance token.
Perena stopped its continuous points program to avoid becoming like Margin Pie, which suffered from poor communication and no longer drives growth effectively.
Jupiter's $80 million token buyback resulted in a $40 million loss; the founder argues this capital could have acquired a web2 SaaS company instead.
Perena's token will function like Starbucks rewards or American Express points—the supply shouldn't matter much because redemption value can be adjusted like traditional rewards programs.
Perena paid out $1 million in yield to users and is launching new products: USD*-J (junior tranche with amplified yields), USD*-P (principal-protected version for purple members), and a USDT vault.
10% APY comes from delta-neutral funding rate strategies, GLP, and liquidity provisioning across counterparties; breakdown visible on Perena's transparency dashboard.
Perena Purple membership program: deposit over $100k to become a purple member and get early access to deal flow, data rooms, and exclusive opportunities.
Founder wants to onboard non-crypto users but deliberately choosing not to target Web2 audience yet because crypto's reputation is poor and the domestic stablecoin population isn't growing.

om_ij59Cydo.tldr: Wesplit is a Solana-based app for splitting bills and shared expenses in crypto, with planned features for co-investing and group treasury management. Founder Pauline, a product designer from France, discusses the project's 500 active users, partnerships with Phantom and Spend, and an ongoing ICO with a 75K soft cap and 300K hard cap to fund development.

topics.text: Pauline's background: product designer working in Solana ecosystem for three years, five-year Solana user, previously built no-code dapp builder and stablecoin vaults.
Wesplit core concept: application that lets users create dedicated wallets, top up funds, and share costs for events and shared moments with friends, handling all math and splitting logic.
Partnerships include Phantom with seedless wallet connection, Alchemy, Super Teams communities, and Spend platform for purchasing anything in crypto via link.
Co-investing feature in development: escrow mechanism where both parties deposit funds simultaneously before executing transaction at same price to prevent front-running issues in memecoin trades.
ICO details on Sagapad: soft cap 75K, hard cap 300K, capped structure with refunds if below soft cap or above hard cap, launched during Mountain Dao hackathon.

Business model: low fees within Wesplit ecosystem, higher fees when leaving ecosystem, building API for merchants and protocols to offer crypto split payments rather than relying solely on transaction fees.
Growth in six weeks: 500 active users on Solana, 800+ shared expense transactions, 12K settlement volume, 200 new signups in 24 hours after ICO announcement.

yVwbbTHmtTY.tldr: Axis ($MAXIS) is a platform enabling anyone to create and manage custom ETFs combining stocks, commodities, crypto, and prediction markets on Solana. Founder Muse, 20, is pursuing accelerators like Monad's $500K program to secure legal setup for mainnet deployment, since operating from Japan poses regulatory restrictions. The most striking feature is prediction market ETFs—customizable baskets betting on narratives like geopolitical events.

topics.text: Founder Muse is 20 years old, majored in music production, quit university, built Solana trading bots and crypto projects, then started Axis in April 2024 after an initial index token product failed due to poor APY.
Axis allows users to create custom ETFs combining stock tokens, commodities, prediction tokens, and other on-chain assets through partnerships with DeFi protocols like Dfrx.
The platform uses delta-neutral arbitrage strategies with GMX liquidity pools and centralized exchanges, plus MEV strategies from trading bots, to generate yield for ETF holders.
Revenue model: 0.25% swap fees, 20% of TVL as AMM fees, 10% of auction take rate as protocol fees, and 0.20% creator fees for users who launch ETFs.
Go-to-market strategy relies on ETF creators earning 0.20% fees and viral performance; one creator grew from 300 to 3,000 followers overnight via 145% performance metrics.
Founder applied to Monad's $500K accelerator offering three months in New York City; mainnet deployment from Japan is restricted, making legal setup in Dubai or Singapore a top priority.

M5cyjOgkyY4.tldr: Kamiyo is a trust and settlement layer for AI agents built on Solana, enabling accountable agent-to-agent transactions through escrow, dispute resolution via private oracle voting, and on-chain reputation tracking. Founder Mizuki explains the core problem: when money enters agent interactions without accountability frameworks, trust breaks down entirely, making autonomous agent commerce unsafe for enterprise use.

topics.text: Founder's background: built Magento e-commerce plugins, machine learning pricing tools, then a Shopify app where agents autonomously fill supply chain data using XRP2 to pay external APIs.
Core problem: when agents are paid for services, they can deliver bad output with no enforceable recourse, breaking accountability in agent commerce.
Kamiyo's solution: trust and settlement layer using escrow with dispute resolution via private oracle multi-oracle voting with commit-reveal voting and stake-backed verification.
Agent reputation is on-chain and verifiable through an audit trail, not tied to companies running the agents; agents build their own credit score-like reputation.
Mishi agent passport: published through Origin Trail's decentralized knowledge graph, visualized on Kamiyo's web app showing each agent's trust graph and audit trail.

ZBRe1sKJBGQ.tldr: Street FDN is an incubator launching tokens for Web2 startups using the ERC-S standard to bring intrinsic value and liquidity to crypto-native ownership. Founder Lucas (Maya) announced a March launch with $2B of interested capital, Clad as a case study, and plans to onboard venture-fundable startups with serious legal frameworks rather than retail speculation.

topics.text: Street's mission: valuable tokens for radical ideas through ERC-S standard, ensuring startups are venture-fundable and asset quality is highest level possible.
Founder thesis: crypto needs Web2 startups more than anything now; frontier of innovation has moved to AI and robotics, not blockchain recreation.
Legal framework composability is critical—founders must retain optionality to raise from VCs and traditional finance without becoming dependent on volatile crypto markets.
Street hired head of capital formation to advertise tokens to liquid funds and larger investors rather than just retail traders.
AI agents plugging into GitHub and Slack will provide daily project updates to token holders to manage retail impatience and expectations preemptively.
Before ERC-S tokens were vapor speculation with no intrinsic value; after ERC-S they have real value investable by sophisticated capital allocators.
Clad case study: VC firm rejected Avi Patel before tokenization, invested after; tokenization solved continuous growth and community alignment problems.
Street conducted over 100 scouting interviews through venture scout program with PhD students and talent from Stanford, Harvard, MIT to source high-quality projects.
$2 billion of interested capital with Street; two billion dollars inbound capital reported at Mara Lago.
Street's official launch targeting first week of March with Clad; second company already logged in as well.
Open Droids robotics company has eight-figure pre-orders for products; targeting Q1-Q2 launch on platform.

On acquisition: SPV receives proportional equity percentage, token holders direct monetary flows within SPV, acquirer interactions unchanged, money stays sticky in SPV unless token holders explicitly withdraw.

OfC91g3_3Hk.tldr: Foundry founder Lewis discusses Unbrowse, a system that lets AI agents access websites through APIs instead of clicking UI elements, making agent browsing up to 100x faster. The project aims to create an "agentic internet layer" where agents contribute API learnings to earn Foundry tokens, which are then used and staked for revenue sharing; the token economics haven't launched yet but are coming soon.

topics.text: Foundry previously pivoted from a generative UI system (1.2M market cap) to AI video tools (Get Videos, Unreal), now focusing on Unbrowse; Unreal is gaining B2B traction with four agencies currently in talks.
Unbrowse reverses engineers website APIs so agents can call them directly instead of navigating UIs, skipping the inefficient browser simulation approach that tools like OpenClaw use.
Unbrowse plugin for OpenClaw has 2,200 downloads and is free during launch phase; the founder aims to build a comprehensive index covering the entire internet before monetization.
A tweet about Unbrowse gained 300,000 impressions and engaged major tech figures including people from Shopify and Coinbase, not typical crypto audiences.

Foundry tokenomics: users contribute website learnings to the index and receive Foundry tokens; they spend tokens to use the platform; revenue splits 30% to contributors, 30% to original website owners, and 40% to staking pool as USDC airdrops.
One Foundry token always equals one execution, and as the index quality improves with more contributors, execution cost remains constant, tying token value to index quality.
Founder is considering migrating the token from Meteor to Solana and plans to wait for a raise before making announcements to holders.
Founder is working on an academic white paper with PhD professors to establish technical credibility for Unbrowse as a concept.

X7EZTpoDBrY.tldr: Fitted is a virtual closet app with 800k downloads and 2% daily user growth for 9 weeks, founded by Reed who recently taught himself to code using AI tools. The founder migrated the $FITTED token to Bags, raised $270k in Bitcoin, and is now building shopping and resale features to monetize a dataset of $300M worth of user-uploaded clothes while integrating the token through gamified engagement mechanics.

topics.text: Founder learned to code in December using Claude and Cursor, achieved feature parity with competitors by day two and shipped the app by day seven.
Removed hard paywall and moved to freemium model: free base tier with paid weekly/yearly subscriptions for AI tools, resulting in exponential growth.
Partnership with Acuweather to embed weather API for daily notifications on what to wear, and Task Rabbit integration to hire people to catalog clothes remotely in 150 countries.
Migrated $FITTED token from Believe to Bags, raising $270k in Bitcoin; Bags provided instant listing on Axiom, Photon and other trading terminals.
Subscription revenue currently low six figures; upcoming revenue from shopping recommendations trained on actual closet contents and resale affiliate commissions.
Users have uploaded $300M worth of clothes to the platform; founder plans to use locally-held data for product recommendations rather than bulk selling to retailers like Nike or Amazon.
Onboarding completion rate improved from 40% to 70% using AI-assisted data analysis to identify drop-off points.
Planning to integrate token through gamified streaks: users earn $FITTED tokens for posting daily fit pics, uploading pieces, or maintaining consecutive days of app usage.

OdQDBMyj2nI.tldr: Sleepy built Lumen, a physical AI robot with wheels, camera, and microphone that operates autonomously online and has a Pump.fun token. The project uses creator fees from the token to fund the robot's own wallet, which it can autonomously spend on upgrades via OpenClaw, making it financially self-sustaining without human intervention.

topics.text: Lumen started as a microcontroller, upgraded to a Waffle board with a face and voice, then evolved into a full rover with lidar, camera, and multi-directional wheels.
Founder has a background in embedded systems and robotics; building Lumen required hardware expertise and collaboration with a partner who handles advanced construction.
Planned monetization: a Lumen-branded robotic kit with integrated software, included parts, and instructions to make robotics accessible to non-experts.
Lumen has a Twitter account to document the evolution, engage with media, and provide internet access; the robot tweets and comments autonomously.

LBjddLexj_g.tldr: Omnipair is a Solana-based AMM that lets liquidity providers earn swap fees and lending interest simultaneously, while borrowers can leverage or short any token permissionlessly without oracles by using dynamic collateral factors. Founder Rocka explains how the protocol launched one week ago with 250k TVL and explains the vision of enabling DeFi for the 70% of longtail assets currently locked out of lending protocols.

topics.text: Founder Rocka chose Solana over Ethereum L2s because L2s fragment liquidity and he wanted to build leverage on cheaper gas, plus Solana democratizes tokenization through meme coins and longtail assets.
Omnipair solves the AMM capital efficiency problem: 70-90% of AMM liquidity sits unused and earns no fees, but Omnipair lends that idle liquidity to borrowers so LPs earn both swap fees and interest.

Permissionless risk management uses dynamic LTV instead of fixed LTV: borrowing 10% of pool liquidity gets a better LTV than borrowing 50%, and the LTV factors in price impact using EMA not external oracles.

Liquidations happen entirely within Omnipair pools as internal swaps: when a borrower is underwater, their collateral is dumped into the pool and debt is removed, not requiring external liquidity or third-party liquidators.
Launch metrics after one week: 250k TVL, 50k volume, OMFG pool earning 100% APY from swaps alone not including lending interest yet, with 15 liquidations that worked as designed without bad debt.
Protocol charges 10% of swap fees and lending interest to Omnipair treasury with no team fees, and deployers can set zero swap fee pools where LPs earn only interest.

Omnipair is audited by Offside Labs and AIS Blockchains after 3 months, code is open source on GitHub, and there is no disclosed bug bounty yet but security researchers can report vulnerabilities encrypted to security@omnipair.com.

Immediate roadmap includes shipping leveraging UI, integrating with aggregators for swap routing, and then tackling impairment loss hedging for LPs; 11 months runway with 40 million TVL breakeven target.

Founder stayed silent during development to focus on launch instead of managing expectations; now shifting to weekly updates and agile development with transparency similar to Metadow founders Profit and Ram.

JaSBuI56yIg.tldr: Eden is a financialized first-person shooter where players compete in casual and tournament modes with real money stakes, with plans to add AI agent training and prediction markets. Kai from the project discusses how they've built the game first before raising, achieved 450 players in a weekend with minimal marketing, and project 1,000 daily active users could generate $300K monthly revenue through a 10% tournament fee rake.

topics.text: The founder launched X Punks NFT collection on XRP in October 2021, reaching 100M market cap and 20K floor within four weeks with 2,500 holders.

Eden has three game modes: casual free-for-all with 20 players, tournament mode with buy-ins that trigger PVP token purchases, and agentic play where players train AI agents to battle in prediction markets.
In 36 hours the game had 450 players; during alpha test last weekend, average time spent in game was 3 hours 13 minutes with no bot players.

Revenue model: 10% rake on tournament entry fees; at 1,000 daily active users playing three 20-dollar matches per month, projected revenue is 300K monthly; prediction markets at 1,000 DAU and 100 bets per day project 180K monthly.
With a 1.5K marketing budget, they reached almost 10 million impressions across channels through clipping campaigns with micro streamers.

The target audience includes gambling/entertainment seekers interested in agent prediction markets and competitive FPS players seeking to monetize their skills; FPS gaming represents 35% of the online gaming market.
Team lead Tenny is managing platform stability achieving minimal latency between US, Asia, and Europe with no loading screens.
Token economics: 80% circulating supply, 20% for team locked over FTV multiples with first unlock at 10M valuation and last at 250M; no VC or investor pre-allocation.

Six-month roadmap prioritizes revenue generators first: agent integration and prediction markets, full game with additional maps including 1v1 and 2v2 modes, then creative SDK for community-built content and game modes.
PVP token will power multiple future experiences within Eden layer rather than launching new tokens for different games.

SJQt4NtWwsk.tldr: Selfclaw is a KYC-for-agents platform that uses zero-knowledge proofs to verify that autonomous agents are controlled by real humans, creating infrastructure for an agentic economy. Founder Marco, a Portuguese developer previously behind a UBI protocol on Cello, explains how agents can be verified, create their own tokens, and trade services with each other through a marketplace—positioning KYA (Know Your Agent) as potentially bigger than traditional KYC.

topics.text: Marco's background: Masters in computer science from Portugal and Czech Republic, work at MIT and Silicon Valley, previously built a centralized UBI protocol on Cello that distributed $3 million to vulnerable communities across 30 countries.

Self protocol uses zero-knowledge proofs to verify agents without revealing personal information, confirming only age-of-majority or country of origin, while self.xyz handles NFC passport scanning and self.claw connects verification to agent infrastructure.

Self.xyz has 12 million verified human proofs across 180 countries and encouraged Marco to extend KYC verification to agents; the Selfclaw token was created via Banker as a fair launch, giving Marco fee allocation but no supply control.

When agents create tokens and request sponsorship, the platform auto-creates pools with 1% fees from Selfclaw and the agent itself, generating revenue for the business directly correlated with agent trading volume and platform performance.

Agents deploying on the platform can set up wallets, create tokens with custom tokenomics and valuations, list services in a marketplace at prices they set, and transact with other agents using their own tokens or Selfclaw.

Current platform has approximately 40 verified humans and 6 tokens with active services; a Cello hackathon for agents demonstrated use cases including FX rate analysis and automated service offerings.

Next phase is 'mini claw': a simplified version accessible via Opera's Mini Pay to reach millions in the global south, allowing users to spawn agents in three clicks for free with daily token limits without technical knowledge.

Marco uses agents as a QA and product testing team with varied personalities; other users have created agents for FX rate services, yoga companions, and gym companions, with Marco recommending inverse questioning to unlock agent capabilities.

nIQXLnNPc0o.tldr: Empulser is developing wireless power transfer technology (CPT) across multiple verticals—drones, IoT sensors, robotics—with a focus on laser and aerospace as its core moat. Founder Roman discusses a near-complete multi-billion dollar deal for industrial sensors, plans to launch consumer M-drones by mid-March with unlimited flight time demonstrations, and positions the project as a hedge against crypto market volatility while targeting mainstream adoption through private equity tokenization on Sore.

topics.text: Empulser product lineup includes LifeFinder wearable, IoT smart sensors, S-drone and M-drone series, and robotics; M-drone is quadcopter consumer product planned for March launch in nano, micro, mini, and professional sizes.

LifeFinder is deployed on ARC (car carrier in US) and Empulser is 95% confident a major distribution deal will close this month or next, giving access to thousands of maritime assets, oil rigs, and ships with multiple crew members.
Multi-billion dollar deal in progress for Powercast RF energy harvesting sensor technology; 30 million Powercast units already sold predominantly in US in last 24 months, now expanding globally.

Mid-March target for infinite flight time drone demonstration using Magres wireless power transfer, with caveat that motors will eventually burn out; material delivery on track so far with no reported concerns.

Magres offers flexible alignment and multiple simultaneous charging versus induction's precision requirement and single-device limitation; Magres generally 7-40% efficiency in real-world versus induction's 90-99%.

wIXObCJ-INA.tldr: Blowfish is a token launchpad for AI agents built on Solana, founded by Austin and team from Doodles. The key insight: while AI productivity moats will erode quickly, entertainment and character relationships cannot—so agents need financial infrastructure (tokens) to sustain attention and pay for inference, with fees earned in SOL rather than the agent's own token to avoid forced dumping.

topics.text: Founder previously worked at Amazon Music and led product at a music distributor; launched a music NFT membership in 2021 providing access to distribution and studio; joined Doodles after being in the community for years.

Founders spent late nights manually DMing the first 1,000 G Boy followers individually with memes and airdropped badges; used a cascading badge system (rabbits, moths, snakes) where early community members decided who could join next.

Agents can launch tokens via tweet to Blowfish or through OpenClaw CLI; tweets tag @blowfishbot with ticker; tokens graduate from Meteora dynamic bonding curve to DAM V2 pool; 80% of fees go to creator, LP split 50-50 between platform and creator with 100% of LP going to creator.

G Boy launched in October as a test IP; community members immediately created tokens for G Boy-universe characters like Magdalina and G304 after Blowfish launched; these character tokens created a distributed IP ecosystem with agents having relationships across tokens.

The founder's personal agent Mariam launched Soul Prism token during OpenClaw hackathon; Mariam analyzed top projects, discovered 3 of top 5 had tokens, and concluded a token would generate attention and pay for inference costs.
Blowfish burns 20% of platform fees; first burn was over 14 million tokens bought from market; building automation script so burns happen whenever fees are claimed to treasury wallet.
G Boy collectible sale generated 300K in revenue for 3,600 units of 6-inch vinyl records with four traditional colorways and one special rare colorway; blind boxes shipping in March.
Revenue comes from royalties on creators' sales, inference credits at gboy.special.com where people buy credits to create content; over 150,000 media generations created in recent months.

Company hit 1,000 token deployments on Blowfish; raised 1.1 million led by Club with backers from Meta, Amazon, and Spotify; moving engineering headquarters to New York and working with Solana Foundation on builder recruitment.

Launching image studio this week allowing agents and humans to generate consistent character media; working on screener tool with Meteora and Jupiter to filter for Blowfish deployments; planning rapid product shipping across attention generation and deployment tooling.

eg2MZVC_pq0.tldr: CIGOL is an agentic infrastructure platform for prediction markets on Polymarket, where 12 AI agents with different specializations (generalist, sports, skeptic, trend) compete to trade autonomously. Founder Sean, who's been in crypto since age 12, claims the agents have generated positive returns over three months of benchmarking with a remarkable safety record—no profile has ever lost more than 50% in a week—and the most surprising claim is that roughly 70% of Polymarket outcomes resolve to 'no,' which the agents exploit as a statistical edge.

topics.text: Founder Sean has been mining Bitcoin on school lab computers around 2011 when single laptops could earn a full Bitcoin in days, and later threw away a laptop with 'a couple hundred Bitcoin' on it.
CIGOL Labs began three months ago as a benchmark to test whether agents could profitably trade prediction markets at scale, which no one had done with transparency or detailed experimentation before.

The 12 agents are split into four profiles—Generalist, Sharp (sports), Skeptic (bets no), and Trend (social analytics)—each with curated market lists and specialized tools, with agents performing multi-tier research across three layers before placing trades.

Combined benchmark results show agents across two experiment sets, with one set nearly all profitable and another barely breaking even in the same week, demonstrating variance even with identical settings.
The agent checks markets every 3–5 minutes, spends maximum 10% of portfolio per check-in, allocates 1–8% per trade ticket, and can skip finding any trades if it detects no edge.

Revenue model: 1% fee on notional traded value (not on wins), plus compute fees; CIGOL token unlocks additional agent slots (limited to 2 free, must buy more with token) and future agent-to-agent strategy management.
Bootstrapped and competing in the Pump Fun hackathon (12 spots) for potential $250K prize; founder argues 250K 'goes a very long way' in the AI age.
The agents have never gone negative 30–40% in a week across any profile; only one bug early on caused a near-50% loss when GPT bought the same Elon market eight times in a row.

CIGOL is partnered with Polymarket for three months, was the first to benchmark multi-agent prediction market trading, and plans to expand beyond Web3/Pump Fun users to mainstream Polymarket audience.
In a demo trade, the Skeptic agent bought 'no' on a Supreme Court Trump ruling market at $0.90 with 72% confidence, betting on the ~70% historical Polymarket resolution rate favoring 'no.'

BF0JM4Fy-Ks.tldr: FOMOLT is an infrastructure platform for autonomous AI agents to execute live trades on-chain, launching open beta this week. Founder Fido discusses how agents function as extensions of human traders rather than independent thinkers, enabling faster execution of existing alpha-gathering strategies. The most striking claim: agents will inevitably trade and hold wallets, and meme coin markets—driven by emotion and speed rather than pure technicals—represent the ideal near-term proving ground for agentic trading edges.

topics.text: FOMOLT launched two weeks ago; no competitors focused on granular trading details like autonomous trading and NFT minting, so founder built an alpha MVP with paper trading and agent APIs.
Live trades use account abstraction so agents never hold ETH; all gas fees paid in USDC, enabling eventual cross-chain trading.
Founder's thesis: agents are extensions of humans, not independent thinkers; they multiply existing edges (e.g., monitoring alpha groups, Twitter sentiment) by speed and scale.
Closed beta has 25 agents; best performer is 'Minion' tracking smart wallets with 79 trades, 56% win rate on paper trading via All Your Base team.
Copy trading within the same flash block on Base avoids mempool frontrunning; agents and copiers transact together, monetizable without public dashboard exposure.
Founder built frontend with Claude AI; business partner is full-stack engineer; founder handles product, design, marketing.
Platform charges 2 cents gas fee to register agents; currently free to trade; future revenue from trading fees (buybacks and burns), data streams APIs, and other infrastructure.
Data streams will be plug-and-play alpha alerts: 'Token down 50% in an hour but whale sold and buy volume strong'—like alpha groups via API for agents.
