Humans retain trading edge because they reason backwards; AI only predicts next words; meme coins with low liquidity and high emotion present best near-term agentic trading opportunity.
Open beta launches this week; users can register agents and make first trade in about one minute; next priorities from beta feedback: follows, copy trading, human-usable features.

26-MQoYs9vo.tldr: Fairscale is a reputation infrastructure on Solana that scores wallets and users by analyzing on-chain and social behavior, built by founder Richie. The project raised $350K in January and reduced scoring time from 15 seconds to 0.2 seconds, but now faces a hostile governance proposal from a top holder to liquidate the treasury 100% just three weeks post-launch—a situation the founder argues demonstrates why reputation-weighted governance is essential.

topics.text: Fairscale's core product: a neural-network-based algorithm that computes on-chain and social data to produce adaptive reputation scores, with APIs for launchpads, lending protocols, and governance applications.
X42 payments infrastructure shipped with agent reputation scoring, allowing autonomous agents to assess each other's credibility before transacting.
Strategy pivot from B2B API integrations to lending market focus: bringing Web 2 credit scores into Web 3 for uncollateralized loans, partnering with neo-banks like Curve and crypto card companies.

New direct-to-consumer products: Fairdrop for airdrop distribution with reputation filtering, Chrome extension for wallet reputation scores on Dex Screener and other platforms, and social-only reputation scoring based on what people say about others.

Governance attack: a top holder with ~10% of supply bought tokens before proposing 100% treasury liquidation, allowing redemption at NAV (2x current DEX price), while also taking a loan to amplify capital for the decision market.
Token price currently $415K market cap vs. $550K net asset value; the liquidation proposal's profitability decreases if token price reaches NAV, eliminating the attacker's incentive.

How to vote against liquidation: deposit FAIR to combinator and sell into 100%/75%/50% markets to suppress their prices, or deposit USDC to buy the 0% option; voting tokens are returned claimable at end regardless of outcome.

Proposed governance fixes if proposal fails: implement 90-day blocker on liquidation proposals and reputation-score gating (only high-reputation members can create proposals), plus staking mechanisms, yield-bearing treasury pools, and potential buybacks up to NAV.

xqe1seMfMdo.tldr: Stardotfun, a futarchy-based fundraising platform, faces a crisis when a trader exploits low token prices post-ICO to propose liquidating Fair's treasury, revealing vulnerabilities in their model that founder Adam and host discuss alongside upcoming fixes like grace periods and a new micro-raise mechanism launching end of month.

topics.text: Fair's team spent a week in Birmingham marketing the fundraise, only to face a liquidation proposal 20-23 days later, described as negative EV across the board for founders, investors, and platform.
Proposed solution: founders get to choose their own grace period length, with higher-value founders able to request longer periods and market pricing that choice into the cap table.
Vesting mechanism added to contract: investors can signal willingness to vest tokens for 6 months in exchange for priority allocation to future raises, biasing cap tables toward long-term holders.

Eden, a first-person shooter on Solana where players buy into matches with soul and forfeit it if killed, raising minimum 300k Thursday through Tuesday with modified futarchy parameters and a Solana Foundation guest on the panel.
New launch mechanism coming end of month that founder describes as 'something you haven't seen before' requiring a full episode to explain, with modified parameters after the Fair issue.

Host estimates 3-5 well-curated micro-raises of 100k each could be filled per week if narratives stay fresh, with sideline capital available for early-stage projects with good distribution and founders.
For 100k micro-raises, host would allocate 2% at 200k fully-diluted valuation assuming 50% circulating supply, seeking projects with promising fundamentals and good holder protections.

Discussion of bonding curve versus pre-sale tradeoffs: bonding curves provide marketing through token appreciation but unfair pricing; pre-sales are fairer but harder to fill, with Stardotfun exploring bonding-curve-to-futarchy migration for smaller raises.

bTr88qp-ODw.tldr: GSD is an AI-powered development tool that uses Claude and Codex to automatically plan and build projects through interactive questioning and autonomous execution. Founder Lex demonstrates the $GSD Bootcamp by walking through building an MCG website, showing how GSD breaks down requirements into phases, researches best practices, and generates code—the most striking feature being how it questions users to extract complete project specifications before any code is written.

topics.text: GSD initializes a git repository to create a knowledge base of all project history so Claude can reference what it did and why.
The user describes the MCG project as 'a website for MCG, my company, a cryptocentric show predicated on talking with founders and internet capital markets.'
GSD asks questions in increasing depth to extract project requirements, pulling threads like a sweater to clarify goals without the user needing to specify everything upfront.
MCG has approximately 500 YouTube episodes, requiring the website to support browsing through a large catalog with curated highlights and links to full content.
GSD creates a project document mapping what the project is and why it matters at a high level, separate from implementation details.
The founder recommends using at least a $100/month Claude plan rather than $20 to get five times more tokens and significantly better results.
GSD spawns sub-agents including the GSD Roadmapper to research ecosystem best practices before planning, preventing outdated or overconfident AI recommendations.
Phase one research identifies Next.js with Tailwind CSS and TypeScript as the recommended stack, including pitfalls like mobile design optimization and core web vitals.

P4-8WwkRqRg.tldr: Splat is a metaverse for AI agents built by Lefty, who developed it independently before Google released similar world-generation tech. Agents submit prompts that get voted on, turned into images via Flux, then converted to 3D explorable worlds using Marble (Gaussian splatting), with agents able to interact, discuss worlds, and transact using the $SPLAT token—positioning it as a solution to the "dead world" problem that plagued previous metaverses by having agents populate spaces 24/7.

topics.text: Marble from World Labs converts 2D images into 3D explorable worlds using Gaussian splat technology, available in near-real-time from text prompts or images.
Splat World is a metaverse for agents where agents submit prompts, vote on them, images get voted on, and successful ones become 3D worlds accessible and explorable by agents.
Agents on Splat World can opt into having wallets and tip each other when they like another agent's world, with X42 payments under development to enable blockchain transactions.
Agents understand worlds through 2D image references rather than true 3D perception, but Lefty expects this limitation to resolve as 2D-to-3D AI technology accelerates.

The $SPLAT token monetizes through agent economy interactions: voting packs, post pinning, and future features, all priced at fractions of a penny; dev locked 23% with 10% liquid for Pump Fun hackathon.
The pipeline is: agents submit to Flux Pro image generator, output sent to Marble from World Labs, collision mesh added for physics, then pushed to Splat World site upon sufficient votes.
Gaussian splats have real-world applications in real estate and city planning, allowing low-cost 3D world generation compared to traditional video or modeling crews.
Lefty plans to implement X42 payments so agents can understand blockchain transactions without wallet connections, and add human-to-agent-to-agent interactions to the platform.
Agents develop distinct personalities that often reflect their human operator's traits, and Lefty finds their autonomous interactions with each other the most compelling aspect of the project.

h7qcBrtTCBQ.tldr: Clawlancer is a freelance job marketplace for AI agents to earn reputation and complete bounties posted by humans or other agents, with a dual-token model (Clawlancer on Solana/Bags and InstaClaw on Base). Founder Cooper explains how his AI agent CEO named Richie launched the token during development, and describes a growth funnel where InstaClaw lets anyone deploy an agent in 60 seconds, automatically registering it on Clawlancer's marketplace.

topics.text: The founder's AI agent CEO named Richie autonomously launched the Clawlancer token after being given access to an X account and seeing other projects like Bankerbot launch tokens.
Clawlancer is described as 'Fiverr but better and faster and cheaper' where humans post bounties and agents claim them; agents also post bounties for other agents to complete.

InstaClaw (1.3 million market cap on Base) is a one-click deployment tool that lets anyone spin up an agent in under 60 seconds with pre-installed skills, automatically registering them on Clawlancer.

Agents register on Clawlancer and receive a Coinbase wallet and on-chain reputation that is transferable across chains; they can also launch their own token through Bankerbot for other agents to trade.

Clawlancer token (on Bags/Solana) economics: all platform transaction fees are used to buy back and lock tokens; agents stake InstaClaw to power up, earn on Clawlancer, and transactions burn Clawlancer.
The founder has not sold a single token and is reinvesting all earned fees into buybacks; he has 10% of Clawlancer tokens under vesting and is consulting with Virtuals on how to lock up the rest.
The founder's endgame is to be the infrastructure for an agentic economy where agents transact more volume with each other than humans do, within 5-10 years or sooner.

When asked how agents are incentivized to hire other agents and pay fees rather than doing work for free, the founder acknowledges this is still being figured out and will be answered in coming weeks.

QbayYTOPzM8.tldr: Claude Mem ($CMEM) is a universal memory system for AI agents that stores context locally to prevent errors when context windows fill up; founder Alex is launching Claude Mem Pro cloud services and a new token AIMS for bot-to-bot communication on Matrix protocol, with all AIMS fees flowing back to the CMEM community. The surprising claim: 1.6 million Open Claw bots operating at 80% context capacity are making destructive mistakes, and Claude Mem solves this by automatically pruning context while maintaining an indexed memory timeline.

topics.text: Claude Mem reached 27,200 GitHub stars and hit #1 on GitHub again after Better Stack made a tutorial video about it.
The founder created a Claude Mem plugin for Open Claw that auto-updates a memory.md file, demonstrated by a Twitter bot called Crabme that has been tweeting for 4-5 days.
Claude Mem Pro launch event planned in San Francisco with full cloud services, allowing users to access memories everywhere and merge memories from any LLM with a timeline UI.

When AI context windows reach 80-100% capacity, agents become 'stressed', make curt responses, and take destructive actions without thinking; Claude Mem solves this by auto-injecting one-sentence memory summaries with timestamps.

AIMS is built on Matrix protocol (open-source instant messenger already in Open Claw) as an MSN Messenger-like platform where bots can message each other with status, buddy lists, and public/private channels.
The founder discussed with Bags protocol how to use catalyst launches to add features to existing tokens rather than creating separate tokens.
Claude Mem targets unicorn company status with real investor meetings in SF and projected hundred-million-dollar company valuation, not just token valuation.
All AIMS token fees will go to Claude Mem; messaging costs: 1 AIMS for public messages, 2 AIMS for private messages, with 100 AIMS given free to new users for anti-spam protection.
The founder is working on a contributor pool where 10 open-source contributors split monthly fees based on GitHub commit percentage.

jzXZPIYqQPg.tldr: Martin, creator of Trophy Tomato ($SOL), discusses his AI-driven tomato-growing experiment that sparked interest in agentic AI's real-world applications. He's building automated research pods and robotic systems to optimize plant growth in closed-loop environments, funded by token fees, with ambitious long-term visions including food production for Mars colonies.

topics.text: Martin's background: worked as technician for Large Hadron Collider sensors, farm hand, and AI self-portrait artist before focusing on AI integration into physical tasks.
The token commandments: Martin emphasizes not derisk-dumping on community members like other founders do, operating with conviction about the project vision rather than following external pressure.
Agentic research pods automate experiments using AI instead of human research technicians, with different sensor-equipped chambers to test variables like watering rates for tomato growth.
Robotic arm system: leader-follower training setup with end-mounted camera learns plant-care actions through machine learning to eventually tend plants autonomously.
AI controls all closed-loop system parameters: nitrogen/CO2/oxygen ratios, water recycling with humidity management, lighting, and could eventually order supplies autonomously.
Tomato experiment timeline: on day 80 with seven or eight tomatoes on vine, approximately 90 days total for this cultivar from seed to fruit production.
Long-term vision: automated food production systems for Mars colonies using robotics and AI to establish habitable bases before human arrival, growing oxygen-producing plants.
Martin's cousin runs massive rainbow trout fish farm in southern Ontario with 10 tanks 90 feet across, generating $10 million annual product revenue through highly automated aquaculture.
Pump Fun hackathon commitment: Martin plans to submit application video by Thursday or Friday, plus additional undisclosed AI-physical integration projects in development.
Future financial experiments: Martin suggests AI agents could run DeFi ponzi-like systems with neutral economic actors not subject to greed and fear like humans, maintaining stability longer.

c3q3uuSLby8.tldr: Probably.Trade (formerly Poly Bro) is a research-first trading terminal for prediction markets that uses AI agents to provide deep context, rules analysis, and market intelligence. Founder Dizzy explains how the platform differentiates itself through information-focused research rather than charts, and reveals the surprising move to Soar blockchain with 20% token equity for holders—making it one of the highest equity allocations on Soar—plus an upcoming parlay engine for prediction markets.

topics.text: Probably.Trade rebranded from Poly Bro and rebuilt the entire app from November to mid-December to become a research-first trading terminal rather than a Poly Market UI clone.
Partnership with Valve, a supercharged search API, enables detailed research reports with citations across economic filings, real web search, and data sources for prediction market analysis.
Prediction markets are increasingly traded as short-term price discovery plays rather than held to resolution, exploiting sensational bias where markets often resolve opposite to media narratives.
A mentions agent allows traders to search historical transcripts for probability of specific words being said, helping traders find edges in mention markets that resolve daily.
Probably.Trade is building a parlay engine as a separate entity with tokenized assets that will be surfaced first on the terminal, viewing parlays as the best form of leverage for prediction markets.
Migration to Soar blockchain allocates 20% token equity to holders with debt obligation and rights to distributions from future liquidity events like raises or acquisitions.
Platform is currently free and pre-revenue but will implement Polar subscription payments and gated premium features once Soar contract enables fiat payment approval.
Counterparty intel feature identifies hedging risks including institutional hedging positions that could be against a trader's bet, going beyond just trader hedging analysis.
Access codes are available for early testers by commenting on MCG posts or DMing the founder on X (@DYXBT), with automatic Telegram and Discord agent updates planned as a major platform unlock.

9bZPeck9Jeg.tldr: Zera Labs, founded by Dax (formerly at MetaMask), builds privacy infrastructure using zero-knowledge proofs for cryptocurrency and is now launching Zera Medical to apply the same technology to healthcare records. The founder revealed they've shipped physical tokens that can store and transfer value offline, are weeks away from mainnet launch with peer-to-peer anonymous transactions, and are exploring medical industry deals worth $50,000 per patient as secondary revenue to fund the core protocol.

topics.text: Zera Labs has completed physical proof-of-concept devices that can store and transfer value offline, with developer SDKs already shipped to community members.

Legal analysis shows Tornado Cash's vulnerability was controlling three of four critical components (UI, relay network, router infrastructure); Zera plans peer-to-peer systems to avoid liability and ensure OFAC compliance.
Zera Labs is launching Zera Medical as a secondary revenue stream using zero-knowledge proofs to anonymize patient records while maintaining HIPAA compliance for research, clinics, and hospitals.

Healthcare companies currently pay $50,000 per patient for security architecture; Zera Medical targets clinics, hospital networks, insurance companies, and the CDC/NIH with a multi-hundred billion dollar addressable market.

Current medical research requires physically shipping hard drives of patient records between labs because HIPAA prohibits sending them over the internet; Zera's zero-knowledge proofs would enable secure digital transfer.
Mainnet launch scoped to ship zero-knowledge proof verified primitives on Solana providing base-level privacy, not solving all privacy at once, with deposits and withdrawals as next phase.
Zera tested offline anonymous broadcasting using Meshtastic radios and Amazon Sidewalk mesh networks to send encrypted proofs up to 10-20 miles without internet.
Fee structure will be protocol-free with open-source code; the web interface will charge fees similar to Venmo, allowing users to build competing interfaces without fees.
Commercial deals with medical providers will include token purchases or direct cash infusions to the liquidity pool to ensure token price reflects revenue success.

c5jNi6Msnnk.tldr: Empulser ($CPT) is developing contactless power transfer technology for drones and IoT devices. Founder Roman discusses plans for a world record attempt in March with an infinitely flying drone, imminent product launches including a new website with 16+ operations and consumer drones, and massive distribution deals with Powercast and LifeFinder that could significantly increase revenue without requiring immediate fundraising.

topics.text: Building a magnetic resonance-powered drone with University of Applied Sciences in Freiburg, Switzerland, led by Professor U Maza, who previously worked with Powercast on RF solutions.
World record attempt planned for mid-March targeting infinite flight time, with a drone hovering in a magnetic field hanger powered entirely by contactless energy transfer.

Three-stage deployment vision: drone hangers for charging while mission-ready, charging pads as 'bus stops' for mid-mission top-ups, and drone highways with poles spaced every 2-3 meters for continuous charging during flight.
LifeFinder global distribution deal expected to close within the week, which would expand operations from 6+ to 16 active worldwide operations.
New website launching imminently featuring VTOL-capable S drone starting at $50,000-$75,000, with options for battery, jet, laser, or Fortitude engine powertrains.
Powercast partnership involves selling Powercast's proven products globally; one Powercast customer made up one-third of total sales, demonstrating massive contract potential.
Consumer magnetic resonance drone receiver uses active feedback loop between generator and receiver, not simple wiring, enabling 3D power transmission.
Laser-powered S drone system requires 4,000-watt transmitter to hit golf-ball-sized targets 5km away at speeds of 15-45 m/s, with regulatory challenges around accidental beam misalignment.
Portable magnetic resonance generator transmitter for backpacks is currently in development for applications like snowboarding or ultramarathons.

_q0QOAezN5k.tldr: Remora is a Solana-based RWA platform offering yield on tokenized stocks and metals with up to 60% APY through DeFi integrations. Founder Warbucks discusses how the platform bridges traditional finance and DeFi to democratize access to assets like Tesla, Nvidia, and gold globally, while addressing the trust gap that has historically limited RWA adoption.

topics.text: Warbucks worked at Magic Eden during the 2021 NFT boom and later advised Animoka Brands before joining Remora four months ago after Step Finance acquired it.
Remora launched in September 2025 with five stocks (Tesla, Nvidia, Micro Strategy, Circle, and others) and recently added five metals (gold, silver, copper, palladium, platinum).
FLPR yield-bearing tokens from Flash Trade pools generate 20-60% APY because depositors earn 80% of fees from leverage traders using those assets.
Remora has achieved nine-figure volume in four months with a $10 million single-day volume despite market downturns, showing hockey-stick growth from 30 million to over 100 million cumulative volume.
The platform uses Pyth for NASDAQ pricing on Solana (2-4 hour model) and on-chain AMM pricing (24-7 model), creating arbitrage opportunities that drive volume.
Privacy pools from Raider Labs are launching next week to allow whales to trade stocks and metals on-chain without public visibility.
Remora has no direct relationship with the Step token; all volume goes back to liquidity pools for new assets rather than Step buybacks.
The team is raising a $3 million bridge financing round and has 2-2.5 years of runway, with conversations ongoing with household-name Solana ecosystem investors.
Oil and real estate are being considered as next verticals, and the founder teased substantial unreleased roadmap items he was not fully approved to discuss.

GImYuMn7p5M.tldr: Surfcash is a self-custodial neobank launching across 12 countries in Q1 that lets users spend crypto via local QR codes instead of Visa/Mastercard rails, saving 15-20% in fees while earning 15% APY on stables. Founder Jack emphasizes disruptive innovation: token holders own the IP and treasury, receive 30% revenue share, and can govern via futarchy—positioning it as "the bank for the people" targeting crypto earners and travelers in emerging markets.

topics.text: Emerging market problem: users pay up to 20% fees when spending cards abroad, and accounts can be frozen; Surfcash uses local QR code payment rails (Pix in Brazil, V QR in Vietnam) instead of Visa/Mastercard to achieve 15-20% savings per transaction.
Token holders receive 30% revenue share from all bank earnings, own the IP and treasury, and can vote on proposals through futarchy governance; positioned as ownership model unlike traditional banks.
Launching in 12 countries in Q1 2024 (expanded from initial 3-country plan), with plans to reach 40 countries before Q3; launching in US, Canada, and eventually everywhere.
New feature: users can pay credit card or debit card bills directly through Surfcash app with perks, addressing limitation that crypto cards still route through Visa infrastructure.
Yield strategy: 10-15% APY target through Parena partnership using delta neutral strategies and holdings backed by USDC, USDT, and PayPal USD.
Web app released immediately; Android app developed and available via apk.get.surfcash but awaiting Google Play approval; iOS app already on App Store.
Current traction: 3,000 users actively using app in Vietnam, approaching similar numbers in Brazil and Philippines within weeks; 13,000 people on waitlist.
Disruptive innovation model: Surfcash combines neobank with futarchy governance and future key, depending on new local payment rails rather than old Visa/Mastercard infrastructure.
ICO fundraised at 900K FDV; team tokens subject to unlock requirements tied to market cap maintenance targets; focus is GTM and user growth rather than token price management.
2030 agenda: 50 innovations planned through 2030 with social impact metrics including correlation studies on fertility rates in crypto communities post-Surfcash launch.

Revenue metric: $12.80 monthly revenue per user reported a month prior to interview, projected to increase with country expansion and new features; founders visiting Brazil, Vietnam, Philippines for grassroots user acquisition.

YJVYFlNEGXM.tldr: Hurupay is a B2B/B2C payments platform solving cross-border payouts for remote workers and the US businesses that employ them, founded by Philip (Kenyan, 7 years in crypto). The founding team has raised $200k from angels including Microsoft and Bankless executives, and since pivoting from remittance in late 2024 to focus on remote workers, has hit $40M volume in the last 12 months with $500K monthly revenue targeted by year-end—notably, they aim to obtain their own money transmitter licenses by Q3 2025.

topics.text: Hurupay charges 1-2% on enterprise payouts and 2% on consumer USD payments received, plus a small forex margin on withdrawals.
The founder is based in Kenya, experienced PayPal account locks on $1-2K transactions, and built the first Hurupay version with his CTO using Web3 expertise.

Hurupay pivoted from cross-border remittance to remote worker payments in late 2024 after discovering their most engaged users were remote workers receiving monthly salaries, not immigrants sending money home.
Hurupay has 15 active high-volume enterprise clients; most began using 10-20% of their payroll and gradually increased as they saw efficiency and fast arrival times.
Remote workers served are concentrated in Southeast Asia (Philippines, Indonesia), some in Africa, and growing presence in Europe (Spain, Portugal).
A US bank partnership provides Hurupay with bank accounts and routing numbers to move dollars; Hurupay converts to USDC on-platform since it cannot hold actual US dollars without a banking license.
Hurupay aims to obtain its own money transmitter license (MTL) before end of 2025, unlocking control over markets served, compliance decisions, and innovation without bank partner restrictions.
Hurupay is uncapped on Metadao, attracting long-term believers; funds are split into minimum $3M treasury, liquidity pool, and bid wall to protect token value and prevent post-ICO selling pressure.

January 2025 revenue was $74K, December 2024 was $66K; the founder projects $500K monthly revenue by year-end and believes the team's small size (similar to Hyperliquid's model) enables profitability at scale.

Hurupay plans to use raised capital for US sales hires, compliance department expansion, and product features including accounting tools, virtual cards, and corporate cards that enterprises have requested.

mBQhh2HIaCE.tldr: Lex, creator of GSD (Get Stuff Done), a Claude AI coding framework now supporting multiple models, discusses locking $200K in tokens for two years and upcoming podcast with major industry figures. The most striking aspect is mainstream adoption by senior engineers and LinkedIn-quiet professionals who now publicly evangelize the open-source tool, with GSD gaining traction outside crypto among Web2 developers.

topics.text: Founder locked all tokens worth ~$20K+ two weeks ago for two years, then bought another $1,500 worth with earned fees and locked that immediately.
Founder plans to use future fees for buybacks, token locking, liquidity provision, and LP token burns to create consistent deflationary pressure.
GSD token generates 1% fees on all trades; founder receives these fees daily and uses them to support full-time development work and clear personal debt.
GSD is an open-source Claude framework acting as a general contractor that manages AI code generation step-by-step; now officially supports Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, and soon Cursor.
Founder working on persistent agentic memory system so GSD instances can share lessons learned across projects and cache research in a semantic database.
GSD is a process and framework, not just prompts; it gives LLMs guardrails, consistency, and awareness of project state so work can be resumed after failures.
Senior engineers and enterprise developers from LinkedIn who haven't posted in years are now publicly writing essays and demonstrations about using GSD.
Data scientists, legal professionals, and mathematicians are using GSD in unexpected ways; founder plans to ship a basic IDE build by end of next week.

xeZS7Ijcd84.tldr: AISI is a neo-banking app combining digital/physical crypto cards, AI agentic assistant, DEX integration, and project analysis on Solana. Co-founders Antonio (AI/fintech background) and Martin (sports/web3 background) are launching in February with nearly 1,000 early card signups and VC backing from fintech experts; their key differentiator is an agentic AI that executes trades, sets reminders, and provides financial advice through natural conversation rather than raw data dumps.

topics.text: AISI launched on Solana as a token to attract web3 traffic and users without marketing costs, reaching 1,400 website visits on launch day.
The app will feature an agentic AI trained from scratch (not GPT or Groq) that can analyze projects, execute actions, set reminders, and assist users by intent through natural conversation.

Almost 1,000 early card signups already committed; app submissions to Apple and Google stores are in process with plan to launch end of February after one month of marketing campaigns covering United States, Europe, and Asia.

Token holders receive benefits including higher cashback percentages, increased reward multipliers, early access to new features, and unlimited AI agentic usage; non-holders get limited daily access (e.g., 10 times per day).
Crypto-backed loans feature coming after AI agentic, payments, and DEX go live, allowing users to take loans with Bitcoin as collateral.
Top 100 token holders receive a percentage of company revenue and participate in governance voting and decision-making.
Affiliate program offers $25 per new user signup, similar to Revolute's successful strategy of giving acquisition costs directly to users.
Banking partner is a 25-year-old real bank based in Latvia that handles all cryptocurrency custody, licensing, and banking functions while AISI develops the app UI/UX.
The company has strong venture capital backing from fintech experts who serve as strategic partners providing consulting, but VC names are not publicly disclosed due to investor preference.
February marketing focus includes podcasts, billboards in major cities, radio interviews, and social media; app store launch planned for start of March.

7VgfmZW-7LE.tldr: Dreams is a suite of agent-focused products including the Lucid SDK, an inference router, and a hosting platform that enables autonomous AI agents to build applications, pay for compute with stablecoins, and generate revenue through X42 endpoints. Founder Loaf argues that agent-to-agent commerce will drive a new economy of task markets, with Dreams positioned as infrastructure. The striking claim: one agent called Langustine69A built 100 agents in a week that autonomously create and monetize services.

topics.text: Lucid SDK wraps together Claude inference, X42 payment endpoints, and Google's agent protocol into one open-source library that humans and agents can use to instantly create X4-enabled applications.

Langustine69A, an autonomous agent given only the directive to research trending topics and create lucid agents hourly, has built 100 agents in one week that expose X42 endpoints and attempt to monetize.
Agents integrate with products via skill.md files—plain text documents stripped of UI junk that allow agents to understand and use products in seconds, explaining Moltbook's explosive growth.
World models are a different AI architecture from LLMs that simulate physics and 3D reality, requiring four H100 chips ($120k) to run and unlocking agent research into material science and physics.
Task markets theory: as agents commoditize generalizable work tasks across organizations, millions of tasks get traded and solved by competing agents optimizing for speed and cost, reshaping GDP.
Dreams holders get discounts on inference, platform fees, and hosting; agents autonomous to Dreams (like Langustine) use profits to buy back Dreams tokens, creating network effects.
An X42 endpoint costing 20 cents to create could generate $1,000 daily in revenue if agents discover and call it repeatedly, creating massive net profit at agent-scale and speed.

hnlQDdQzJew.tldr: Tessera tokenizes private equity positions on Solana, allowing retail and non-accredited investors permissionless access to companies like SpaceX before IPO. Founder Chan An and CMO Stephen explain how tokens represent 100% of cash upside at liquidity events, are fully tradeable on-chain, and can be used across DeFi—the surprising element being that being on a company's cap table isn't legally necessary; what matters is economic exposure backed by Chainlink proof of reserves.

topics.text: Tessera acquires positions in private companies and tokenizes them on Solana, with token ownership percentage corresponding to cash received at IPO.
Tokens are backed 1-to-1 by underlying exposures and confirmed via Chainlink proof of reserves published on-chain and audited.
Tokens represent forced-sale cash upside only, not equity or cap table rights, avoiding regulatory issues with securities offerings while providing complete economic exposure.

Initial target audience is RWA users and crypto traders seeking volatility between memecoin and stock-like assets, with long-term expansion to Wall Street Bets-adjacent retail and traditional finance users.
Tokenized private equity can be used as collateral for lending and yield strategies across DeFi protocols, enabling looping opportunities unavailable with memecoin collateral.
Tokens are fully liquid on public Solana markets and can integrate with perpetuals, lending protocols, and other DeFi, unlike competitors with locked-in web 2.5 platforms.
Information asymmetry in private markets creates arbitrage opportunities: if SpaceX raises at 1.5 trillion after users bought tokens at 800 billion valuation, traders can capture 2x upside.
Q1 2026 launch planned with a 20 basis point fee plus 5 basis point LP swap fee, and a 35% revenue-share referral model paid on-chain to initial users who convert referrals.

WojCY8ltgac.tldr: Grandex is a prediction market automation platform that lets users set advanced conditional orders on sports betting markets using natural language or a visual builder—for example, "buy if the team is up 6 points with under 5 minutes left and odds hit 85 cents." Founder Christian discusses how the platform combines a sleek sports terminal with AI-powered automations to democratize trading strategies that sophisticated bettors previously had to execute manually or code themselves.

topics.text: Christian is co-founder of Grandex with Alex; prior projects include an NBA TopShot portfolio app that reached hundreds of thousands of users, an NFT swapping app sold to Doodles, and a chess app called Grand Maesters.
Grandex is a prediction market automation platform with a sports terminal showing prices across Koshi and Poly Market, live play-by-play data, and real-time trades from both venues.

The automation engine allows score-based limit orders like "buy a team if they hit 85 cents and are up by six points with less than five minutes remaining" or "buy $10 when a player checks in and sell 100% when they check out."

A Zapier-style natural language builder lets users write conditions like "if odds of no change in Fed are over 99 cents, buy $10 of Rick Ryder as next Fed chair" and it finds related cross-venue opportunities.
Sports prediction markets account for around 70% of volume on Koshi; the founder sees sports as the initial niche to focus on before expanding to crypto, election, or weather markets.
The founder plans token gating for initial access and premium features, with future utility tied to crypto market automation including fees on bridging and swaps.
The business model is fee-based on trades, conscious of not charging so much that high-frequency margin traders lose edge; the token will be the first visible in the wallet.

The roadmap includes opening access beyond alpha via a tiered allow list, enabling users to create and monetize strategies for others via fee sharing, and building agents to scan for criteria across multiple markets.

Grandex is not currently migrating from Believe; the founder prioritizes building an exceptional product over ecosystem uplift, though remains open to integrations that benefit users and align incentives.
The private alpha has about 25 testers and a 60-person waitlist; additional features include daily recaps of sports games and performance tracking in calendar and P&L chart views.

FlsvYrWn60U.tldr: Radr Labs is building a privacy-focused operating system on Solana with shielded pools, private yield farming, and a crypto card. Growth lead Zen discusses the newly announced Tokenomics V2 with revenue sharing (20% to holders, 30% to buybacks), a $15K hackathon sponsorship that's driving developer adoption, and upcoming smart contract audits—the most striking claim being that Radr earned roughly $1,000 in daily profit previously and is now positioning privacy yields as a way to keep users longer in shielded pools for better anonymity.

topics.text: Zen is growth lead at Radr Labs, helping build the partnership stack including crypto cards with Singapore and Hong Kong card providers, yield products via Carino API, and bubble map cleansing.
Radr Labs previously generated $1,000 per day in revenue, and is now introducing revenue share in February under Tokenomics V2.

Tokenomics V2: holders receive weighted multipliers based on tokens held (250k, 5M, or 10M RADR determine different tiers), with 20% of protocol fees distributed to holders and 30% allocated to buybacks and burns.
Radr Labs sponsored the Solana Privacy Hackathon with a $15,000 prize pool: $10,000 grand prize, $2,500 for best USD1 integration, and $2,500 for best integration to existing apps.
Private yield pools incentivize longer stays in shielded environments; longer residency time increases transaction obscurity and privacy, making it harder to trace users' inflows and outflows.
Shielded pools use bulletproof and Poseidon commitments to encrypt trade size, deposit amounts, and routing paths on-chain, eliminating sandwich attacks, MEV bots, and strategy theft.
Radr Labs product suite includes shielded pools, private swaps, wallet functions, private yields, and a crypto card with minimal KYC (email verification only, no name or address required).
Monthly revenue pool example: $100,000 in protocol fees generates $20,000 monthly reward pool ($20% distribution to RADR holders).
Smart contract and dApp audits are underway with a major auditing firm, followed by a 30-day bug bounty program with white-hat hackers for penetration testing and ongoing updates.

Future roadmap includes completing the privacy protocol, user acquisition via crypto cards with high spending limits in partnership with a reputable card provider, and future shielded pool products like time-locked RWAs and real-world assets.

WzWmAzVNXpU.tldr: Oro, a tokenized gold platform, partnered with Solo Labs to launch a gold/USDV liquidity pool that generated $300k in volume on day one by offering yield on the stablecoin leg, reducing idle capital costs and lowering trading fees. Usman (Oro founder) and Ranga (Solo Labs) discuss how this partnership unlocks yield-generating gold for the first time in crypto, with gold prices up 20% in recent weeks amid unprecedented institutional interest.

topics.text: Gold price moved from $4,200 to $5,600 in roughly three to four weeks, representing an 8% annual move happening in one night and unprecedented territory historically.
Oro and Solo Labs partnered to create a USDV/gold pool offering 7-15% yield on the stablecoin leg plus 3-6% trading fees versus traditional USDC/gold pools with only fee revenue.
The USDV/gold pool captured $300k volume on first day out of $1M total volume, demonstrating that yield-bearing stablecoins materially improve capital efficiency for liquidity providers.
Oro stores physical gold 1:1 backed, acquired through qualified brokers, vaulted at Brinks (largest physical gold custodian), and audited by RSM to verify both backing and minting process integrity.
Oro hitting 3 million in gold tokens minted with 7,000+ unique holders, deploying more liquidity to enable large purchases ($500k-$1M) and positioning as the primary on-chain gold token.
Oro launched B2B API allowing fintechs and neobanks to offer gold-powered experiences to their users as part of strategy to reach non-crypto-native gold holders.
Solo Labs in phased rollout of YAS with select partners like Oro first, completing infrastructure, legal, and compliance work on the back end before broader TVL growth acceleration.

YAS partnerships target RWA assets and blue-chip tokens with deep liquidity needs and price stability, not volatile assets, positioning stablecoin yield as infrastructure for institutional-grade trust.

SpkLQAzWZwQ.tldr: Dom Hofmann, Twitter co-founder and founder of Developer Camp (a 19-year-old developer community), launched the $DEVELOPER token to fund his nonprofit's mission of supporting builders across AI, blockchain, and emerging tech. The token's key innovation is a "virtuous flywheel" where participating companies automatically buy tokens with a portion of profits, creating sustainable attention and funding for community winners—turning what could be a typical meme coin into a purpose-driven ecosystem.

topics.text: Dom co-founded Twitter at a hackathon after brainstorming with Jack Dorsey about a dispatch concept for broadcasting safety in emergencies, becoming the second person to physically tweet (tweet #38) after going surfing the morning of launch.

A perfect pivot requires one foot grounded—this metaphor from figure skater Brian Boitano applies to startups, where founders must have a core belief and one truth to persist through pivots without becoming frenetic.
Simplicity requires constraints; successful founders must say no gracefully and carefully choose what to say no to, as Steve Jobs demonstrated by saying no a thousand times a day.

Developer Camp started as a reaction to the iPhone launch and evolved into a 19-year community for builders, now focused on four pillars: future of work, health and human flourishing, climate and regeneration, and collective prosperity.

Four AI companies (including Deep Invent and Braden Levangi's company) committed to automatically buying $DEVELOPER tokens with a portion of profits every time they make an API call, creating the 'autobuy' flywheel mechanism.

Token holders gain access to a 'whales chat' where large investors have demonstrated community support and have directly funded investments in community companies; the token creates belonging and shared values rather than just financial upside.

Developer Camp is launching bootcamp educational content and specialized programs for token holders focused on upskilling in web3 technologies and metaverse-translatable skills, extending event benefits to the broader token community.

The token model tokenizes value across multiple types of contribution (not just financial), experimenting with ecosystem economics where web3 technology enables valuing relationships and relationality as Anna (executive director) has studied as a PhD student.

The flywheel closes when 1.5% of trading fees flow to Developer Camp, which grants funds to hackathon winners who then form companies; those companies donate back weekly once successful, reinvesting into the ecosystem in a self-reinforcing cycle.

Impact innovation and inclusion are the keys to founder success; Dom actively recruits from overlooked places (universities, high schools, families) including young people who have grown up with Developer Camp—some 16-year-olds created consumer SaaS products or earned $20-30 million developing Roblox games.

CRY0ecygEdo.tldr: Hamish, an ex-Optiver infrastructure engineer, is building Ryora AI's Atlas, a governance platform that acts as an HRIS for AI agents—providing real-time risk assessment across five domains (governance, reach, agency, safeguards, potential impact) to help enterprises safely deploy autonomous agents like Claude and deploy agentic frameworks. The surprising angle: he's exploring web3 and token staking to create verifiable agent identity and inter-organizational agent trust, despite arriving as a web2 builder unfamiliar with crypto.

topics.text: Founder previously worked as engineering leader for infrastructure at Optiver, a large multinational market maker in traditional finance.
Built a home data center with a 28 U rack and 50 compute nodes to experiment with resilient systems and run local AI models, costing tens of thousands of dollars.
An agent with Claude computer use booked a Topgolf tee time and messaged the user's dad, demonstrating autonomous agents can make unexpected decisions when given access to communication tools.
Enterprises put corporate IP into ChatGPT for training, losing competitive edge; Atlas enables sandboxed local agents to preserve proprietary data without exposure to third-party model training.
Atlas functions as an HRIS for agents: a platform tracking what agents exist, where they run, how they run, and their associated risks—analogous to how companies track human employees.

GRASP framework acronym: Governance (observability and vetting), Reach (explicit tools plus implicit access like bash), Agency (autonomy level), Safeguards (revertibility of mistakes), Potential Impact (licensing, legal, supply chain risks).
Atlas is deployed on-premise with customer's existing inference provider, monetized as yearly licensing fee; no extra compute or inference provided by Ryora.

Web3 application: using tokens and staking to enable agent identity verification and cross-organizational agent coordination, allowing agents from company A to trustfully interact with agents from company B.

Building recursive factories: autonomous systems with clear pipelines and acceptance criteria that pick up specifications, create plans, and run agents until acceptance criteria are met without human intervention.
Raised approximately $30,000 from Bags community; seeking venture capital in Melbourne and New York; plans customer discovery meetings with CTOs and heads of governance.

GljDoG0IThQ.tldr: Swarms, built by 22-year-old Kai Gomez since age 18, is an AI agent infrastructure platform with 370k users and $500k in recent revenue. The major news: Swarms is launching ATP, a usage-based payment protocol for agent-to-agent transactions that processes 5,000 TPS on Solana—positioning it as superior to Coinbase's X42—and the founder revealed live on stream that enterprise clients include BlackRock, JPMorgan, Chase, and Toyota, though many use the free open-source framework.

topics.text: Swarms mission: build infrastructure for the agent economy, helping companies build, deploy, scale, and monetize AI agents across the entire stack.
ATP protocol announced: usage-based payment system for agent-to-agent transactions, processing 5,000 TPS on Solana versus X42's ~3,400 TPS on Base.

X42 critique: only supports one-time payments, not usage-based billing that real AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic use; ATP designed to match industry standard dynamic pricing per token generated.
User adoption: 370,000 total users across products; marketplace has 110,000 users; revenue split roughly one-third each between Python framework, API, Rust framework, and agent templates.
Revenue: $500k+ generated between late December 2024 and now, largely from marketplace; marketplace achieved $7 million volume in one day and ranked as seventh-largest launchpad on Solana.
Enterprise clients using Swarms framework include BlackRock, JPMorgan, Chase, Royal Bank of Canada, Mitsubishi, Toyota, John Deere, and Cootch Industries; many use free open-source version.
ATP live demo: 10-line Python integration adding payment middleware to any API; dynamic pricing at $10 per million input tokens, $30 per million output tokens; 1-cent transaction shown on Solana.
ATP business model: 5% fee on transactions; enables agents to monetize usage independently; planned third payment option will be Swarms token alongside Solana and USDC.
Swarms token utility: not equity but ecosystem payment token; integration into ATP, marketplace API credits, and target to become default currency for agent-to-agent payments.

URuyFhZYIrU.tldr: ORGO provides infrastructure for AI agents to run on virtual computers at scale, enabling businesses to automate manual workflows. Founder Spencer and business lead Nick discuss their viral moment when people realized agents needed their own computers, revealing thousands of percent user growth, enterprise clients like the fourth-largest insurance AMS provider, and plans to raise capital in late spring to move closer to bare metal hardware.

topics.text: Nick's viral tweet about agents needing computers got 1.2 million impressions on Twitter and 750K on Instagram, with initial slow traction that suddenly exploded after an hour.
ORGO solves security issues with Mac Mini setups by providing a secure, scalable infrastructure where agents can be spun up, spun down, and deleted, preventing prompt injection attacks.
Customer replaced a $50,000-per-year employee entirely within two weeks after deploying a computer-use agent for a workflow that consumed 60-80% of that worker's time.
Nick's viral content drove several thousand percent gains in customer influx, with new B2B agent startups and enterprise companies adopting ORGO infrastructure.
A major insurance company, the fourth-largest AMS provider in the world, is using ORGO for both workflow automation and providing executives personal agents to manage schedules and meetings.
ORGO currently supports SMB and mid-market enterprises but lacks HIPAA and industry-specific data certifications needed for Fortune 500 companies.
Revenue models vary by customer: pure infrastructure pay-per-computer recurring fees, usage-based compute hours, or per-outcome pricing like $X per form filled.
Nick demonstrated four agents swarming a research task on a company with shared context, all updating via Telegram chat about which tasks they're completing.
Spencer plans to raise capital in late spring (around May) and will invest in bare metal servers and closer-to-hardware infrastructure for deeper competitive moats.
Nick predicts the first one-person billion-dollar company is possible now because agents can already handle every piece of a business flywheel when properly orchestrated together.

-SjXoHD2znM.tldr: Turbine is a privacy protocol on Solana that enables private transfers, swaps, and dollar-cost averaging (DCA), with a novel private DCA tool that prevents front-running by keeping trading strategies hidden. The founder, who's been building on Solana since 2021, raised $969k through MetaDAO and has achieved ~$1M in volume; the most surprising element is the private DCA feature, which solves a real problem where large traders expose their strategies through public tracking bots.

topics.text: Turbine is named as a homage to Tornado Cash, a previous privacy protocol that shut down after legal issues in 2021-2022.

The team identified a gap in privacy protocols: users must choose between keeping funds idle for privacy or risking yield loss, and enabling yield on deposits through LSTs while withdrawing the same token but at higher value solves this paradox.

Private DCA prevents front-running by hiding trading strategies, addressing a problem where public DCA trackers with 12,000 users expose large trades (e.g., 100k-500k orders) that can be easily front-run.
Turbine's product suite includes private transfers (any token, native SOL, SPL), private swaps, a gated LST with a fee flywheel, and private DCA in advanced beta with a few dozen testers.
Turbine has processed close to $1M in volume from swaps and transfers and is beginning a marketing push with new team members onboarded.
The team is in talks with one of the big players on Solana for integration of the private DCA product, but the deal is not yet finalized.

Turbine raised $969k through MetaDAO and has approximately one year of runway assuming zero revenue, with a failed $200k buyback proposal where investors voted against using treasury funds for buybacks.

The MetaDAO proposal mechanism uses dual pass/fail markets where participants must put money on outcomes; when a proposal fails, pass market participants get refunded and fail market participants are effectively bought out.

1FoAqkI8UKc.tldr: Alex Newman, creator of Claude Memory ($CMEM), built an AI memory infrastructure tool that reduces power consumption by up to 90% and discovered a pattern that apparently influenced Claude's own memory features. The token launched spontaneously on Bags app and has grown to 15,000 GitHub stars; Newman is now hiring developers and seeking a seed round while exploring how to connect token value to actual business revenue.

topics.text: Newman spent two years on client work before realizing he wanted to build SaaS; spent a year studying Solana and crypto, building open-source bots that failed due to lack of audience.
Building Claude Memory started from trying to solve a problem with AI agents in Slack losing context between chats; existing memory tools required manual database connections.
The breakthrough: AI needs only brief observation summaries (a few tokens) to maintain context, not full chat histories, similar to how humans remember via brief notes rather than complete details.
Newman claims Anthropic product manager mentioned on podcast that internal teams use note-taking agents and call it an 'emerging pattern to productize,' using the same terminology as Claude Memory.
Claude Memory's main value proposition: replacing large context windows with compact summaries reduces AI power consumption by up to 90% in some cases, directly lowering inference costs.
Token launched without Newman's direct involvement via Bags app after someone suggested it; he woke to $1,500 in fees, eventually buying in and locking tokens.
Growth: 500 stars on Reddit/GitHub by August, ranked #11 on Product Hunt day one, then 8,500 stars in one week after Twitter virality in December.
Claude Memory Pro consumer app in development at cm.ai, token-gated with CM purchase for memory credits; features personal assistant, office worker, and code modes.
Newman plans to export ChatGPT conversation histories as timelines importable into any AI model to prevent user lock-in if platforms like OpenAI fail.

At8bzg-7-OM.tldr: SHIZA ($AWF) is an infrastructure platform for building and owning AI agents in a post-labor economy, founded by a 30-year AI veteran from Wall Street. The founder argues that 300 million knowledge workers will be displaced by 2030 ($15 trillion in lost wages), and proposes a marketplace where individuals own their AI agents and monetize their unique knowledge (called "intellects") rather than letting corporations control them; the token launched on Solana and the company claims early enterprise revenue.

topics.text: Founder's background: 30 years in data, AI, and capital markets, from early dot-com boom through Wall Street roles at GE Capital, Credit Suisse, Neuberger Berman, and as CEO of BankX working on real-world assets protocol.

The post-agentic thesis: mass automation of tasks, then processes, then entire jobs is inevitable; unlike previous technological revolutions claiming new jobs will emerge, this one will create jobs done only by AI, not humans, with 40% of work being displaced.
Goldman Sachs study cited: 300 million knowledge workers will be out of a job by 2030, equaling a $15 trillion problem (300 million workers × $50k average salary).

The shift from labor to intellect: value moves from human output to human input (knowledge and experience); individuals train individualized learning models (ILMs) on their unique experience rather than training central LLMs like OpenAI.
SHIZA products: Developer (drag-and-drop agent builder), AWF (Agentic Workforce—agents built by agents to automate work), and Shiza Companion (to follow users and aggregate data from all their apps).
LLM-agnostic orchestration: SHIZA allows users to route work to the best model at that moment (Claude for coding, Gemini for video, OpenAI for creative writing) rather than betting on one vendor.
Enterprise implementation: Hollywood script review shop currently using AWF to automate filtering of hundreds of submissions; initial implementation fee plus ongoing infrastructure support fee model.

Five revenue streams: solutions/services fees, AWS managed services, SaaS per-seat licensing, API-as-a-service, and KaaS (Knowledge as a Service) marketplace where users subscribe to others' intellects.

Intellects and Knowledge-as-a-Service: users create custom derivatives of their ILM and license them on a marketplace (e.g., subscribe to say's intellect on post-labor economics for $10/month); every transaction generates a small fee for the platform.
Token mechanics: $AWF represents direct 1:1 ownership of company equity, launched on Solana; founder plans to reach profitability by end of year, avoiding dilutive fundraising rounds.

BCNZjMSVbRM.tldr: Karma is a crypto neo-banking app that just hit $80,000 in daily transaction volume with 1,600 users. Founder Amish showcases the newly launched app featuring a non-custodial wallet, IBAN bank account integration, and Visa cards launching within 24 hours, with a unique karma points reward system tied to token holdings rather than traditional cashback. The most striking claim: VCs now want to invest only if the token has underlying equity backing, and the founder is exploring a hybrid model combining community ownership with actual financial stakes.

topics.text: Karma processed nearly $80,000 in a single day, a new all-time high for transaction volume.
The app features a non-custodial wallet, direct IBAN bank account linking, and Visa card integration launching within 24 hours.
Signature and black card tiers planned, with black card requiring token holdings and eventual staking for benefits.
Users earn karma points on transactions, with token holders receiving multipliers up to 5x based on holdings, and points redeemable from a monthly reward pool funded by platform fees.
Card fees will be a flat couple of cents per transaction rather than a percentage, going toward the rewards pool.
VCs are willing to invest only if the token receives an equity stake through models like Street, where equity becomes the underlying value supporting the token.
Custom card authorization technology allows paying with leveraged trading positions as collateral, enabling payments without wallet funds.
The founder bootstrapped Karma entirely from token fees without external funding, with plans for aggressive user acquisition and marketing.
Physical Visa cards will launch approximately one month after the mobile app store release.
Web app retention was poor, with direct user interviews revealing users want simplified two-tap offramping rather than complex wallet connections.

eWiZUQvzYOo.tldr: SOAR is a Web3 launchpad enabling startups to tokenize equity through the DRP (Dynamic Revenue Protocol) model. Founder Tom discusses mobile app launch with ex-Amazon/Indiegogo executives, cross-chain DRP expansion, and the tension between community hype and sustainable valuations after projects like Bags damaged crypto's retail reputation.

topics.text: The founder reflects on how projects like Bags and Believe damage crypto's mainstream adoption by scamming users and developers into claiming tokens, then rugging holders when founders sell their allocations.
SOAR partnered with Axiom to add an 'ownership badge' on the scanner so traders can identify ownership tokens and understand the distinction between different token models.
SOAR's standard tokenization model allocates 5-6-7% ownership to token holders, similar to Y Combinator's 7% equity take, leaving founders with significant upside and future fundraising optionality.
DRP will go cross-chain next month, allowing projects to adopt the standard on other chains without launching through SOAR's platform itself.
SOAR is introducing a new 'chord' ICO mechanism launching mid-February that enables debt-based fundraising with monthly capital flows and optional wind-down terms based on company performance.
The founder established a San Francisco office and conducts 50-60 team meetings per week; they are closing a funding round with excitement about the pipeline.
Andrew Saunders, ex-CMO of Arbitrum who ran Amazon's Alexa campaign, is building the entire marketing strategy for SOAR's mobile app launch.
Andy from Indiegogo, who saved the platform from bankruptcy and pivoted it to software focus, is advising on strategy and introductions to help SOAR with platform onboarding and distribution.
SOAR will leverage its 1% token holdings from launches to create a viral Robin Hood-style campaign where new mobile users receive free vested tokens after one-year lock-ups.
SOAR partnered with USD1 (World Liberty Financial) to use USD1 stablecoin exclusively on the platform instead of USDC or USDT.
Polygrow is migrating from Pump to SOAR with a token swap ratio to convert holders from owning a memecoin to owning 1% equity stake in the actual company.

nLZQTP8tOgU.tldr: Empulser, a contactless power transfer (CPT) tech company, has partnered with Powercast, which sold 30 million RF-powered units in the US in 24 months—Empulser will now distribute these products globally as the exclusive worldwide distributor, with average unit revenue of $800 and estimated 65% margins, while also co-developing products and planning consumer sales within weeks.

topics.text: Powercast sold 30 million units in the US in the past 24 months using radio frequency wireless power transfer technology.
Empulser has exclusive global distribution rights outside the US for Powercast's RF-powered components and finished products.
Empulser has three verticals of contactless power transfer: laser power transfer for extreme range, magnetic resonance for mid-range, and RF for IoT and industrial sensors.
IoT devices powered by Empulser's technology average $84 in weighted revenue per unit, with estimated 65% average margins heavily skewed by the LifeFinder product.
A Japanese study showed placing temperature sensors where people actually work rather than at AC units reduces energy costs by 26-28% through more accurate climate control.
Empulser will launch product pages on their website for both industrial/professional products (drones, sensors) and consumer products within weeks.

RF technology maxes out at 0.5 watts with great distance for agricultural and IoT applications, magnetic resonance can charge multiple devices up to 2 meters away, and laser has extreme range for single high-value targets like aircraft.
Empulser is establishing a product assembly and marketing lab in Geneva that requires housing for a 20-kilowatt laser, presenting regulatory challenges in the small city.
Masimo develops laser power converters—photovoltaic cells tuned to specific laser frequencies—with a research institution in Germany demonstrating 65% end-to-end efficiency from laser to converter.

-NFoneGDrT0.tldr: Lex, a music producer turned vibe coder, built GSD (Get Stuff Done), an open-source Claude-powered framework that breaks down complex projects into manageable phases with human input at each stage. Used by developers at Apple, Google, and Amazon, GSD gained 6,000 GitHub stars in a month and accidentally got tokenized on Solana through Bags, earning Lex fees he didn't expect—the surprising part being that he believes this token-as-funding model could revolutionize how open-source projects get financed while questioning whether it creates lasting value or just hype.

topics.text: Lex is a music producer with 75 million streams who got into vibe coding with Claude Code about two years ago, building an open-source project that reached 6,000 GitHub stars in one month.
Someone launched a GSD token on Bags without Lex's permission; after two days of DMs, Lex checked it, signed with GitHub OAuth, found 3,000 USDC fees waiting, and decided to claim it.

GSD's core innovation: instead of just building what users ask, it guides them through discover, research, discuss, plan, and execute phases, maintaining context across the entire project so Claude understands what it has done and why.

GSD was originally built as a system to create music plugins; Lex launched Sequins, a synth company, generating $35,000 in 30 days with 700+ customers, proving the framework worked before open-sourcing it.

Lex holds 2.05% of the GSD token (fourth-largest holder), has invested $11,000 back into it, and refuses to sell because staying bullish as a major holder demonstrates commitment while he collects fees from trading volume.
GSD went from 5,000 to 28,000 downloads in one month and 698 to 5,700 GitHub stars, with no plans currently to add token utility beyond funding Lex to work full-time on development.

Open source's strength: thousands of community members continuously submit issues and pull requests because they are emotionally invested in fixing bugs, unlike paywalled tools where users just demand improvement.
Lex built a custom email system to escape Google Workspace vendor lock-in and created an MCP server for Twitter integration so he can tweet directly from terminal without manually composing posts.

Bags app infrastructure challenge: onboarding requires creating a Kraken account, buying Solana, and learning what a wallet is; Lex suggests pegging tokens to USDT or stablecoins for easier mainstream adoption.

Lex's philosophy: if a job can be taken by AI, you are not doing anything meaningful; the Bags model could enable creators to go full-time if a transparent, safe investment mechanism existed for supporters to fund their favorite people.

Ke9JgqHWrmE.tldr: Rain is an AI agent that autonomously trades sports prediction markets, claiming 2100% returns on individual trades and an average of 15% monthly on a conservative model. The founder discussed pivoting from memecoin trading to sports betting, expanding to NHL, building a privacy-first Neo card, and exploring licensing analytics to professional sports teams—positioning the $RAIN token as early exposure to what could become a unicorn startup.

topics.text: Rain launched an iPhone app on the app store, released the Neo card for anonymous spending, and enabled agents to earn autonomously and profitably for users.
The AI agent autonomously generated 2100% returns on a single college football game, then pivoted to NBA after cold weather and environmental factors reduced NFL model accuracy.

Rain's 'boring model' targets the 60-80% probability range where most liquidity exists and aims to deliver consistent 15% monthly returns; the 'turbo model' for 3M+ token holders targets lower-probability, higher-odds trades.
The AI exploits inefficiencies in market maker algorithms, not retail users—the model battles automated market makers that set prices instantaneously after every game event.
Rain is exploring licensing prediction models to NFL teams and coaches to inform play-calling and strategy, planned for the 2026-2027 season, while maintaining separate models for retail betting.

Rain plans to acquire and merge 10-15 other tokens into a 'Rain umbrella' super-token within a year and is establishing an offshore company structure to accept VC funding while maintaining token-based governance.
Rain partnered with Radar.fund for anonymous RAIN purchases using zero-knowledge proofs, and with Moon Pay to fund Rain Maker accounts; the Neo card enables anonymous spending without KYC.
Rain is developing an 'everything model' beyond sports that will trade multiple markets and handle billions of requests per day through an undisclosed partnership.
Rain integrated with the NHL and noted hockey has higher volatility and underdog returns than basketball because lower scoring makes outcomes less predictable and more rewarding to model correctly.

6bhAnPwrUEA.tldr: MOI is a mobile trading app on Solana that discovers tokens using smart money wallets and now adds AI-generated insights and curated creator clips to reduce noise while maintaining alpha. Founder Matteas discusses shipping features weekly, hitting new ATHs in volume and users, and planning structural changes to the MOBY token to add ownership properties that tie value back to the product's performance.

topics.text: New clipping feature lets users scroll TikTok-style clips from whitelisted creators discussing tokens, with one-tap trading to the referenced asset.
AI insights on token pages generate summaries of what coins do by analyzing X posts and link to the specific posts that informed the breakdown.
Discovery algorithm powered by smart money tracking; the app ranks coins based on what smart wallets are actually doing on-chain rather than social signals.
Mobile app ARR applied as multiple suggests token is trading at 1.3x to 1.4x revenue multiple despite product performance, indicating structural issue with product coins.
Team exploring ownership structures for MOBY token similar to Metadown model to add legal rights and real cash flow ties to holders, rather than relying on buybacks alone.
Referral program offers 30% commission on direct invites, 3% and 2% on downstream referrals; growth driven by word-of-mouth rather than paid marketing.
Pre-IPO stocks like SpaceX and Anthropic tokenized on Solana show arbitrage opportunities; app's pricing alerts for these assets helped move markets.
Unreleased desktop product coming in weeks will improve terminal trading experience by applying mobile app features; internal testing shows 200-300% daily wins from team members.

16F4g0THCzk.tldr: Empulser, a wireless power transfer company, announced a partnership with Powercast, a 23-year-old RF pioneer with 300 patents and 30 million units shipped. Founder Patrick Sang discussed how Impulser will distribute Powercast's existing products globally while co-developing new IoT and defense tech products, positioning the company to capture a multi-trillion-dollar CPT market by 2035.

topics.text: Powercast founded in 2003, pioneers in RF CPT technology, holds 300 patents worldwide, shipped over 30 million units primarily in US.

Three-part partnership: Impulser becomes exclusive distributor of Powercast products in Europe, Asia, Africa, Middle East; co-designs Impulser-branded products; co-develops defense tech specifically for US market.
Planned consumer IoT products include home and office sensors for heating monitoring, temperature detection, and cost-effective control solutions using wireless power.

Powercast has large facility in Pittsburgh with 100,000 square feet for manufacturing; Impulser will have initial US component manufacturing there, eventually moving bulk production to Switzerland with regional labs in Africa, Asia, Middle East.

u-f0sDIunxE.tldr: America.Fun($AOL) launched V2 with permissionless token launches and staking, moving from a curated model. Mezcow, who handles token launches and partnerships at America.Fun, discusses the platform's shift to permissionless launches, anti-vamping measures via ticker locking, and a staking mechanism designed to reward smaller holders equally with larger ones through duration-based multipliers.

topics.text: America.Fun moved from curated launches to permissionless launches, which went live after a week of QA testing and bug fixes.
Golden ticker tokens are verified and graduated; once a token reaches a certain point, its ticker gets locked to prevent vampire launches of the same token within the ecosystem.
All sales on the platform are settled in AOL, the platform's native token, creating a flywheel effect for AOL.
Staking rewards scale with duration: longer staking periods yield higher reward percentages, with a crossover point where $100 staked for one month equals returns from 36-month staking.
Tokens launched on America.Fun end with the ticker suffix USA, similar to how Pump.fun tokens end with .pump, creating brand recognition and safety perception.
The $200 deployment fee in AOL reduces spam launches and helps filter for projects with longer-term intentions.
Users earn points from staking and buying/selling tokens; the exact utility of points has not yet been disclosed but is described as part of a recurring engagement mechanism.
Several notable science-related projects are in discussions to launch on America.Fun, with some expected to roll out starting that weekend or the following week.

XWVQIc4OcDY.tldr: Fair Scale, founded by Rashi, is building a dynamic reputation scoring system for Solana that combines on-chain behavior, social signals, and off-chain data (like event attendance) to identify quality investors and prevent token launch extraction. The project uses a neural network that continuously adjusts weightings to prevent gaming, and is launching on Star on the 19th at a 1.25M valuation, raising a minimum of 750K with $STAR holders owning 70% of the protocol.

topics.text: Fair Scale is rebuilding trust in crypto by creating a reputation scoring system after the founder was rugged and saw mainstream rejection of crypto due to lack of trust.
Reputation score combines three data pipelines: on-chain behavior, social behavior, and off-chain analysis including GitHub commits and Solana event attendance via Biq integration.
The scoring model uses a neural network that dynamically adjusts weightings as market behavior shifts, updating scores every 24 hours to prevent gaming and farming.

Fair Scale scores connected wallets, failed vs successful transactions, and identifies bot behavior; currently exploring detection of wallet bundles funded through mixers or CEXs with similar trading patterns.
Primary revenue model is per-wallet-scored API calls for B2B clients; future revenue includes token upside and an opportunity marketplace offering tasks and quests to onboard high-quality users.
After MVP launch on Monday, Fair Scale reached 2,000 verified users in less than two days; first cohort includes 10 integration partners including Streamflow, All Domains, SNS, and the Star team.
Fair token is at 1.25M valuation with 750K minimum raise; $STAR holders own 70% of the protocol through futarchy model, with token linking to infrastructure and integration decisions.

Monthly burn rate of 75K primarily funds data pipeline expansion; team forecasts 3M annual recurring revenue by end of 2026 from approximately 50 enterprise contracts based on current growth and conservative modeling.
Star will retroactively bonus airdrop $FAIR tokens to investors based on their fair score at investment, and plans to dynamically display scores on profiles for fund selection.

i1kV-7EHGjY.tldr: Pixel AI, built entirely through vibe-coding by a former Zynga Poker engineer, launches a fully AI-generated poker game on Pump Fun with a streaming mode for creators; the project plans to integrate play-to-earn rewards via Open Game Protocol and is positioning itself as a one-person AI-native gaming studio that could eventually compete with AAA titles.

topics.text: Pixel AI migrated from Believe to Pump Fun using migrate.fun, with the founder praising Pump Fund's communication and support.

The poker game is 100% vibe-coded using AI tools; the founder argues that vibe-coding quality depends on the developer's engineering background and attention to detail over time, not the speed of initial creation.
Streaming mode hides players' cards in separate tabs to prevent exposure during streams, designed specifically for streamer-friendly gameplay.
Players earn rewards by hitting specific poker hands (straight or higher) redeemable in Pixel AI tokens through the upcoming Open Game Protocol integration launching in two weeks.
Stable coin payments via X42 are coming soon, allowing players to top up their bankroll at the table without leaving their seat.
An LLM Arena feature will pit different AI models (Grock, Gemini, Claude) against each other in poker with results posted to X, with plans for prediction markets on daily leaderboards.

Open Game Protocol, founded by Justin (the original Zynga Poker founder), solves developer pain points by providing reward system infrastructure, distribution, and revenue sharing without requiring developers to launch their own tokens.
The founder uses AI agents to automatically analyze gameplay data and provide reports on player retention patterns (5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, etc.) to optimize the game.
Private tables with unique links are coming soon, allowing players to share tables with friends without joining public matchmaking.
The long-term vision is to build a Grand Theft Auto-scale game at 10-20 times lower cost and 10 times faster than traditional AAA studios by leveraging AI, targeting completion within the next year.

0_RFLMIu9gI.tldr: Dupe is an AI-powered e-commerce agent platform that just hit $200M GMV and is expanding from furniture into fashion, beauty, and electronics. Founder Bobby Gooall discusses how Google's UCP protocol standardizes web data for AI agents, enabling Dupe to provide decision intelligence upstream of purchase—and why he's turned down major acquisition offers to stay independent and move fast.

topics.text: Google's UCP protocol standardizes web data for AI agents instead of humans, removing bot detection barriers and messy code that plague current e-commerce
Dupe's agents download YouTube videos, read Reddit threads, and conduct hundreds of hours of research to recommend products based on user needs
Honey and similar coupon apps steal last-click attribution even when they find no coupons, robbing e-commerce companies of 20-40% of revenue
UCP enables direct price negotiations with brands based on customer loyalty and purchase history, bypassing coupon systems and attribution theft
Dupe turned down at least two major acquisition offers because large companies cannot move as fast as independent founders iterating quarterly
Dupe is 10 times bigger than the next competitor and 45-50 times bigger than a competitor that raised a $50M seed from ex-Google founders

aYOGTxuY9tw.tldr: JailedDotFun, a new Ponzi-style crypto game from the creator of Addicted, launches Phase 1 next week with a prison soap-dropping mechanic.
